Once the Nevada sun has finished beating down on the circular roof of T-Mobile Arena on Saturday, a cloud will hover above the south end of the Sin City strip.

When Ryan Garcia defends the WBC welterweight title against Conor Benn, the main-event contest pits one of America's most-divisive boxers against one of Britain's. These are two fighters who so often entertain in the ring, but whose places in a bout of this magnitude are questionable to say the least.

open image in gallery Ryan Garcia (left) and Conor Benn (front right) at their launch press conference ( Getty )

Garcia is defending the belt he won in May – fairly, even impressively – but his title shot against Mario Barrios came within nine months of his previous outing: a loss to Rolly Romero with the WBA strap on the line, when “King Ryan” was dropped and outpointed in New York City's Times Square.

Go back one fight further, and Garcia did drop Devin Haney three times en route to a stunning decision win, but this victory was reversed upon the revelation that the 28-year-old had failed a drug test.

Garcia has always proclaimed his innocence, and one might argue that he did his time by serving a one-year ban. But how he went from failing a drug test to fighting for a world title on his comeback, to losing but fighting for another world title in his next bout, is frankly near-impossible to justify.

Looking back at the American’s last five results, they read: win, loss, no-contest, win, loss.

And there are similar questions around the legitimacy of Benn’s place as challenger this weekend.

He will enter Las Vegas with the momentum of back-to-back points wins over former world champions – Regis Prograis and Chris Eubank Jr – but these don’t quite convey the reality of the Briton’s position.

The win against Prograis (past his best, to the point that he retired afterwards) took place at a 150lb catchweight, with Benn hurting the American once but failing to capitalise. The victory over Eubank Jr, whom Benn admittedly dropped twice late on, took place up at middleweight, and it followed a loss to Eubank Jr seven months prior – also at middleweight, where some feel Benn’s rival was drained.

open image in gallery Benn dropped Chris Eubank Jr twice in the final moments of their November rematch ( Getty )

Enjoy 185+ fights a year on DAZN, the Global Home of Boxing Never miss a fight from top promoters. Watch on your devices anywhere, anytime. Buy Now . If you sign up to this service we will earn commission. This revenue helps to fund journalism across The Independent.

Enjoy 185+ fights a year on DAZN, the Global Home of Boxing Never miss a fight from top promoters. Watch on your devices anywhere, anytime. Buy Now . If you sign up to this service we will earn commission. This revenue helps to fund journalism across The Independent.

So, when Benn faces Garcia for the WBC’s prestigious welterweight strap, the 29-year-old will be fighting at 147lb for the first time in two-and-a-half years.

And tracing our way back to Benn’s fight in February 2024 is pertinent. That outing was his second in the US in five months, after he was provisionally suspended from boxing in the UK, having failed two drug tests in summer 2022.

Before those drug tests, Benn was largely living up to his nickname of the “Destroyer”, and he had just dismantled Chris Algieri and Chris van Heerden in legitimate challenges. Since those drug tests, however, he is yet to score a stoppage – including since he was cleared to box in the UK again, in late 2024 – with his style arguably evolving from a seek-and-destroy approach to a volume-heavy one. It is important to note that Benn maintained his innocence throughout the entire drug-test saga.

In any case, against Garcia, he will be keen on a long-awaited trademark performance, especially after his rumoured $15m deal with Zuffa Boxing.

open image in gallery Garcia before his WBC title win against Mario Barrios in February ( Getty )

When Benn spoke to The Independent ahead of Saturday’s fight, he said of Garcia: “We’re just not the same. My pillars are very different to his. Mine’s family, working hard, choosing the hard way – because the hard way pays off later on – whereas he’s one of these Gen Z kids, ‘kid-men’ who want an easy life. I’m just not wired that way. Suffer now and live the rest of your life as a champion is my sort of mindset.”

Benn was not speaking about Garcia’s drug-test controversy, but some boxing fans might take issue with the Briton’s words anyway; for all of Benn and Garcia’s protestations, both have been accused of not pursuing the tougher path.

It will be interesting to see who garners the greater support throughout fight week. This year, the term “hate watch” has entered the vernacular of many sports fans: the idea of watching a match with an intense desire for one particular competitor to lose. Arsenal’s loss to PSG in the Champions League was a prime example for many English football fans.

Benn and Garcia both have their detractors. But in Las Vegas, as Mexican Independence Day looms, the Mexican-American boxer is likely to be seen as the hero in T-Mobile Arena – regardless of Garcia’s alleged missteps in recent years.

Kimberly Levaco is not like other girls. This much is obvious from the first time we glimpse the hero of Kimberly Akimbo, lacing up her skates at a small-town New Jersey ice rink. She is on the cusp of her 16th birthday, but you wouldn’t know this by looking: she is played by 66-year-old stage veteran Maria Friedman. Kimberly, we quickly learn, is a teenager with a rare, one-in-fifty-million disease, a genetic disorder similar to the real-world condition progeria, in which her body ages four to five times quicker than it ought to.

As you might imagine, there is an inherent melancholy to David Lindsay-Abaire and Jeanine Tesori’s stage musical, making its UK debut at the Hampstead Theatre after an acclaimed, Tony-winning run stateside. From the very first scene, Kimberly is a sort of doomed figure, a woman coming to the end of her life at the point when it’s meant to be starting. (The life expectancy for people with her condition is 16 years old.) She is surrounded by teenagers wrapped up in the frivolous concerns of adolescence, and adults – including Buddy (Peter Hannah), her deadbeat, booze-dipped dad, and Patty (Niamh Perry), her scatty, mercurial and heavily pregnant mother – who barely seem to have grown up themselves. Kimberly Akimbo mostly opts to keep things light, treating its premise with a kind of wry humour; if there’s such a thing as breezy morbidity, this show has it.

The parameters of Kimberly’s world are contained within one shapeshifting set, designed by Soutra Gilmour, which rotates 360 degrees to become an ice rink, a high school (evoked by a facade of hallway lockers), a library, and Levaco’s three-story house. A giant animated backdrop, mostly used to resemble a big clock, is the only thing remotely cheap-looking or superfluous; mostly, this is a robustly clever staging, and the scale feels just right in its depiction of a New Jersey town that people are itching to leave.

The cast are strong without exception – among them Gilli Jones as Kimberly’s tuba-playing, anagram-obsessed love interest, and Alice Fearn, a tornado-like force, as Kimberly’s chaotic criminal aunt, who rumbles into town partway through the first act with a harebrained get-rich-quick scheme. It’s Friedman, though, who’s most impressive, ably mimicking the physicality of a teenage girl with a sincerity that evades caricature; it’s the sort of role that is almost never available for older actors, and she makes it look natural. At 66, her voice remains a thing of power and clarity.

Shows like this often live and die by the music, and there is much to enjoy about Tesori’s score and Lindsay-Abaire’s lyrics, which are never really intricate (beyond the odd internal rhyme) or profound, but consistently lively and well-judged. The music is a cut above most modern musicals, tempering the sort of bright, generically popish sound of its bigger numbers with more classical musical-theatre forms elsewhere.

open image in gallery The company of 'Kimberly Akimbo' ( Marc Brenner )

The question, with imports like Kimberly Akimbo, is whether they will be able to charm British audiences in the same way they did Americans: will a joke about the ignominy of being a Bruce Springsteen hater in New Jersey carry over to North London? Ultimately, the show keeps things broad. This is not a musical about New Jersey at all, or about an ultra-rare genetic malfunction that only a handful of people will ever have to deal with. It is a show about ageing, and about youth – those most thoroughly universal of experiences. And in this, it is a clear success.

‘Kimberly Akimbo’ is at the Hampstead Theatre until 7 November

News.title: Accounting guru blew $13M of investors’ cash on a dream Caribbean wedding and Super Bowl tickets, feds say
News.content:

Federal authorities have arrested a 42-year-old California woman accused of orchestrating a $13.3 million investor fraud scheme involving her startup company, using the illicit proceeds to fund personal luxuries that included a Tesla, an Inglewood home, Super Bowl tickets and a destination wedding.

Shiloh Luckey, a resident of Inglewood, was apprehended on Sunday in Fort Lauderdale, Florida, just prior to embarking on a cruise vacation. After her release on bond in the Sunshine State, she is scheduled to appear in a Los Angeles federal court in the coming weeks.

According to the U.S. Attorney’s Office, Luckey faces an indictment charging her with nine counts of securities fraud, three counts of wire fraud, one count of bank fraud, and two counts of money laundering.

open image in gallery Shiloh Luckey, Founder & CEO, ComplYant, on Centre Stage during day two of Collision 2022 at Enercare Centre in Toronto ( Sportsfile/Getty )

Federal prosecutors allege that between September 2020 and September 2023, Luckey deceived investors into funding her Los Angeles-based business, ComplYant App Inc. She reportedly presented prospective backers with updates, pitch decks, and promotional materials that falsely inflated the firm's subscription numbers, customer base, cash reserves, and recurring revenue.

Additionally, Luckey allegedly persuaded victims to invest by falsely asserting she was a licensed certified public accountant with extensive experience in accounting, tax management, and compliance. Authorities noted that she has never held a CPA license.

Relying on these misrepresentations, victims poured millions of dollars into what they believed was a promising startup based on Luckey's claims, according to court documents.

In reality, prosecutors contend that Luckey diverted a portion of the raised funds toward personal expenditures, including her residence in Inglewood, a Tesla car, and a wedding on the Caribbean island of Anguilla.

open image in gallery Prosecutors contend Luckey then used a portion of the funds to pay for personal expenses, including the purchase of a home in Inglewood, a Tesla car, and expenses for a wedding on the Caribbean island of Anguilla, shown here ( Getty Images )

By September 2023, ComplYant suffered severe liquidity problems and shut down entirely, causing investors to lose their entire financial contributions. Prosecutors estimate that Luckey fraudulently obtained at least $13.3 million in total.

The indictment also details an alleged check-kiting operation in September and October 2022. Prosecutors say Luckey wrote a bad $1.5 million check from a ComplYant bank account lacking funds, deposited it into a company account at a separate bank, and wired the money to buy her home before the first institution identified the check as worthless.

She then cleared the negative balance created by the check-kiting scheme by depositing fresh proceeds from incoming securities-fraud investors, officials said.

If convicted on all counts, Luckey faces a maximum sentence of up to 30 years in federal prison for bank fraud, up to 20 years for each count of wire and securities fraud, and up to 10 years for each count of money laundering.

News.title: West Nile virus hits Europe as temperatures climb
News.content:
“The future looks rosy for West Nile virus and other mosquito-borne viruses that follow it to the New World,” wrote the science writer Carl Zimmer in his 2011 book ‘Planet of Viruses’.

“That’s because the future is going to be warm and wet.”

More than a decade on, and after a record-setting hot summer, Mr Zimmer’s prediction has come to pass: the mosquito-borne disease, once confined mostly to the warmest parts of Africa, has become firmly entrenched in Europe, experts have warned.

At least 1,086 locally acquired cases of West Nile virus have been recorded across the continent over the last three months, as mosquitoes continue their slow march northwards.

The insects – which are cold-blooded – need warm weather to accelerate their life cycles and survive long enough to spread disease.

Across July and August, countries including Italy, Spain and France recorded West Nile cases in previously unaffected regions and cities, while others, including the Netherlands, recorded their first deaths from the virus this summer.

“I don’t think there are any more ‘tropical viruses’... the geographic barrier of these viruses no longer exists because of climate change,” said Dr Krishanthi Subramaniam, a microbiology lecturer at the University of Liverpool.

News.title: Britain pioneers new dried blood products for the modern battlefield
News.content:
A powdered blood product that can be mixed with water and used in minutes could help solve the challenges of treating severely wounded soldiers on hard-to-reach battlefields.

Britain is rethinking how to get blood to soldiers on the frontline, in the latest sign that the war in Ukraine has forced Western militaries to reconsider assumptions about modern combat medicine that had held since Iraq and Afghanistan.

The product, known as “spray-dried plasma”, is made by turning liquid plasma – the clotting-rich component of blood – into a stable powder that can be stored at room temperature for years before being rehydrated with water when needed.

“Plasma is vital for saving soldiers in war zones,” said Dr Ian Nesbitt, a former military anaesthetist and Faculty Lead for Anaesthesia at the David Nott Foundation, which trains doctors working in conflict zones.

“It helps blood clot when someone is injured. But in war zones, getting plasma to soldiers is incredibly complicated. It’s actually the logistics of it that are a real problem in maintaining a reliable supply of fresh frozen plasma for acutely injured patients.”

The NHS and the UK Ministry of Defence signed a strategic partnership this summer to jointly develop new blood products for frontline soldiers, focusing on dried plasma.

The agreement formalises work under way with a biotechnology company called Velico Medical. If successful, it will be used in future battlefields like the one in Ukraine.

“The war in Ukraine has woken up all countries, not just the UK,” Professor Renata Gomes, Chief Scientific Officer at NHS Blood and Transplant (NHSBT), told The Telegraph.

News.title: Mosquitoes are evolving to evade bed nets – but there may be a solution
News.content:
In Papua’s low-lying mangrove swamps and dense tropical rainforests, mosquitoes have always got to work early.

Here, the disease-ridden insects begin feeding in the early evening as people socialise and children play. It’s a characteristic that’s hampered malaria control efforts, because it has rendered bed nets less effective. People are bitten before they climb under the netting to sleep.

It’s also part of the reason that Indonesian Papua remains one of Asia’s most persistent malaria hotspots. Last year, cases across the country jumped by 30 per cent, to 706,000 new infections. The vast majority, roughly 90 per cent, were reported in Papua’s six provinces.

The same pattern is now emerging in parts of sub-Saharan Africa, where mosquitoes used to bite mostly at night and where the rollout of insecticide-treated bed nets is estimated to have averted 450 million malaria cases between 2000 and 2015, according to modelling in Nature journal.

A number of studies suggest mosquitoes in Africa are evolving in response to the mass rollout of bed nets, biting earlier in the evening, or later in the morning. In some cases, species which already did this have become more dominant, while others are adapting their habits.

“We’re battling evolution. And right now, we’re losing,” said Prof Neil Lobo, a research professor in the Eck Institute for Global Health at the University of Notre Dame.

“Mosquitoes are adapting. They’re biting outdoors, they’re biting earlier in the evening when people aren’t under their nets, and they’re becoming resistant to the insecticides we use. So we’re reaching the limits of what bed nets alone can do,” he told The Telegraph.

But there may be a solution.

News.title: Palmer and Rogers complete 12-minute rescue mission to save Chelsea
News.content:
Xabi Alonso needed the cavalry – and referee Jarred Gillett – to stop Chelsea making a quick exit from the Carabao Cup and, boy, did they come up trumps for him.

Chelsea had looked to be heading out of the competition shortly after half-time, but, in Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers, Alonso has a cheat code that is capable of masking even the worst defending.

Alonso’s side have shared 26 goals in the five games they have played this season. It has certainly been an entertaining start by Chelsea’s latest manager.

Palmer, Rogers and Pedro Neto stepped off the substitutes’ bench to complete a stunning rescue mission against Leeds United. Palmer scored twice, Neto once and Rogers helped himself to at least a hat-trick of assists. He claimed it was four, but the record books may say three.

When it was announced Palmer had been awarded the player of the match, Rogers responded by saying: “Mate, I got four assists. I can’t believe that! That’s mental. He scored a pen!”

News.title: Martin Odegaard bails out comically wasteful Arsenal
News.content:
In five matches this season, Odegaard has already scored four goals. That is three more than he managed in the whole of last season. The Arsenal captain is fit again and he is flowing. As ever, when Odegaard flows, Arsenal flow.

“That’s what we need, the players with that mindset to decide the game and play with that personality,” said Mikel Arteta. “He has got that edge. He’s getting into those positions much more in recent games.”

In the end it was a thoroughly deserved victory for the Premier League side, who were superior to Napoli in every department. Were it not for their comically bad finishing, they would have guaranteed the result long before Odegaard’s 75th-minute strike.

Their expected goals figure suggested they should have scored more than four goals, compared to Napoli’s 0.22. In total, they registered 26 shots – the most of any Arsenal team on record in a single Champions League match, and the most on record a Napoli team has ever faced.

“With the amount of chances we generated, the scoreline has to reflect a very different result,” said Arteta. “The number of players that got into this situation, the amount of situations that we generated in various ways was something that pleased me a lot.”

News.title: Mac Allister not so sad now after Liverpool comeback winner
News.content:
Do your talking on the pitch, as the old adage goes, and Alexis Mac Allister emphatically did just that as Liverpool came from behind to thrillingly win their first Champions League tie under new head coach Andoni Iraola in what was his debut at this level.

On the eve of this encounter, against a strong Atlético Madrid, one of the clubs who have recently tried to sign him, Mac Allister had spoken of his sadness. Sadness that, unlike fellow midfielders Dominik Szoboszlai – Liverpool’s other scorer here – and Ryan Gravenberch, he had not been offered and signed a new contract.

So, earn it. And many more goals – and overall performances like this – there is no doubt the Argentinian will have a deal placed in front of him. He scored with an arresting second-half shot, which proved to be the winner, and the smile across his face said it all. Not so sad now as he was later substituted to a standing ovation with Gravenberch taking his place.

The goal came early in the second half, with Iraola attributing that to adjusting his tactics after being flummoxed by Atlético’s back five and packed midfield in a first half when Liverpool were second best.

Mac Allister was heavily involved through the build-up, eventually picking out Rio Ngumoha on the left whose shot was blocked and pinballed around. It dropped to Mac Allister, 20 yards out, and he hit the kind of unerring drive that gives the goalkeeper no chance. And so it proved. Boom. And Anfield was bouncing.

News.title: Gay does enough to earn another chance as England dominate again
News.content:
There are two places up for grabs in England’s top three and three players vying: Gay, Jordan Cox and Jacob Bethell, who spent the day on the players’ balcony dropping a reminder of his looming return. A hundred for Durham by Ben McKinney, the one challenger outside of the squad, tweaked the ante up further.

One of Cox or Gay will make way for Bethell when England begin their next series in Johannesburg on December 17, which will be the first Test of the Stephen Fleming era and the first big call he has to make. Cox was on the up after scores of 75 at Headingley and 55 in the first innings at Lord’s, looking the part at No 3. Gay’s luck had run out with a grubber in the second Test and he wasted a couple of 30s in other innings. Cox has opened in first-class cricket and Bethell could also take on the role of Ben Duckett’s partner. The squeeze was on.

But Cox perhaps got a little ahead of himself and played what could be a costly, impetuous shot at Mohammad Abbas to fall for six and hand Gay a chance. Neither Cox nor Gay have been tested on the back foot by genuine pace which will happen at the Wanderers in December but their performances have to be judged against the backdrop of a seam bowlers’ summer. Gay is averaging 27.1 from 10 innings, a number probably worth another 10 runs given the conditions.

His dismissal 20 minutes before the close, playing on driving away from his body, was the one time his footwork was non-existent and Razaullah deserved the breakthrough for coming back and hitting 90mph after tea following so little first-class cricket and a rushed call-up amidst the bloodletting.

News.title: I got a first look at Apple’s new £2k iPhone – it’s not just the price that makes it stand out
News.content:
Apple has entered the foldable phone race with the iPhone Duo, following years of speculation about whether the company would ever bend its famously rigid design philosophy.

Barely a month after Samsung dropped its latest Galaxy Z Fold 8, this is the moment Apple stakes its claim in a category it has avoided for the last decade. I was at the launch event at Apple’s HQ in Cupertino, California for a first look.

Similar in size to a British passport, the new smartphone unfolds like a miniature book to reveal a large 7.6-inch inner screen. When closed, it’s shorter and wider than a traditional iPhone, and when opened, it resembles a small iPad.

What makes the iPhone Duo worth your attention isn’t just that it’s the first hinged phone with an Apple logo, but that it addresses some of the biggest frustrations currently plaguing folding mobiles.

You can barely see the crease on the inner display, and it doesn’t look like a cheap plastic sheet. It’s intuitive to use, and fully waterproof, which is rare among rivals. Whether all that justifies a £2,000 price tag, however, is another question entirely.

Sports.title: ‘They’re terrible’ – Former Man City ace Rodri forced into grovelling apology after being caught on camera blasting club
Sports.content:
RODRI’s comments have caused a stir after he was caught slamming Barcelona’s LaLiga opponents from the bench.

Last Sunday, the £65.4million midfielder was subbed off in the 62nd minute with Barca 3-0 up against Valencia.



The former Manchester City man, 30, was spotted discussing the Los Che set-up with Pau Cubarsi without even covering his mouth.

According to Mundo Deportivo, Rodri said: “I apologised to my friend and colleague Jose Gaya (Spain defender and Valencia captain) and to the entire squad as well.



“I also want to make it clear that it was simply an expression of surprise – anyone watching the video can see that.

“At no point did I intend to mock anyone or take a difficult moment for a team out of context.



“Quite the opposite – we all want Valencia to return to where it belongs in the league, it is one of the best clubs in the competition.

“I simply wanted to say that.

“I would also add that it was a private conversation; I think we should all learn a bit more from this, as things really do get taken out of context sometimes.

“But at no point did I mean any disrespect. My apologies to Valencia.”



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

The World Cup winner apologised after Barca’s 5-1 Champions League victory over Feyenoord.

And while the footage has no audio, broadcaster Movistar claimed they lip-read and Rodri took no time to admit his mishap.

Many fans have not accepted his apology after his first start since returning to Spain.

During the box office show down, Rodri was seen saying: “They’re really weak – these guys are really weak… Really weak. They’re really bad, man. They’re terrible.



“How did they finish last season? They didn’t even make it past midfield in the second half…”

Valencia’s defeat left them at the bottom of the table with zero wins from their first four games.

Sports.title: Awkward moment Jose Mourinho is forced to correct reporter on live TV after monumental Champions League error
Sports.content:
JOSE MOURINHO had to awkwardly correct a TV reporter mid-interview after his first Champions League win back at Real Madrid.

The Portuguese boss oversaw Real’s 2-1 win over Inter, courtesy of goals from Kylian Mbappe and Federico Valverde.



After the game, a journalist interviewing the Special One for CBS said it was nice to see him back at the Bernabeu in the Champions League.

However, Mourinho replied by reminding them he had played there with Benfica last season.



With a smirk on his face as he finished the sentence, the 63-year-old said: “I played last season here with Benfica.”

Mourinho’s Benfica team suffered a narrow 2-1 defeat to Real in Spain, with Aurelien Tchouameni and Vinicius Junior scoring the goals in a comeback victory for the hosts in a narrow two-legged play-off clash.



The reporter clarified they meant him being in the Real dugout, to which Mourinho replied: “Yeah, but Champions League is Champions League, no?

“I enjoyed last season with Benfica, but with Real you have a different – I don’t want to say motivation or responsibility because I had it fully in Benfica – weight of history of the club.”

He continued: “These eight matches, it’s not like the second or the third matches are crucial, they’re not.

“But if you can start like we did with three points against one of the top teams, then it’s a good start.”



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Real suffered their first loss under Mourinho at the weekend as the manager was haunted by one of his former Tottenham players, Troy Parrott, who climbed off the bench to score the winner for Real Betis.

They face Rayo Vallecano next weekend, where they will be hoping not to lose any more early ground to Barcelona in the title race.

Mourinho returned to Real for a second spell after previously managing the club between 2010 and 2013.

He won La Liga, the Copa del Rey and the Spanish Super Cup in his first spell, and will be aiming to repeat the trick or even win more this time around.

Sports.title: World’s biggest stadium with 115,000 capacity and cost £9BILLION to build ‘leaked’ as host of 2030 World Cup final
Sports.content:
MOROCCO have seemingly leaked where they expect the 2030 World Cup final to be played, despite FIFA yet to make an official announcement.

Royal Moroccan Football Federation president Fouzi Lekjaa has confidently claimed the Grand Stade Hassan II in Benslimane will host the biggest game in world football.



The stunning new stadium is being built in Casablanca and is set to boast a staggering capacity of almost 115,000.

Speaking at an event held by the Authenticity and Modernity Party in Bouznika, Lekjaa said: “What you should know is that the province of Benslimane will have the honour of hosting the 2030 World Cup final.



“And God willing, may there be a final bringing together Morocco and France so that we can take our revenge.”

His comments came despite FIFA having yet to officially decide which stadium will stage the final.

Morocco are co-hosting the 2030 World Cup alongside Spain and Portugal.

Argentina, Paraguay and Uruguay also hosting a game each at the start of the tournament to mark the 100-year anniversary since the first World Cup in Uruguay.

And the race for the final is shaping up to be a battle between some of the most spectacular stadiums in world football.

The Hassan II stadium is at the centre of Morocco’s bid, with its design inspired by traditional Moroccan tents used during celebrations.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Construction is expected to be completed in 2027, giving the venue three years to be tested and prepared before the World Cup kicks off.

But Spain has two heavyweight contenders of its own in Real Madrid‘s Bernabeu and Barcelona‘s Camp Nou.

The Bernabeu underwent a huge redevelopment between 2019 and 2024, transforming the iconic ground into a futuristic multi-purpose venue.



It now boasts a retractable roof, while its natural grass pitch can be split into sections and stored underground in a climate-controlled facility.

The stadium has also been wrapped in a futuristic steel facade and fitted with a giant 360-degree video screen around the upper tier.

Barcelona’s Camp Nou is also undergoing a mammoth redevelopment costing around £1.3billion, with the club aiming to eventually increase its capacity to around 105,000.

The iconic Camp Nou could prove particularly attractive to Spain given Barcelona’s influence on the national team.

Eight Barcelona players were included in Spain’s squad for their World Cup triumph this summer, with eight of the players also products of the club’s famous La Masia academy.

Sports.title: I won 13 Premier League titles for Man Utd… Pep Guardiola once told me the shock star he’d ‘take tomorrow’
Sports.content:
RYAN GIGGS has revealed Pep Guardiola once hailed Marcus Rashford as

Manchester United’s best player.

And the ex-Manchester City boss said he would sign the Red Devils

forward “tomorrow”.



Giggs recalled a chat he had with Guardiola at a dinner hosted by Sir

Alex Ferguson almost a decade ago.

Giggs, 52, said: “I had dinner with Sir Alex and Pep. He has a charity

auction where someone bids to have dinner with people. We’ve done it

with (Jurgen) Klopp, Pep and Eric (Cantona).



“There were a few of Sir Alex’s friends so there’s about eight of us.

Sir Alex sat me next to Pep. I’m gonna say this was about eight or

nine years ago.

“I’ve gone to Pep, ‘Who do you like at United?’ He said, ‘Well, who

do you think?’

“I went: “De Gea?” He said “No”. “Luke Shaw“, he replied: “No”.

“He said, ‘The best player at United is Rashford. I would take him tomorrow’.

“I went, ‘Oh right, okay’. It made me think, ‘What is Pep seeing in him?’

And that was as a centre-forward.”

Rashford is back at United after 18 months away on loan at

Aston Villa and Barcelona.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

The forward, preparing for tonight’s Champions League tie with Sabah

and Sunday’s Manchester derby against City, is trying to win back the

Old Trafford fans.

Rashford was bombed out by ex-boss Ruben Amorim but the England star

has started the last two matches under Michael Carrick.

Giggs, a 13-time Prem winner and legendary left-winger during United’s

glory days under Ferguson throughout the 1990s and 2000s, told the Rio

Ferdinand Presents podcast: “I feel a little bit sorry for him because

I grew up as a winger.

“You had me, (Andrei) Kanchelskis, (David) Beckham, Nani. We were all used to the box-to-box. It’s a different dynamic. He’s not a natural wideman.

“Marcus has moved from centre-forward where it is sharp little

movements to up and down, up and down.



“I played in a 4-4-2 while they are wide forwards now but the

fundamentals don’t change. You still have to track your full-back or

be on the back post if the ball is crossed from the right.

“Marcus has maybe a couple of times not stayed with runners or jogged

back instead of sprinting. What gets the crowd going at Old Trafford?

“If it’s 0-0 after 20 minutes, a goal, a shot or a tackle. That’s what

he has to do. It’s not what he thinks he is on the team to do. People

think goals and assists.



“Fans will forgive you for dribbling and getting tackled or hitting a

shot over. Not all the time.

“But they won’t forgive you for not tracking back. They just won’t.

“I love Marcus and I want him to do well. I wasn’t sure if it was

right for him to come back because of the hype around him. It’s a lot

of pressure for him.

“But he’s got the talent. If he is running at players and tracking

back…if he does that for a season then he will be a superstar.”

Sports.title: How Cesc Fabregas guided Como to Champions League by copying tactics of all his ex-managers, except former Chelsea boss
Sports.content:
CESC FABREGAS is remembered as one of the best midfielders in the history of football, and already poses as one of the brightest young managers in the world.

Fabregas, 39, needed less than two seasons since taking over his first ever coaching job to make history as he led Italian minnows Como to the Champions League for the first time in the club’s 119-year history.



But this comes as no surprise as the Arsenal and Chelsea legend learned from the best ever bosses in the history of the game during a glittering 20-year playing career.

That includes the likes of Pep Guardiola, Jose Mourinho, Arsene Wenger, Antonio Conte, Vicente del Bosque and Luis Aragones.



It all started back in 2003 when Fabregas – then a 16-year-old wonderkid – moved to north London from Catalonia after impressing Wenger, 76, who was famous for working with promising young prospects.

After eight successful years with the Gunners – which included 57 goals and 97 assists in 303 appearances as well as FA Cup and Community Shield honours – the former Spain international returned to Barcelona, where he started in La Masia’s famous academy in 1997.



That is where he linked up with Guardiola, 55, where he took his game to the next level playing with the likes of Lionel Messi, Andres Iniesta and Xavi under the Catalan tactician.

Meanwhile, Fabregas had been taking notes on everything he was learning from these two managerial titans – who turned out to be his biggest influences when he made the big leap to the dugout in 2024 for a club he co-owns as minority shareholder.

Both Wenger and Guardiola taught him the importance of good communication with players, inspiring trust and taking youngsters under his wing.

But it was because of Arsenal‘s legendary gaffer that he adopted a philosophy based on forward-thinking football.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Fabregas told DAZN: “Arsene Wenger is like a second father to me. Obviously, he worked a lot on transitions, attacking the space, something that is even more important in modern football. I learned a lot from him and want my team to do that.”

And Fabregas combines the tactics he learned from Wenger with control and – especially – patience.

He told ESPN: “What I learned from him [Wenger] the most is the patience you must have with the players. I know that nowadays patience doesn’t exist because coaches are fragile and we are too scared that if you lose two games, you’re out.

“So you always try to compensate that by putting the most experienced players or the best players, or maybe not the ones who deserve it the most. I’m liking a lot working with the young players. And this requires patience as well, because there is ups and downs with a young player.

“You need to put a little bit more effort in the training sessions, more time globally. This is something that I learned, that when you want to develop something, you need patience.”



However, Wenger and Guardiola weren’t completely identical and that worked wonders for Fabregas as the latter was the one that highlighted the importance of a manager being “himself” and sending a clear message to players and staff.

The ex-Manchester City boss maintained more of a distance with players and thus didn’t treat the legendary midfielder “as his son” like Wenger did.

However, Guardiola was the one that taught him the most in terms of tactics.

Fabregas said: “I think, tactically, Pep is the one that I learned the most from. He always studied the opponent. He always knew exactly what they could do and he could give you solutions.

“And this is what I try to bring to the table for the players. They always need help to identify what’s happening on the pitch. And I think Pep helped me a lot in this way to understand different things.”



Meanwhile, Fabregas also played for Spain under two other influential figures in the late great Aragones and Del Bosque, 75, with whom he won back-to-back Euros in 2008 and 2012 as well as the 2010 World Cup.

Aragones gave him freedom and allowed him to be versatile – a principal that he insists on when dealing with his players at Como – while Del Bosque made him feel comfortable by instilling calmness and peace within his game that helped him overcome mistakes he made on the pitch.

Mourinho, 63, then brought him to Chelsea in 2014 and taught him about bravery on the pitch as well as the importance of working on players’ confidence outside of it, which worked wonders as he won his first Premier League title in 2015.



Fabregas said: “What I like the most about him is how he handles the dressing room. How he plays with the head of the players, how he knows how to identify who is in the right mental predisposition to achieve whatever the team needs in that moment.

“He’s very fast at understanding the player, what the team needs at each moment, and who can give them what he needs in order to win games.

“He’s not scared to make changes. I remember sometimes he would make three changes at half-time because he knew exactly in his head how he wanted to achieve different things in the second half.

“And in this case, I think Jose was very, very brave. And he always used to tell me, go with your idea. Once you identify a problem, fix it immediately. Don’t let it pass.”

But it was Mourinho‘s replacement that Fabregas copied the least when he made the plunge in management.



Conte, 57, led the Spaniard to a second Prem and FA Cup honour but his tactics didn’t allow him enough freedom, like he had at Arsenal, Barcelona, Spain and Chelsea under his predecessor.

Fabregas told Coaches’ Voice: “Probably with Conte – tactically and physically – is the coach that I worked more with.

“Tactically, when I speak about this subject, I would say that he always wanted to tell you exactly what you have to do on the pitch and it is not something that I was very, very motivated by.



“Because [of] my intuition and my tactical capacity on the pitch – knowing where to find the space at the right time. Because for me, in football, you cannot tell a player to do the same thing every single time.

“When other teams started to study you and understand how you play it became much more difficult for us to adapt because this was all we knew how to do and that’s why my idea of football is to try and teach my players to be as best as they can in every situation that they can find on a football pitch.

“It’s not easy, it needs a lot of time and dedication and individual meetings and collective meetings but I believe this is the best way for a player to feel powerful on the pitch.”

Fabregas has picked up a combination out of all the esteemed managers he has worked with, but insists on letting his players – especially the likes of Nico Paz, Martin Baturina and Tasos Douvikas – perform freely.

But of course most of his tactical philosophy is based on Wenger and Guardiola that emphasises on structured build-up play, numerical superiority and midfield dominance.



Como, who are set for their first ever Champions League match tonight when they host RB Leipzig at Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia, primarily operate in a 4-3-3 formation focused on short passing sequences and compact midfield spacing.

Fabregas prioritises playing through the middle to facilitate quick ball transitions and loves to maintain a solid defensive shape when out of possession in a 4-1-4-1 formation.

Meanwhile, all his midfielders continuously rotate and take on different roles during the game.

But overall, Fabregas appears to be more of a student of Guardiola as he is innovative and tactically astute while playing with a classic Spanish football style that sees him retaining possession, setting up centrally and looking to break down the opponent’s lines.

And he now shares an important lesson he picked up outside the pitch as he instructed his players to invest their lucrative wages on improving their game and prolonging their career instead of needless luxury, like private jets and fast cars.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Fabregas told the BBC: “The best investment you can do, even if you are not earning crazy money – instead of taking private planes, instead of getting great cars – spend the money on chefs at home, in mental coaching preparation.

“If you are not happy with the level of the fitness coach, always get a little bit extra, sleep well. Spend money on these things that can get value for your future.”

Sports.title: Wrexham star Elliot Lee reveals surreal Ryan Reynolds phonecall & warns West Ham face Championship shock
Sports.content:
ELLIOT LEE has warned his boyhood club West Ham that Hollywood-backed Wrexham are heading to London to deliver a brutal Championship reality check.

The free-agent midfielder knows both clubs inside out after coming through the Hammers’ youth ranks before driving Wrexham’s sensational rise from non-league to the brink of the Premier League.



And Lee insists Phil Parkinson’s team actually boast MORE Championship battle-hardness than West Ham’s multi-million-pound squad ahead of Friday night’s showdown.

He told SunSport: “If you look at Wrexham’s team, the amount of Championship appearances in that squad is probably more than West Ham’s.



“The Hammers are not a Championship club but the second tier is a completely different ball game and it’s tough.

“They could struggle because many of their players don’t know the league as other teams do.”



It is a far cry from the summer of 2022 when Lee dropped into the National League following a surreal phone call with Deadpool icon Ryan Reynolds.

Lee was a seasoned EFL midfielder who had just left Luton when Wrexham made their ambitious move.

He said: “My agent wasn’t sure whether to tell me because I’d never been in the National League. It wasn’t my intention to play there.

“I had a couple of Zoom calls over that summer with Phil Parkinson and then I had a phone call with Ryan just before I signed.”



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

What struck Lee immediately was the A-lister’s total honesty and lack of ego during their conversation.

Reynolds made no attempt to preach tactics to the experienced playmaker, focusing purely on his vision for the club and town.

Lee said: “It was just a normal chat with Ryan but the main thing was how genuine he was. He didn’t try to talk tactics with me.

“If a Hollywood actor had tried to call me up and throw tactics at me, I probably wouldn’t have bought into it. But he was the complete opposite.”



Lee witnessed first-hand how Reynolds and co-owner Rob McElhenney transformed the working-class city into an emotional juggernaut.

And the 31-year-old compares the fanatical passion at the Racecourse Ground to what his dad Rob Lee experienced during his time at Newcastle.

Lee said: “Wrexham is a fishbowl where they live, breathe, and work for football. We compare it to my dad’s time at Newcastle with the overwhelming support.

“The owners turned a city where there was maybe no hope into something so exciting. I’m an adopted Wrexham lad now.”



That emotional roller-coaster reached its absolute peak on the unforgettable night Wrexham sealed their historic escape from non-league football after 15 years against Boreham Wood.

Lee rates that night as the single greatest moment of his journey in North Wales.

He said: “I don’t think you can beat getting out of the National League. The emotion around the place and with the owners was just amazing.

“It was a night I’ll never forget because of the relief. It meant so much to the people of Wrexham to actually achieve it.”

Lee, who played in the Premier League and scored in Europe for West Ham, knows the Irons face a brutal adjustment period in the second tier.



With Friday’s game being the Hammers’ third in six days, Lee warns the relentless grind will test them to the limit.

He said: “It’s a real grind and the games come thick and fast. It’s very different to the Premier League.

“It might take some of the players a while to adjust, but you just have to hope their talent shines through.”



He also points to club captain Jarrod Bowen as the man who must carry the entire club back to the big time.

Lee said: “Jarrod staying as captain was huge. It’s up to him now and he’s got to have it all on his back to get them back up.”

After earning five career promotions, Lee is now keeping fit as a free agent while waiting for the right project to catch his eye.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Along with his three promotions with Wrexham, the midfielder also went up from League Two to the Championship with Luton.

He added: “I don’t plan to be out too long. I want to find another home and add a few more promotions to the CV.”

Sports.title: Ex-Man City star sentenced to two years but dodges prison after cocaine addiction saw him scam pals out of £30,000
Sports.content:
FORMER Manchester City star Eike Immel has dodged a prison sentence – after a court heard his cocaine addiction led him to scam pals out of £30,000.

The German keeper spent two years with City, making 50 senior appearances before retiring in 1997.



Immel, 65, won a Bundesliga title with Stuttgart and also played for Borussia Dortmund.

But prosecutors called for the ex-goalie to receive a 29-month jail term after allegedly failing to repay friends €34,000 in loans.



However a court in the German city of Marburg instead gave him a two-year suspended sentence on Wednesday.

Judge Dominik Balzer told Immel: “You will go straight to jail if you reoffend in the future.”

The 19-cap former West Germany international was also ordered to attend regular drug treatment and perform 200 hours of community service.

His lawyer Burkhard Benecken told the court: “If Mr Immel receives treatment for his cocaine addiction he won’t commit any more crimes – I’m certain of that.

“He is not somebody who cons people so he can drive a Ferrari. He needs rehabilitation above all.”

Immel said: “I can only restate how painful this has been for me. I won’t lie any more, and hope for a second chance.



“I had no health insurance, and bailiffs came to my door. Nobody from the world of football wanted anything to do with me, and I never learned how to manage money.

“I want to change my life. I can work in goalkeeper training camps, and I’ve had offers to appear in reality TV shows.

“I have a new partner who looks after me. It is worth my while to be a respectable guy.”



Immel was declared bankrupt in 2008. He previously said he lived “the life of Riley” on his playing salaries from his German clubs and City.

But the ex-keeper admitted to blowing almost £10million after his divorce and a series of unwise investments.

Sports.title: Arsenal files: Fans urged to avoid Naples and cook up ‘cover story’ to avoid trouble as Emerson Nwaneri makes CL squad
Sports.content:
GUNNERS supporters were advised to have a “cover story” to avoid being caught up in fan trouble during their time in Naples.

The Arsenal Supporters’ Trust (AST) posted that recommendation on social media the night before Wednesday’s match.



There was also advice from the club, who urged fans not to wear club colours or congregate en masse in public areas.

Supporters were also told to avoid the city centre, particularly if they were easily identified as Arsenal fans.



Further advice instructed those travelling to Naples to avoid becoming isolated in areas away from the city’s port, where fan trouble has previously occurred.

The AST issued their own warning on Tuesday night for those who had gone out a day early.



They tweeted: “Sorry to have this say this in 2026 but advice for those in Naples tonight from the Police is to be careful after 9pm.

“Hotel bars seem to be the safest option.

“Have a cover story ready – even change the background on your phone if it’s Arsenal.

“We recommend that supporters do not visit the city centre. If you choose to do so, you should remain vigilant.”



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

LU BEAUTY

LUIS MUNOZ scored a “world class” goal to help Arsenal get off to a flying start in the Uefa Youth League.

The forward, 14, struck an effort into the top corner in injury time as the Gunners’ Under-19s kicked off their campaign with a 2-1 victory.

Andre Harriman-Annous had put Arsenal ahead before that, but the visitors were pegged back thanks to a Napoli equaliser.

Munoz – who aged just 14 years and 263 days old became the second-youngest scorer in Youth League history behind Max Dowman – came up trumps to win the game in the dying moments.



Arsenal Under-21 head coach David Horseman said: “The finish is just world class.

“On any stage, that’s a goal that’s fit to win any game. But we know that we’re not just giving people token games.

“We brought a squad that we thought could win the game, and he was part of it. He came on and had the decisive moment.

“But it is a world class goal, and I don’t use that word lightly; that’s for sure.”



CREDIT WHERE IT’S DUE

ARSENAL fans that missed their Champions League opener against Napoli will not lose their away credits.

Some Gunners supporters failed to make the game in Naples on Wednesday night due to travel chaos.

Air traffic control issues in the UK forced hundreds of flights to be cancelled on Tuesday afternoon and Wednesday morning.

It meant that some fans were unable to make it out to Italy for the first game in Europe this season.



But those who failed to do so will not be punished by the club for failing to attend the game.

Arsenal run an away-credit scheme, so as to reward those that travel to see them in action.

The more credits a fan has the easier it is for them to get a ticket for the biggest away games.

Supporters can have their credits hit, though, if they purchase a ticket but fail to turn up for the match.

Arsenal are well aware that in this case many fans were unable to attend due to circumstances out of their control and so they will not lose their credits.



NWAN FOR THE FURTURE

EMERSON NWANERI could potentially make his Champions League debut this season after he was named in Arsenal’s B List squad against Napoli.

Nwaneri, who is the younger brother of Gunners ace Ethan, was one of 30 youth players to be named in the secondary squad list for Arsenal’s European opener.

The B List submissions include any player Arsenal could field in their Champions League game who was born on, or after, January 1 2004, and has been eligible to play for the club for any uninterrupted period of two years since his 15th birthday, or for a total of three consecutive years.

Clubs submit their B List the night before every Champions League game.

It is the same list that allowed Max Dowman and Marli Salmon to make their Champions League debuts last season.



Nwaneri was included in the list ahead of the Napoli game, alongside a host of other names.

Other players named in Arsenal’s B List squad for the Napoli trip included Myles Lewis-Skelly, Max Dowman, Marli Salmon, Ceadach O’Neill, Andre Harriman-Annous and Ife Ibrahim.

While Nwaneri’s inclusion doesn’t guarantee a debut, it shows he could be used if Mikel Arteta opts to roll the dice.



Nwaneri was not included in the first-team matchday squad for Napoli; instead, he played for the Under-19s in the Uefa Youth League against Napoli U19s.

The 16-year-old played the full 90 minutes as Arsenal got off to a perfect start with a 2-1 victory over their Italian opponents.

SKELL RAISER

MYLES LEWIS-SKELLY kept the spirit of Arsenal fans high after their win over Napoli.

As is often the case for European away games, Gunners supporters had to stay in the ground for well over an hour after the full-time whistle.

During that time, a few Arsenal players that did not play in the game did some running drills.



One of those was MLS and, as he headed back down the tunnel, the travelling fans asked for him to give them a song.

The teenager bellowed at them “we know what we are”, which led to those supporters in the stadium singing about how Arsenal are champions.

It lifted the mood on what was a long night for Gunners fans, who were bused in and out of the stadium via a police escort.

SSARD TO SAY GOODBYE

LEANDRO TROSSARD was in the stands at the Emirates Stadium when Arsenal beat Chelsea on Sunday.

The Belgian, who left the Gunners to join Besiktas for £15.3m this summer, sat alongside injured defender Jurrien Timber to watch the match.



His appearance came just over 24 hours after he had played for Besiktas, registering a crucial assist as they beat Fenerbahce 2-1 last Saturday.

Trossard has started all four of Besiktas’ league games this season and looks set to play a huge part in their campaign.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The winger was a fan favourite at Arsenal and his absence is being felt by the supporters, as well as in Mikel Arteta’s squad.



His exit, alongside Gabriel Martinelli’s move to Al-Hilal, means Arsenal remain short on the left wing with Ebere Eze having to deputise Christos Tzolis in the role.

Sports.title: Martin Odegaard has changed his approach and is transforming Arsenal for the better
Sports.content:
Martin Odegaard has already smashed his stats from last season. And if the rejuvenated Arsenal captain stays in this form, he will quickly surpass the past two seasons put together.

Odegaard has been the driving force in Arsenal’s impressive start to the campaign as he has overcome trust issues and “playing safe” to get back to his very best form.

Norway midfielder Odegaard has already scored four goals this season - one in the Community Shield, two in the Premier League and one at Napoli in the Champions League.

But his all-round game has really caught the eye. He is playing with a new freedom which he showed at the World Cup with Norway and has carried on into this season.

‌



Last season, Odegaard managed just one goal for Arsenal in an injury-disrupted campaign. The previous season, he managed six in all competitions. But he was also dogged by injury after damaging his ankle on international duty in September 2024.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

At that point, Odegaard was seen as absolutely irreplaceable for Arsenal. His injury lay-off was seen as a massive blow. And, quite frankly, he struggled to come back to his best that season.

‌



Last season, there always looked to be an issue of trust in terms of Odegaard did not look entirely happy on the pitch. It looked as if he was not quite sure of his own body and whether he was about to break down again. He was troubled by a knee issue.

He played in the run-in but was not at his best and yet the World Cup seems to have given him back his confidence, his belief and his super power.

Sky Sports pundit Gary Neville identified it after Arsenal’s victory over Chelsea when Odegaard scored the winner. Neville said: “He did get into a cycle of being too safe. If anything, he got into a languid, playing it sideways, playing the easy pass.

“He’s capable of being sharper and making those late runs into the box more than he does. That’s what he did against Chelsea.

‌



View 3 Images Odegaard already has four goals for Arsenal this season

“Can he get the ten or 12 goals, the ten or 12 assists in a season which means he would be one of the best in the league? When Arsenal need goals, he needs to look for danger. He knows what to do, he’s got the capability.”

Odegaard is showing it again now. He is the player driving Arsenal forward. He ran the game in Naples. He played 107 passes which was more than anyone else and completed 92 which was second only to Declan Rice. Not perfect but it actually shows he is taking risks.

He covered an incredible 11.6km (joint top with Piero Hincapie) and did not stop working, running and looking for goal. It was no surprise he scored the winner and got the breakthrough.

‌



We should not forget that Arsenal were playing Napoli who were champions of Italy just 14 months ago. Arsenal had an XG of 4.05 and had just 0.22 XGA. That is an incredibly dominant performance.

And it was driven by Odegaard who is keeping the ball better, making things happen and is the focal point of Arsenal’s team again.

View 3 Images Arsenal have been purring at the start of the season - and Odegaard has played a huge part

Arsenal were branded Set Piece FC last season. They have yet to score a set-piece goal this season in five matches, the Community Shield, three Premier League games and now one Champions League game.

‌



That cannot be a coincidence. It is because Odegaard is back. He was one of the best midfielders playmakers in the Premier League. He can be among the best in Europe. Arsenal are so much better with a fit and firing Odegaard in the team.

They play a different way, they keep the ball better and are far better to watch. The gang of three - Odegaard, Kai Havertz and Bukayo Saka - have a brilliant connection which Arsenal have missed so much.

Arsenal’s win over Chelsea was the first time since December 2024 that Odegaard, Havertz and Saka had started a third straight league game together.

They are connected again, Odegaard is at the heart of it and Arsenal look such a better team for it.

‌

Sports.title: Jamie Carragher sticks to his guns on Alexis Mac Allister after Liverpool contract dig
Sports.content:
Jamie Carragher sticks to his guns on Alexis Mac Allister after Liverpool contract dig

Alexis Mac Allister bemoaned his Liverpool contract situation before scoring on Wednesday night - but Jamie Carragher was still not a fan of his approach

View 2 Images Jamie Carragher has consistently called out Liverpool players who speak about their futures publicly (Image: James Gill - Danehouse/Getty Images)

Jamie Carragher has called out Alexis Mac Allister for going public with his Liverpool contract frustrations and insists the Argentine is "not right" for using a press conference to air his views.

‌



The Reds midfielder, in the lead up to their clash with Atletico Madrid, was quizzed on his future and didn't shy away from admitting he was sad that the club had not yet approach him about extending his stay at Anfield.

‌



Mac Allister concedes that seeing fellow midfielders Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai land new deals has stung, especially given his role in the team's Premier League success of 2025.

‌



The World Cup winner enjoyed the perfect evening off the back of those comments, scoring for the Reds as they came from behind to down Atletico at Anfield, and whilst Carragher admits he's "walked the walk" he's still not a fan of how he went about his business.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



The pundit said on CBS Sports: "Mac Allister, who talked the talk yesterday and today he walked the walk. Still doesn't make what he did yesterday right in the press conference, but he'll be looked on more favourably after getting the winning goal."

Carragher has consistently bemoaned Liverpool stars who air their contract grievances through the media - expressing his disapproval when Virgil van Dijk and Mohamed Salah did so. The Egyptian would later depart whilst Van Dijk remains on Merseyside, but is into the final year of his contract.

Mac Allister admits he had offers to leave Liverpool in the summer but was determined to remain, even if he has been frustrated by how his contract saga has played out.

‌



View 2 Images Alexis Mac Allister scored the winner as Liverpool downed Atletico Madrid

He said: "Everybody can see I give my 100% for this football club every single day in training, games. Of course, I have very good games and bad games like everyone but always I give my best."

"I see Dominik and Ryan renewing their contracts and that makes me very happy because they deserve it, but at the same time it makes me a little bit sad as I didn't get mine.

Article continues below

"Of course there is still time. The fans don't need to worry because I will give my 100 per cent until the last day I am here. We will see what happens."

Sports.title: Bayern Munich chief comes clean on Bradley Barcola transfer with Luis Diaz dig at Liverpool
Sports.content:
Bayern Munich chief comes clean on Bradley Barcola transfer with Luis Diaz dig at Liverpool

Bradley Barcola arrived at Liverpool in a £123million deal, but Bayern Munich had also targeted him after signing Luis Diaz from the Reds last year

View 2 Images Bradley Barcola completed the blockbuster £123m move to Liverpool this summer (Image: Getty Images)

Bayern Munich director of sport Max Eberl has admitted that Liverpool blew them out of the race for Bradley Barcola this summer but insists it is Luis Diaz who truly draws fans to the stadium. Liverpool sold the Colombia international in a £65.5million deal last summer.

‌



The Reds were initially reluctant to let Diaz leave after an outstanding season in which he scored 17 goals in all competitions for the former Premier League champions. A year later, Barcola arrived at Anfield for £123million from Paris Saint‑Germain.

‌



Bayern, along with several other clubs, including Arsenal, had been linked with Barcola before the France international completed his move to Liverpool. However, Eberl explained that the price tag ultimately put the Bundesliga giants out of contention for a deal.

‌



"To be honest, I already knew Bradley from my time in Leipzig, I wanted to bring him to RB," Eberl said. "We sat down together and discussed it, that's how I developed a closer relationship with Bradley.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



"So, there was always interest. Of course, we also considered Bradley at Bayern. But when you hear those kinds of sums, it was too much for us. With Luis Diaz, we made a decision that was also expensive, but on a different scale than Bradley.

"Moreover, Diaz is a player that draws fans to the stadium. We're extremely happy with him."

Eberl's remarks about Diaz suggest a subtle dig at the Reds, hinting that Liverpool's pursuit of Barcola may not carry the same weight or commercial pull. The Frenchman was handed his first Liverpool start on Wednesday night as they hosted Atletico Madrid in the Champions League.

‌



Andoni Iraola's side produced a 2-1 comeback, with Dominik Szoboszlai cancelling out Marcos Llorente's opener before Alexis Mac Allister smashed in a late winner. But Barcola's night ended on a sour note after he picked up a fresh injury concern in the second half.

View 2 Images Bradley Barcola in action for Liverpool against Atletico Madrid

Just before the hour mark, the former PSG winger pulled up clutching his calf. After receiving treatment from Liverpool's medical staff and being consoled by team‑mates, he was replaced by Victor Munoz.

‌



Speaking after the game, Reds boss Iraola eased fears of an injury scare and revealed: "No it’s just cramps, especially with Bradley. We are kind of rushing him a little bit as he hasn’t played any minutes in pre-season.

"We want him there but at the end we decided for him to give us whatever he has and let’s see now how they recover for the next one, as we play again in three days."

Barcola began his Liverpool career with a cameo off the bench at Ipswich Town on Friday night, coming on just after the hour mark. Those were his first minutes since featuring in France's third‑place play‑off 6-4 defeat to England at the World Cup.

Sports.title: Liverpool given worrying Bradley Barcola verdict after Andoni Iraola injury update
Sports.content:
Liverpool given worrying Bradley Barcola verdict after Andoni Iraola injury update

Bradley Barcola started for Liverpool for the first time during their win over Atletico Madrid but the Frenchman had a wasteful night in front of goal

View 2 Images Bradley Barcola missed several golden chances in Liverpool's win on Wednesday night

Liverpool's new signing Bradley Barcola played in their win over Atletico Madrid on Wednesday night but the Frenchman's finishing ability has been called out with Tim Sherwood, who claimed "he missed a few sitters".

‌



Barcola completed his £123million move from PSG late in the summer transfer window with the two-time European champion seen as a difference maker for the Reds.

‌



He made his debut off the bench in Friday's win at Ipswich and made his first start in the victory over Atletico in the Champions League. Barcola didn't contribute to either goal, even though he had his chances.

‌



In the first half he saw a one-on-one effort saved by Jan Oblak and then, in the second 45, he was sent clear but with the goal at his mercy struck his effort wide in front of the Kop - which has seen him criticised for his wastefulness.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



Sherwood said on Sky Sports: “No, it wasn’t a good night. He had a lot of opportunities. He looked a threat, but he had a few opportunities bearing down Oblak and he just couldn’t find the finish. He’s not a fantastic finisher, I have to say that. A few sitters he missed tonight.

“The good thing about him is that he stretches defenders. He runs without the ball, so you don’t have to take possession of the ball and dribble. He goes, checks and makes good runs.”

Barcola was withdrawn prematurely, but Andoni Iraola rebuffed any injury fears and revealed the winger was simply struggling with cramp. He also brushed off his goalless night and instead praised the Frenchman for finding himself in the right positions.

‌



View 2 Images Bradley Barcola missed out on scoring his first Liverpool goal

He said: "With Bradley, it's about building his physical condition. We don't really know - or we didn't know until now, probably - how much he can play because he hasn't had any minutes in pre-season for PSG. He played 30 the other day [and] today we had some question marks, how many minutes he can give us and probably now we know.

"I'm very happy because also he has had two very clear chances against the 'keeper. He hasn't scored, but I want him there. There is where he has to make the difference, arriving to those spots, those positions, and I'm very happy because in - I don't know how many minutes he's played - two times against the 'keeper is a good sign with Bradley."

Sports.title: EFL manager makes outrageous 'volleyed his cat' statement in best interview of the season
Sports.content:
EFL manager makes outrageous 'volleyed his cat' statement in best interview of the season

An EFL manager was inventive when describing a key decision made during a Championship game

View 2 Images An EFL manager made his thoughts clear on a key decision made in a Championship match (Image: Sky Sports)

Charlton Athletic boss Nathan Jones had a bizarre way of describing the linesman’s reaction after seeing a goal disallowed for offside. The Addicks drew 0-0 with Queens Park Rangers at The Valley on Wednesday night.

‌



Both sides have made impressive starts to their Championship campaigns. Charlton headed into the game having picked up 10 points from their first five games, with QPR matching the home side’s tally.

‌



A win for either team could have potentially seen the victor end the night top of the table. However, Charlton were denied all three points after seeing Tyreece Campbell's first half effort disallowed for an offside call in the first half.

‌



While the game ended goalless, the match was not short of talking points. Charlton boss Jones did not hold back as he slammed the assistant referee’s decision in a box office interview and blamed officials for his side dropping points.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

“They were giving offsides willy-nilly because we had one in the second half that wasn’t and the goal is a great goal,” Jones told Sky Sports. “It’s a great ball, it’s a great counter-attack, it’s onside and it’s cost us three points. That’s cost us three points once again.

‌



“And the arrogance of the linesman is mental because he’s like looking at me as if I’ve just volleyed his cat! He is looking at me as if I have done something and going, ‘Nah.’

“The biggest error of the night and he’s cost us the game and that is the Championship. Because the Championship is brutal, these are a good side, we’re competing with monsters.”

View 2 Images Tyreece Campbell saw his goal disallowed for Charlton against QPR (Image: Charlotte Wilson/Offside/Offside via Getty Images)

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Jones also made it clear that he had been unhappy with the decisions made in Charlton’s previous game. The club lost 4-0 to Stoke City last weekend, going behind to an early Justin Devenny penalty and seeing Danny McNamara sent off shortly after the interval. The ruling out of Campbell’s goal against QPR appeared to compound the manager’s frustration with officials.

“We scored the only goal of the game and once again, I’m sick of it,” Jones said. “Honestly, I’m sick of it. On the weekend, I had to put up with a performance from an individual that was…I want to use adjectives but I can’t because I’ll get in trouble…that was beyond the realms of belief.”

Article continues below

Charlton will hope to get back to winning ways against Portsmouth on Saturday. Meanwhile, QPR are set for a tough trip to current league leaders West Bromwich Albion this weekend.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta spotted 'raging' at three Arsenal stars during Napoli win
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta spotted 'raging' at three Arsenal stars during Napoli win

Arsenal secured a narrow win at Napoli on Wednesday night and, as they attempted to see out the game, Mikel Arteta lamented three of his players for not tracking back

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta saw Arsenal keep up their percent start to the season

Mikel Arteta was seen letting rip at three of his attacking players during Arsenal's win over Napoli - demanding that they work off the ball.

‌



The Gunners kept up their perfect start to the season after winning in Naples, owing to Martin Odegaard's strike on 75 minutes. The Premier League champions though were wasteful throughout as they spurned numerous chances.

‌



After missing one that would've made it 2-0, Arteta felt that Kai Havertz, Noni Madueke and Christos Tzolis weren't tracking back as Napoli countered in an attempt to score a late equaliser.

‌



The Arsenal boss blasted the trio, demanding that they get back into position, which was spotted by TNT Sports co-commentator Lucy Ward.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



She said: "Mikel Arteta was absolutely raging on the sidelines that Havertz, Madueke and Tzolis weren’t recovering after that attack. It was so interesting. As the Arsenal attack finished, those three all sort of ambled back, and Mikel Arteta ran down the sidelines and shouted at them to recover."

Arsenal were able to hold out as they secured victory in what will be one of their more challenging away days in the Champions League. Although they do still face a daunting trip to Bayern Munich later in the tournament.

Arteta was full of praise for how his side performed and felt the narrow margin of victory didn't highlight how dominant they were, but admitted that they were wasteful in front of goal.

‌



View 2 Images Martin Odegaard scored Arsenal's winner in Italy (Image: Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC)

He said after the game: "We fully deserved the three points. The performance probably doesn’t reflect the result, the team was superb. We showed quality in a lot of moments to break them down and it was a shame because we missed so many great chances.

"On any other day the result would be different. We should have done it in a different way because of the amount of chances we created but we got the win in the end."

Article continues below

On his Norwegian match winner he added: "Martin is contributing with goals that are impacting results which is what we want from our attacking players. We want them to be decisive and certainly he was again today."

Sports.title: Man Utd confirm final Champions League squad for Sabah clash as eight players added
Sports.content:
Man Utd confirm final Champions League squad for Sabah clash as eight players added

Manchester United have confirmed their 25-man Champions League squad, with eight players added to the B-list ahead of their opening match against Sabah FK

View 2 Images Michael Carrick's Man United Champions League squad has been finalised (Image: NurPhoto, NurPhoto via Getty Images)

Eight players have been added to Manchester United's squad ahead of their Champions League clash against Sabah. United make their return to Europe's top competition by welcoming the Azerbaijani side to Old Trafford on Thursday night.

‌



Michael Carrick's side feature in the tournament nearly three years after finishing bottom of their group in 2023/24. United named their 25-man Champions League squad last week, with highly-rated youngsters Kobbie Mainoo and Leny Yoro notably absent.

‌



That squad remains fixed for the league phase, yet both players remain available for selection thanks to the B list. Players can be allocated in this area if they are young and club-trained.

‌



Players born on or after 1 January 2005, who have been eligible to play for the club for two consecutive years since turning 15 (or three years including a loan spell), are permitted to feature on the B list. This list can be updated throughout the tournament, with players required to be submitted to UEFA either on or before the day prior to a Champions League fixture.

United have moved swiftly to place Yoro and Mainoo on the list alongside six further players. Left-back Harry Amass, central defender Daniel Armer, Darren Fletcher's sons Jack and Tyler Fletcher, midfielder Jim Thwaites and exciting prospect Shea Lacey have all been named ahead of United's first European outing of the campaign.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Youngsters Ayden Heaven and Tynan Thompson were ineligible to feature on the B list. Both players have been placed in United's 25-man squad or 'A list' as neither has been at United long enough to qualify for the 'B list'.

Amass could yet feature for United after Luke Shaw missed training on Wednesday. Carrick suggested the defender had simply earned another recovery day.

United's participation in Europe's premier competition has been less frequent than the club grew used to following Sir Alex Ferguson's exit. Nonetheless, Carrick is determined to galvanise his team towards a strong showing in the Champions League and deliver both consistency and a deep run in the tournament.

‌



"Well, we certainly can achieve it, we're capable of achieving it," said Carrick. "It's up to us to then take the step of doing that. I think you saying that as well shows the steps that we're trying to make from previous years of not being in the later stages of the competition.

View 2 Images Leny Yoro and Kobbie Mainoo are on Man United's Champions League B list (Image: Ash Donelon, Manchester United via Getty Images)

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



"I think we've got to be humble enough and realistic enough to know where we're coming from and where we want to get to. That, like you say, Bruno's only played in that one. It's part of us to keep pushing the standards and to be the best we can possibly be.

"We want to be there as quickly as possible, as everybody does, but again, it's understanding the steps that need to be put in place to be able to do that.

"We're capable of some really, really good things, and especially on our day, we feel that we can go up against anybody and come out on top.

‌



"It's up to us to bring that over a consistent period and consistency through games. In the end, that gets you the results and hopefully puts us in those stages that you're talking about."
