Demirovic quickly re-established the lead ​in the ​26th minute and then completed ​the hat-trick with a hooked volley six minutes later. “For me personally it was the perfect start and also for the team as a whole,” Demirovic told Dazn.

Quick Guide Championship: Ten-man West Brom win at Derby to go top Show West Bromwich Albion held on for a memorable 1-0 victory over Derby at Pride Park, after playing for more than an hour with 10 men. Aune Heggebø's early goal proved enough to take the Baggies top of the table, despite Brayann Pereira being dismissed on his debut after collecting two first-half yellow cards. Derby had started the stronger, but West Brom swept downfield to score in the 16th minute, Jimmy-Jay Morgan whipping in a low cross from the left which Heggebø [pictured] finished at the near post. The visitors were rocked by the dismissal of Pereira in the 34th minute, as he was shown a second yellow card for a clumsy challenge on Charlie Taylor. The hosts went close just before half-time when David Ozoh flashed a low ball across the six-yard box with no white shirt able to turn it in. Derby should have levelled in the 68th minute but Lars-Jørgen Salvesen headed over from Joe Ward’s cross. Late on, Nat Phillips made a great clearance after a late goalmouth scramble, summing up a performance full of grit and resolve. James Morrison's side move above West Ham to top the Championship table with 13 points from six games. Either Charlton or QPR could have joined them on 13 points, but the sides played out a stalemate at the Valley. Derby, meanwhile, slipped into the bottom three with their fourth defeat in six games. Norwich moved up to ninth in the table as they edged past visitors Birmingham 2-1 to make it three wins in four league games. Oscar Schwartau's screamer opened the scoring, the young Dane lashing an unstoppable right-footed drive past James Beadle from 25 yards out. Papa Diallo's first goal for the Canaries doubled their advantage before the break, as the Senegal winger sidefooted home from Andre Brooks' cross. Carlos Vicente pulled a goal back for the visitors, but wasted a glorious chance to equalise near the end as Chris Davies’ men suffered their first league defeat this season. Press Association Photograph: Morgan Harlow/Getty Images Europe Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Sporting, quarter-finalists last season for the first time since 1983, fought back to see off Galatasaray 3-1 in Lisbon.

Galatasaray took an early lead through Gonçalo Inacio’s own goal but Geny ​Catamo punished poor defending to equalise in the 27th minute. Luis Suárez converted a 57th-minute penalty to put Sporting ahead and a blistering free kick from Rodrigo Zalazar six minutes later sealed the win.

Sports.title: Cole Palmer powers Chelsea to comeback win over Leeds in nine-goal epic
Sports.content:
Where’s the fun in doing it the easy way? Chelsea remain chaotic at the back but can drag their opponents into horrible places. It helps, mind you, to have some assistance from the referee. Jarred Gillett and Cole Palmer? They made for a killer combination as Chelsea swerved embarrassment and treated Stamford Bridge to one of life’s rarities: a classic in the third round of the Carabao Cup.

Gillett, a referee who always seems to be guessing when he makes key calls, was the villain as far as Leeds were concerned. They had just gone 2-0 up when Gillett altered the flow of the tie by pointing to the spot after Pep Chavarría made the most of slight contact from Daniel James. The subsequent conversion from Palmer was inevitable and from there so was the comeback from Chelsea, who rattled through four goals in 12 minutes before eventually reaching the last 16 by winning 6-3.

It made little sense. It could have gone down as Xabi Alonso’s first misjudgment as Chelsea’s manager. The Carabao Cup is important given the Spaniard’s side are not in Europe, but his rotation almost backfired. Chelsea were shambolic after making nine changes – the 16-year-old debutant Reggie Watson was overrun in midfield while Estêvão Willian and Jamie Gittens struggled in attack – and Alonso was in emergency mode when he made a quadruple change at half-time.

“I take responsibility,” Alonso said. “No player is to blame. It’s the decisions we took. When you don’t have this time to work with them, it’s difficult to compete at this level. I need to take my own blame for the things that happen. I need to be able to help them better. They are not responsible. After you need to react and think what’s better for the team.”

Quick Guide Championship: Ten-man West Brom win at Derby to go top Show West Bromwich Albion held on for a memorable 1-0 victory over Derby at Pride Park, after playing for more than an hour with 10 men. Aune Heggebø's early goal proved enough to take the Baggies top of the table, despite Brayann Pereira being dismissed on his debut after collecting two first-half yellow cards. Derby had started the stronger, but West Brom swept downfield to score in the 16th minute, Jimmy-Jay Morgan whipping in a low cross from the left which Heggebø [pictured] finished at the near post. The visitors were rocked by the dismissal of Pereira in the 34th minute, as he was shown a second yellow card for a clumsy challenge on Charlie Taylor. The hosts went close just before half-time when David Ozoh flashed a low ball across the six-yard box with no white shirt able to turn it in. Derby should have levelled in the 68th minute but Lars-Jørgen Salvesen headed over from Joe Ward’s cross. Late on, Nat Phillips made a great clearance after a late goalmouth scramble, summing up a performance full of grit and resolve. James Morrison's side move above West Ham to top the Championship table with 13 points from six games. Either Charlton or QPR could have joined them on 13 points, but the sides played out a stalemate at the Valley. Derby, meanwhile, slipped into the bottom three with their fourth defeat in six games. Norwich moved up to ninth in the table as they edged past visitors Birmingham 2-1 to make it three wins in four league games. Oscar Schwartau's screamer opened the scoring, the young Dane lashing an unstoppable right-footed drive past James Beadle from 25 yards out. Papa Diallo's first goal for the Canaries doubled their advantage before the break, as the Senegal winger sidefooted home from Andre Brooks' cross. Carlos Vicente pulled a goal back for the visitors, but wasted a glorious chance to equalise near the end as Chris Davies’ men suffered their first league defeat this season. Press Association Photograph: Morgan Harlow/Getty Images Europe Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Equally Alonso can take credit for responding. His moves were decisive. Reece James offered security after replacing Watson and Pedro Neto scored after coming on for Malo Gusto, who could barely complete a pass during a wretched first half. Leeds, beaten at this stage for the 14th time in 18 years, were overwhelmed once their lead was halved. Morgan Rogers and Palmer were devastating after replacing Estêvão and Gittens. Rogers had a hand in four goals and Palmer, who scored twice, seemed affronted by the notion of Leeds going through.

It finished as another thrilling attacking display from Chelsea, who have scored 16 goals in Alonso’s first five games. There are flaws to fix at the other end, though. Leeds also experimented, Daniel Farke making eight changes, but controlled the first half. They led when the Bosnia and Herzegovina centre-back Tarik Muharemovic, signed from Sassuolo last summer, headed Harry Wilson’s corner past Mike Penders in the 23rd minute.

Chelsea have already conceded 10 goals in all competitions. Leeds could have doubled their lead through Sean Longstaff. Valentín Barco and Watson, son of the former Wigan midfielder Ben Watson, were second best in midfield.

Leeds were on their way when Barco lost possession three minutes into the second half. Ethan Ampadu charged past Rogers and found Lukas Nmecha, who teed up Brenden Aaronson to make it 2-0.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Pedro Neto fires home Chelsea’s third goal at Stamford Bridge. Photograph: Adam Davy/PA

Chelsea needed a lift. Chavarría crossed from the left and went to ground. Gillett whistled and Palmer scored with 53 minutes played. “He gave out of nothing a penalty where it wasn’t even a chance for them,” Farke said. “A quality player scores and the body language of the Chelsea players was different.”

Palmer was in his element, equalising in the 55th minute after Rogers laid the ball off for his pal to stroke a casual finish past Michael Zetterer from 20 yards. Chelsea were rampant and led on the hour, Palmer and Rogers combining for Neto to finish well. Leeds looked dizzy. They readied the changes but Danny Welbeck made it 4-2 with a sharp turn and finish in the 65th minute.

Leeds kept fighting. Dominic Calvert-Lewin came on and pulled one back to remind Alonso of Chelsea’s defensive weaknesses. Chelsea responded, Rogers crossing for Barco to score his first goal for the club. The sixth followed, Barco’s mis-hit shot diverted in by Welbeck. “A crazy nuts game,” Farke said. That’s been the way for Chelsea under Alonso.

Sports.title: Scottish Premiership: Miovski hits last-gasp Rangers winner and Celtic keep 100% record
Sports.content:
A dramatic last-gasp strike from substitute Bojan Miovski gave Rangers a 1-0 Premiership win over St Mirren at Ibrox.

Back in the technical area after a two-game touchline suspension, Derek McInnes watched St Mirren’s Australian goalkeeper Jacob Chapman keep the home side at bay in the first half with a string of saves, albeit helped by some poor finishing.

Craig McLeish’s side, who lost 5-1 at Ibrox in the Premier Sports Cup last month, grew in confidence after the break and Fraser Taylor missed a great chance while the frustrated home support returned to the state of agitation which characterised the start of the season.

However, in the final seconds of normal time, Miovski, on for Djeidi Gassama, pounced in the box to grab the winner to make it four victories in a row.

Summer signing Mika Baur notched his first goal for Celtic as the Scottish champions maintained their perfect start to their title defence with a 1-0 victory away to St Johnstone.

View image in fullscreen Celtic’s Mika Baur scored his first Celtic goal at McDiarmid Park. Photograph: Steve Welsh/PA

The German midfielder struck from close range early in the second half after the debutant Hoops keeper Sam Johnstone had produced a stunning first-half save to deny Saints midfielder Joel Cotterill.

It was a night when the Celtic head coach, Martin O’Neill, was able to demonstrate the depth of his squad before Sunday’s Old Firm meeting away to Rangers in the Premier Sports Cup, with key players such as Camilo Duran, Benjamin Nygren and Kieran Tierney on the bench and defender Cameron Carter-Vickers given the evening off.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Although far from their convincing best, the Hoops did enough to close out a sixth consecutive league victory this term and their 13th in a row in total stretching back to the closing weeks of last season.

Sports.title: Boxing Day is back: Premier League makes early announcement on Christmas fixtures
Sports.content:
Christmas has truly come early with the Premier League announcing the return of a full Boxing Day schedule for the 2026/27 season.

A cherished date in the football calendar, last campaign saw just one game played, which saw Manchester United beat Newcastle 1-0.

2 Premier League fans can get excited for the return of Boxing Day fixtures Credit: Getty

It was the fewest amount of games to take place on December 26 in Premier League history.

Not since 1982 had there been less matches on Boxing Day, and that was only because there were none that year.

However, in an early announcement, there will now be seven Premier League games on December 26.

What are the Boxing Day games?

Boxing Day fixtures for 2026/27 season Aston Villa vs Leeds United - 12.30pm

Everton vs Sunderland - 3pm

Fulham vs Brighton- 3pm

Ipswich Town vs Brentford - 3pm

Tottenham Hotspur vs Bournemouth - 3pm

Hull City vs Liverpool - 5.30pm

Newcastle United vs Manchester City - 8pm

The festivities will begin with Aston Villa hosting Leeds in the lunchtime kick-off at 12.30pm.

There will then be four 3pm games: Everton vs Sunderland, Fulham vs Brighton, Ipswich vs Brentford and Tottenham vs Bournemouth.

Hull will host Liverpool in the 5.30pm game before the day concludes with Newcastle vs Manchester City at 8pm.

The remaining fixtures in Gameweek 17 will take place on December 27.

Chelsea visit Coventry at 2pm, Nottingham Forest head to Manchester United at 4.30pm and Crystal Palace welcome Arsenal at 7pm.

Why was there just one Boxing Day game played in 2025?

The traditional set of Boxing Day fixtures in 2025 were abandoned due to expansion of UEFA competitions, while FA Cup matches were moved to take place on weekends.

But with Boxing Day this year to fall on a Saturday, the Premier League are able to broadcast a full set of fixtures.

2 Boxing Day football is a tradition unlike any other Credit: Getty

Fans were left furious by the scrapping of Boxing Day games last year, with the Premier League announcing in November 2025 that they would return to the calendar this term.

And on Thursday, they announced their rundown of Boxing Day games - more than a month earlier than they did last year.

The decision to go early has reportedly been due to pressure from clubs to allow fans to be given more time to plan, which will minimise any disruption.

Meanwhile, the Football Supporters Association have been in talks with those involved for the clashes to be announced sooner rather than later.

Gameweek 17 has subsequently been amended before any games dating from November onwards.

Sports.title: Premier League star boycotts Switzerland over furious World Cup row with manager
Sports.content:
Leeds forward Noah Okafor has revealed he will not play again for Switzerland as long as boss Murat Yakin is in charge.

The 26-year-old has released a lengthy statement on social media, where he has commented on broken promises and betrayed trust.



4 Okafor has declared he will never play under Yakin again for Switzerland's national team Credit: Getty

Okafor, who has scored twice in 26 games for the Red Crosses since making his international debut in 2019, was part of their World Cup squad in North America.

What has Noah Okafor's role been at major tournaments?

Having been frozen out of selection since November 2024, the former AC Milan man was hopeful of playing a key part in North America following a season in which he scored eight Premier League goals for Leeds.

But for the second major tournament in a row, he played a peripheral role - much to his dismay.



The former Red Bull Salzburg star, who made three outings from the bench at the 2022 World Cup under Yakin's tutelage, was an unused substitute in each of Switzerland's five fixtures at Euro 2024.

And in the most recent edition of football's global tournament, Okafor was again overlooked by Yakin - making just one appearance from the bench - while remaining on the bench on five occasions.



Okafor is no stranger to public fall-outs with Yakin, with the latter previously questioning his attitude and his impact on the pitch.

He has now issued a statement on Instagram where he has vowed to never represent his country again - though he did hail Yakin for guiding Switzerland to the quarter-finals of the World Cup for the first time since 1954.



What has Noah Okafor said about his Switzerland future?

Okafor said: "Dear fans, these lines are the hardest I have written in my career so far, after careful consideration, I have decided to step back from the Swiss national team until further notice.

"This decision is extremely difficult for me, but I want and must express it now, there was never anything greater for me than playing for Switzerland.

"Every time I wore this jersey, I tried to leave my heart on the pitch. I would have loved to continue playing for Switzerland in the future and giving everything for our country.

4 Okafor has been an unused substitute in ten of Switzerland's last 11 matches in major tournaments Credit: Getty



4 Yakin has previously questioned Okafor's attitude Credit: Getty

"But under the current circumstances, I simply can no longer do so. It is important to me to clarify one thing, this decision has nothing to do with playing minutes.

"I know that I haven't always done everything right in the past. Young players make mistakes, and I have apologized for that. But now the situation is different.

"Even during the World Cup, I always accepted difficult phases and put myself at the service of the team. It was a great honour for me to be at the World Cup for my country.



"I believed for a long time that the situation would change. A year after the European Championship, Murat Yakin came together with members of the coaching staff specifically to see me in England to have a clarifying conversation.

"It was a very appreciative and good conversation. We were able to look forward and clear up misunderstandings. I was grateful to Murat Yakin for that.

"That is precisely why I traveled to the World Cup with a good feeling, full of motivation and with the firm intention of giving everything for the team and for Switzerland.

"Which made what I experienced there all the more disappointing. Not because I played very little, but because of the way I was treated. For me, it was the most difficult time of my career so far.



"First off, I know that some people will now think again, 'Ah, Okafor again, he's just offended because he hardly played.'

"But again, my decision has nothing to do with my playing minutes. I travelled to the tournament to support my team in the best possible way - on the pitch and off it.

"Things happened that deeply affected me. Trust has been broken. Promises were not kept. And when I was allowed to play against Algeria, even minor mistakes were reacted to far away from our goal in a way that deeply hurt me.

"In the weeks since, I have thought a lot and decided for myself that under the current manager, I no longer want to play for the national team.



"Murat Yakin is doing a great job and has achieved something historic with Switzerland. Success proves him and his work right.

4 Okafor's only outing in the 2026 World Cup came against Algeria - a 19-minute cameo off the bench Credit: Getty

"And of course, I don't want any special treatment from him. Only mutual respect and trust - but I don't see this foundation for the coming years.

I sincerely wish the team all the best. I am happy about every success of the team and think that we achieved great things at the World Cup.



"Many of my teammates are friends, and I will continue to cheer for them and support them.

"I am grateful to Switzerland for everything I was able to experience. Playing for this country was and remains something very special.

"Believe me, whenever I stood on the pitch, I left my heart for this jersey. See you soon, Noah."

Switzerland captain Granit Xhaka was quick to message a love heart emoji, along with striker Breel Embolo.



Okafor, who has registered one assist from five outings for Leeds this term, will be looking to open his account for the season against Newcastle next Monday night.

Sports.title: ‘He’s struggling’ – Liverpool starter must step up or risk brutal transfer
Sports.content:
Milos Kerkez must up his game at Liverpool or risk being sold - he is not justifying his £40million price tag.

That's the view of many across the talkSPORT network as the 22-year-old continues to struggle since joining the Reds from Bournemouth in 2025.



4 Liverpool defender Kerkez is struggling for form, leading many to question his role in the team Credit: Getty

A stellar 2024/25 season at the Vitality Stadium saw the left-back register eight goal contributions from 38 top-flight matches.

But he failed to replicate the form that saw him emerge as one of the division's top full-backs in his opening campaign in Merseyside.

Chipping in with just one goal and two assists, the defensive part of his game was also called into question.



There was hope from Reds fans that his performances would improve this term after his former mentor Andoni Iraola replaced Arne Slot in the dugout.

However, despite starting in the club's opening four games of the season, his struggles persist, with his ball-watching almost proving costly in Wednesday night's 2-1 win over Atletico Madrid in the Champions League.



He allowed Marcos Llorente to run beyond him after failing in his attempt to play the offside trap, with Liverpool managing to fight back to claim all three points.

What has been said about Milos Kerkez?

Prior to the game, Liverpool cult hero Danny Murphy told talkSPORT that the player is one of Iraola's biggest problems.



And now legendary broadcaster Andy Gray, who was on commentary duty for talkSPORT, has cast doubts over Kerkez.

He said: "The Kerkez I saw at Bournemouth is not the Kerkez I am watching right now, that’s what I would say.

“I was not surprised Liverpool went and bought him when he was playing for Bournemouth – one of the best full-backs in the league by a distance.

4 Hungary international Kerkez has failed to replicate the form he showed at Bournemouth Credit: AFP



“But he hasn’t quite settled into that role where he was there.

"I don’t know whether sometimes a club’s too big for people, I hope that’s not the case with Kerkez."

Kerkez was a topic of discussion on the Sports Breakfast show on Thursday morning, with Rangers legend Ally McCoist quick to point out his role in Atletico's opener.

He stated: "He's struggling, isn't he? You can see it, and it's not through lack of effort, he's definitely trying to get forward, but he gets caught for the goal.

"I don't know what he's thinking about the goal, he's got to look at the ball and see that he's not going to get out in time.



"He's deeper than his two centre-backs, Llorente has timed his run well and finishes it really, really well."

4 Kerkez still has four years left on his contract in Merseyside Credit: AFP

Meanwhile, the Telegraph's Merseyside correspondent Dom King questioned whether Liverpool could look to sell Kerkez should his form not improve.

He remarked: "There is a position that either Milos Kerkez has to raise the standards or it will end up being something that Liverpool have to assess.



"But still a work in progress, when they don't press in sync then there's problems for the defence, but they're getting there."

For ex-Manchester United forward Alan Brazil, his mind has already been made up over the defender - insisting Liverpool should bin him off in 2027.

In a blunt assessment of Kerkez, he simply stated: "He's got to go, I'm sorry."

Charlie Adam, who won the League Cup at Liverpool in 2012, was yet another that has commented on growing concerns regarding Kerkez.



4 Iraola is yet to taste defeat from his opening four matches as Liverpool boss Credit: Getty

He said: "I thought there were moments [against Atletico] where I just worry, at times Liverpool are so open, when they go and they try and go full press they're getting caught at the moment.

"A lot of the goals last year were similar to that in transition, there were big spaces for Atletico to attack and that's where the goal comes from into [Julian] Alvarez and he slides it in [to Llorente].

"I think the back line, Kerkez needs to drop because [Virgil] van Dijk actually pushes up and he doesn't see what's behind him, Kerkez needs to go with the runner."



It remains to be seen whether Kerkez will start against Fulham on Saturday, or whether Iraola turns to Kostas Tsimikas.

Sports.title: Erling Haaland backed to overtake Cristiano Ronaldo and make all-time football history
Sports.content:
Erling Haaland has been tipped to become the highest scorer in football history.

The Manchester City striker has already scored five goals in all competitions this season.

4 Haaland has been backed to become football's all-time leading scorer Credit: Getty

His latest strikes, a brace against Porto on Tuesday, have seen the 26-year-old tipped to surpass Cristiano Ronaldo's scoring feats.

The five-time Ballon d'Or winner is currently the all-time leading scorer in the history of the sport with 979 goals for club and country.

Haaland's Champions League double has taken his career tally to 364 goals in 440 matches, with Ronaldo having played 890 more times.

Haaland backed to become all-time great

talkSPORT's Darren Bent believes the Norway forward can go on to make history, though.

Speaking on Drive alongside Andy Goldstein, he admitted: "There’s definitely an argument to say that he could be one of the greatest natural goalscorers we’ve ever seen. His numbers are just crazy."

Bent added: "I know a lot of players that get so bogged down by touches, getting involved and needing to feel it. He does not care if he touches the ball in a game 10 times."

Ronaldo, who turns 42 in February, is set to retire next summer with this season earmarked as his last in professional football.

In order to overtake his goal tally, Haaland would have to score 39 goals a season for 16 years if he was to play until he was 42.

However, Bent is concerned longevity could be the only factor that stops him from making history.

The former England international explained: "The only thing that will stop him being the greatest goalscorer of all-time is longevity.

4 Ronaldo's record tally currently stands at 973 goals in 1,330 matches for club and country Credit: Getty

"If he gets injured or something because he has had his injury problems.

"I’m not quite sure he’s as durable as (Cristiano) Ronaldo. Ronaldo would just go season upon season upon season."

Haaland has previously faced ankle issues amongst other injuries in his career.

His longest absence for City since joining the club in 2022 saw him miss just 10 matches between December 2023 and January 2024, though.

Can Haaland surpass Ronaldo?

When told how many goals Haaland must score per season to overtake Ronaldo, Bent replied: "There’s no reason why he can’t do that. There’s no reason why he can’t, he’s got everything.

"He’s not bothered about touches. All he cares about is that (scoring) and I really respect him.

4

"The biggest compliment I can give him, other than him being fantastic, is that he’s always ready for when that chance comes.

"The amount of times a striker will miss an opportunity and we go, ‘he wasn’t ready for that’. That never happens to Haaland. Or we go, ‘that’s come too early for him’.

"He almost prides himself on ‘it doesn’t really matter’, minute one or minute 90, whenever it may be, I might not touch the ball for 25 minutes, when that chance comes that’s what I’ve been brought in for. To finish off these chances.

"I just think he’s been phenomenal ever since he made his debut."

Haaland's scoring feats

Haaland has already scored 167 goals in 203 appearances for City across the last four years.

Of those 115 have been in the Premier League, with Haaland the quickest player ever to reach a century of goals in the competition.

4 Haaland's brace against Porto has taken his career total to 364 goals in 440 games Credit: Getty

Erling Haaland's career statistics 2015-17: Bryne - 0 goals in 16 apps 2017-19: Molde - 20 goals in 50 apps 2019-20: Red Bull Salzburg - 29 goals in 27 apps 2020-22: Borussia Dortmund - 86 goals in 89 apps 2022-Present: Manchester City - 167 goals in 203 apps 2019-Present: Norway - 55 goals in 62 caps Total: 364 goals in 440 apps

The three-time golden boot also has a goal-a-game record in the Champions League with 59 in 59 for City, Borussia Dortmund and Red Bull Salzburg.

His scoring figures at international level are even more impressive, though.

Haaland has 62 goals in 55 caps for Norway since making his debut as a 19-year-old in 2019.

Those include seven goals at this summer's World Cup as he fired his nation to the quarter-finals.

Sports.title: The biggest British football rivalries, including the only elite level city derby
Sports.content:
Every football fan will argue that their club's biggest and fiercest rivalry deserves its place on the UK's 'Mount Rushmore' of derbies.

Well, even talkSPORT has struggled to narrow the picks down to just four selections.



8 Sports fans use Mount Rushmore - the iconic carved sculpture depicting influential US presidents - as a benchmark to list the most influential things in a specific subject - but talkSPORT argues four is not enough! Credit: Getty

Every Thursday, Max will pick his definitive list using the Mount Rushmore ranking method - four iconic people, matches etc - in a variety of categories. However, four is quite hard, so he's arguing for a fifth, which is why Max has called his Mount Rusmore-or-less.

And there's no better place to start than derbies; it's the one every fan first looks for and is essentially a cup final within itself.

Celtic vs Rangers: 'More than just football'

Scott explained: "This is a 50-50 divide within the city, separated by the River Clyde, and it's more than just football.



"I know that's cliché, but this is political, this is religious, and it's the fiercest derby out there.

"And that 12.30 kickoff on a Saturday or a Sunday, which is in place, by the way, for policing and safety purposes, is compulsory viewing."



Celtic and Rangers fans have been banned from attending Old Firm away matches as a result of the on-pitch clashes between supporters.

"I'd much rather watch League One than Scottish football," Scott added. "However, when it's the Old Firm Derby, you have to watch it.



And even if you're one of these people that sits there and thinks, 'Rangers and Celtic wouldn't make it out of the Championship', you cannot deny that this, as a derby, in and of itself, is unlike anything we'll ever see in England.

8 Dating back to 1888, Glasgow hosts one of the fiercest derbies in football and you can guarantee there will be fireworks Credit: Getty Images - Getty

8 As well as fiery battles on the pitch, both sets of supporters have been involved in large-scale disorder leading to away fans being banned from games Credit: PA

'The biggest and best rivalry'

"This is partly down to the violence which we've seen prevent away fans from going into the stadiums.



"In many ways, it's a stain on the game, but you cannot take away from how passionate this is.

"For me, watching the Old Firm Derby, it's like a break away from a much more sanitised version of football that we get in the Premier League.

"And I love the Premier League. It's still the best league in the world, but the authentic, raw passion that you get in Glasgow on an Old Firm Derby day is unrivalled.

"Arguably, it's the fiercest, the biggest, the best rivalry in UK football in derbies!"



Aston Villa vs Birmingham is 'an absolute corker'

Scott continued: "I think people have a little bit of a recency bias because Birmingham haven't been in the Premier League since 2011, but that doesn't take away from how much these two clubs hate each other.

What is Mount Rushmore? The faces of George Washington, Thomas Jefferson, Theodore Roosevelt and Abraham Lincoln are carved into the stone in South Dakota, chosen for their representation of the most important events in the United States' history. As a result, fans use the idea to create their own version to list the most influential or iconic games and people that define their selected categories.

8 Although the sides have been in different divisions, the passion between Birmingham and Villa fans remains high Credit: Getty

8 The UK is home to some of the most fiery rivalries in world football where you can guarantee things will get heated among fans, players and coaches

"St. Andrews and Villa Park are just 2.4 miles apart. It's, in fact, the closest derby in England."



The Second City Derby hasn't taken place since 2019, when Jack Grealish was assaulted by a Blues fan on the pitch before he scored the winner in a 1-0 triumph for Villa in the Championship.

Scott said: "That catapults his career, or one of the many things to catapult his career to become a treble winner that we saw at Manchester City.

"Just because it's outside London, just because these two clubs aren't always in the Premier League, doesn't mean this isn't an absolute corker of a rivalry."

Arsenal vs Tottenham is the only legitimate elite-level derby in London

This season, there are six Premier League clubs based in the capital, which means there are 30 combinations of a London derby each year.



And that's just in the top-flight; Charlton Athletic, Millwall, Queens Park Rangers, and West Ham make up the London sides in the Championship - with all 10 sides also potentially facing each other across each of the two domestic cup competitions as well.

However, Nottingham Forest fan Scott argued: "I've got a bee in my bonnet about Londoners trying to create a rivalry out of everything.

"QPR against West Ham, it's not a derby. The only legitimate elite-level derby in London is the North London Derby.

"It's a genuine turf war. You go back to 1913, and the Woolwich Arsenal, now Arsenal, were a South London club until they moved to Highbury, and it became a turf war.



"And that's essentially the feel I get from Arsenal and Spurs fans about how much they hate each other. It's like a gang turf war.

"This is a legitimate, fierce, massive UK rivalry.

"And the irony is, this now-famous song about North London forever that Arsenal sing, it's not legitimate.

"Spurs have been the forever North London club. And so, apologies, Arsenal fans, it's a massive derby, but Spurs were there first."

8 Arsenal's move from south to north London in 1913 sparked the rivalry that has seen countless flashpoints - and Arsenal winning the league at Tottenham's home twice Credit: Getty



Statistically, the dirtiest derby in UK football

It's not the Old Firm Derby. It's the Tyne-Wear Derby, averaging over five yellows a game and a red card every other game.

"It goes all the way back to King Charles I, who essentially gave Newcastle a monopoly over the coal industry, which had an economic impact on Sunderland. That's where this hatred begins.

"And it's not just back to the times of King Charles and Cromwell. This is industry rivalry, whether it's coal, whether it's shipmaking.

"They've always been at loggerheads. They've always been in competition, and you see that on the football pitch.



"I think they'll probably look down on these sort of so-called London rivalries when QPR or Fulham are playing Chelsea.

"It's not a scratch on the Tyne-Wear Derby, let me tell you."

8 Police officers hold back a crowd of Newcastle fans outside St James' Park prior to Sunderland's arrival in March Credit: Getty

8 Man United have many enemies in the Premier League, but the rivalry with Liverpool trumps that with City as well as the Merseyside derby Liverpool contest with Everton Credit: Getty

What has been snubbed?

"I haven't included Millwall vs West Ham," Scott began while leading up to his fifth and final selection.



"I haven't included the Steel City derby in Sheffield. I haven't included the East Midlands derby, the Brian Clough derby between Forest and Derby. Haven't included the Merseyside derby, for crying out loud..."

But to add insult to Everton's injury, Liverpool have been included - but against arch-rivals Manchester United.

"The reason being, these are the biggest clubs in England, two of the biggest institutions in world football.

"Both have got 20 titles. Liverpool, of course, have a slightly richer European history, but you think about [former managers] Fergie, Paisley, Shankly, Klopp.



"They have permeated English football imagination since the get-go. Two clubs, both with their own sort of tragedies.

"These are the biggest clubs in England. Nobody can argue otherwise, and therefore I can't not have them in my Mount Rushmore - or less of UK football derbies.

"It's elite. Simple as."

Sports.title: Evangelos Marinakis axes another manager as multi-club owner acts after seven games
Sports.content:
Evangelos Marinakis axes another manager as multi-club owner acts after seven games

Evangelos Marinakis has sacked Olympiacos manager Jose Luis Mendilibar just seven matches into the new season.

The departing boss becomes the 25th manager dismissed by the Greek businessman, who also owns Nottingham Forest and Rio Ave, in 16 years.



3 Mendilibar has been sacked by Olympiacos seven matches into the new season Credit: Getty

Mendilibar has been dismissed despite not losing a match inside 90 minutes so far this season.

However, he has paid the price for Olympiacos' failure to reach the league phase of the Champions League.

His side were beaten on aggregate by NEC in the third qualifying round after an extra-time defeat in the second leg.



Despite an unbeaten start domestically in the league and cup, Mendilibar was sacked after Tuesday's 3-2 win over Volos.

Reports claim Imanol Alguacil will be appointed as the next Olympiacos manager.



The former Real Sociedad boss is available after leaving Al Shabab in February.

Alguacil previously won the Copa del Rey during his time with Sociedad.



His first match in charge of Olympiacos could be at home to OFI Crete on Saturday.

Olympiacos statement

In a statement confirming his exit, Olympiacos said: "In football, as in life, there are cycles that eventually close, but what resonates in eternity is what you have achieved.

"The appreciation, respect and love of the Olympiacos family will accompany you forever, General, along with the strong emotions that united us and are eternal. Thank you for everything."

3 Mendilibar paid the price for Olympiacos' early Champions League exit Credit: Getty



Mendilibar had been in charge since February 2024, with the Spaniard winning the Conference League later that year.

He followed up that success with a domestic double in his first full season as manager.

Olympiacos missed out on the title last season, though, finishing six points behind AEK Athens.

Marinakis' manager history

Mendilibar is the latest manager to be dismissed by Marinakis during his time as a football club owner.



The 59-year-old has now axed 25 across his three teams since first buying Olympiacos in 2010.

Marinakis completed a takeover of Nottingham Forest in 2017 before adding Portuguese side Rio Ave to his portfolio three years ago.

3 Marinakis has now dismissed 25 managers in 16 years as a football club owner Credit: Getty

At Forest alone, he had four different permanent managers last season, with Oliver Glasner becoming the club's fifth head coach in 10 months in July.



However, his methods have delivered success across his clubs.

Olympiacos have won 11 league titles in 16 years under his stewardship, with Marinakis is into his second spell as club president.

Meanwhile, Forest returned to the Premier League for the first time in 23 years back in 2022.

They have since remained in the top-flight as well as reaching the Europa League semi-finals last term.

As for Rio Ave, they have established themselves in the Liga Portugal, with this season their fifth consecutive campaign in the first-tier.
