Sports.title: Richarlison in talks with FIFA over drastic action to force Tottenham transfer
Sports.content:
Richarlison in talks with FIFA over drastic action to force Tottenham transfer

Richarlison has approached FIFA to try and terminate his Tottenham contract, talkSPORT understands.

The Brazilian believes he has a case to tear up the final year of his deal after being left out of Spurs' 25-man Premier League squad.

4 Richarlison may have already played his final match for Tottenham Credit: Getty

Richarlison is in talks with Vasco da Gama about a return to his homeland.

Could Richarlison have left Tottenham in the summer?

The 29-year-old had been heavily linked with a return to Everton before the summer window closed.

He scored 53 goals in 152 games for the Toffees during his four-year spell in Merseyside between 2018-2022.

But he subsequently rejected the chance to link up with David Moyes.

He then issued a statement on social media where he referred to Everton as his 'favourite team', while slamming Spurs for how they acted during negotiations.

And having then been left out of the north London outfit's top-flight squad, he is now seeking a swift exit away from the club.

Richarlison isn't the first player to take their case to FIFA after being shunned by their employers.

Last year, his compatriot Renan Lodi was in a similar situation at Al Hilal, with the full-back left out of their Saudi Pro League squad.

He sought out FIFA intervention to rip up his deal to join Brazilian outfit Atletico Mineiro, with football's governing body upholding his claim.

Richarlison, who started in Spurs' opening Premier League day defeat away at Brentford, could now have played his last game for the club.

4 Brazil international Richarlison has scored 32 goals in 134 games for Tottenham across all competitions Credit: AFP

What has been said about Richarlison?

Reacting to the news live on talkSPORT, former Crystal Palace owner Simon Jordan believes that a dangerous precedent could be set if the forward gets what he wants.

He said: "He's been demoted now to the Under-21s, hasn't he?

"What they'll be citing is some degree of sporting chance that enables him to have his contract [ripped up].

"I think it would be tragic if they did, because it means that players could do as they want.

"They can be dreadful and have no consequence, they can have dreadful discipline, and dreadful behaviour and have no consequence behind it.

"FIFA are an adjudication, but if the club haven't done their job properly and protected their position, and there is a threat here and there is a threat to the contractual status because he's been demoted to a different space to the contract that he signed, which is obviously a signature for the first team...

4 Richarlison was part of Spurs' squad that won the Europa League in 2025 Credit: Getty

"As an owner's mentality, I would think that's pretty sad that a player can get away with being an absolute pest."

Jordan was then pressed by co-host Jim White as to whether that Richarlison's contract being ripped up works best for both parties.

To which he remarked: "I'm sure Tottenham wants him to go, but not on his terms.

"I'm sure Tottenham realise that, they must have a commercial view on what he's worth.

"They must have an understanding of what it's worth to get rid of him, because he doesn't want to be there, and they probably don't want him.

"So what would be the purpose of parking him up, running down his contract, paying his wages and getting nothing for him?

4 Richarlison is into the final year of his contract in north London Credit: Getty

"So despite the fact I'm not the greatest admirer of those that are running Tottenham Hotspur at this moment in time, I don't think they're that silly.

"So there is clearly a distinction between the player and his representation, believing they can get exactly what they want, how they want, where they want, irrespective of what makes it work for those that hold his registration.

"If that's the world we are now living in with contracts, pretty soon contracts will be worth nothing."

Referencing Lodi's case, Jordan then added: "Hopefully the circumstances are not the same, and he [Richarlison] doesn't get to exploit a loophole.

"And if he does, then Tottenham Hotspur are fools and left themselves open to it."

Jordan then urged Spurs to try and keep hold of the player until the January window, before flogging him off.

Sports.title: Liverpool star Alisson Becker hit with £8,000 fine after furiously lashing out at fourth official's board following penalty decision during Reds' 2-2 draw with Nottingham Forest
Sports.content:
Alisson Becker has picked up an £8,000 fine for misconduct following a furious outburst in the wake of Liverpool's 2-2 draw with Nottingham Forest last month.

The Brazilian goalkeeper was left raging after he conceded a penalty to Oliver Glasner's side at Anfield, with former Red Neco Williams being hauled down in the area.

Morgan Gibbs-White subsequently buried the spot kick, before Victor Munoz levelled the scores to help Andoni Iraola's side avoid defeat.

Becker, still livid with the penalty decision at full time, was seen kicking the fourth official's board as he made his way towards the tunnel, and on Thursday was hit with a four-figure fine for the outburst.

A statement from the FA read: 'Liverpool's Alisson Becker has been fined £8,000 for misconduct at the Premier League fixture against Nottingham Forest on 29 August.

'It was alleged that the goalkeeper acted in an improper manner around the tunnel area after the final whistle.

🚨 Alisson Becker has been fined £8,000 for misconduct during the match against Nottingham Forest z😳! pic.twitter.com/dEF2qDcjIX — The Final Whistle (@Rufus_45) September 10, 2026

Alisson Becker in a heated discussion with referee Sam Barrott during the clash with Forest

Alisson has been fined £8,000 after kicking the fourth official's board in frustration following Liverpool's 2-2 draw with Nottingham Forest last month

'Alisson Becker has subsequently accepted the charge against him and received the standard penalty.'

The sanction follows a ruling from the Premier League's Key Match Incidents Panel which found that the penalty should not have been awarded in the first instance.

The body, however, insisted that VAR Michael Oliver was correct not to advise on-field official Sam Barrott to review the decision on a pitchside monitor, with the incident not reaching the threshold for a video intervention.

The KMI panel voted 3:2 that Barrott should not have given the penalty, and supported the VAR outcome 5:0.

'The contact from Alisson was inevitable as a consequence of his momentum in attempting to save the ball,' the KMI Panel said. 'The contact made was not reckless and below the threshold for a penalty.

'However, the non intervention by the VAR was unanimously supported on the basis that it was not a clear and obvious error.'

Sports.title: Leeds star Noah Okafor QUITS international football aged just 26 after explosive bust up with Switzerland manager
Sports.content:
Leeds United winger Noah Okafor has told Switzerland he will not play international football again while boss Murat Yakin remains in charge.

The 26-year-old was part of the Swiss World Cup squad but played just once - as a late substitute in the round-of-32 win over Algeria. The World Cup call-up came after four goals in his final four games of the season for Leeds.

In March, he ended a 16-month exile from the Switzerland squad after a clear-the-air meeting with Yakin, who he had previously criticised - along with Swiss bosses - for failing to communicate with him while he was not being selected.

Okafor referred to the rift in a subsequent interview, admitting that 'I know I didn't do everything right.'

But now he has decided to step away from the international arena.

In a statement on Instagram Okafor said: 'Dear fans, these lines are the hardest I have written in my career so far. After careful consideration, I have decided to step down from the Swiss national team until further notice.

'This decision is extremely difficult for me, but I want to and must state it now. There was never anything greater for me than playing for Switzerland.

'Every time I have worn this jersey, I have tried to leave my heart on the pitch. I would have loved to continue playing for Switzerland in the future and give everything for our country. But under the current circumstances, I simply cannot do it anymore.

'It is important to me to clarify one thing: This decision has nothing to do with playing minutes. I know that I haven't always done everything right in the past.

'Young players make mistakes, and I have apologized for that. But now the situation is different.

'Even at the World Cup, I always accepted difficult phases and consistently put myself at the service of the team. It was a great honor for me to be there for my country at the World Cup.

'I believed for a long time that the situation would change. A year after the European Championship, Murat Yakin came to England with members of the coaching staff specifically to have a clarifying conversation with me.

'It was a very appreciative and good conversation. We were able to look forward and clear up misunderstandings. I was grateful to Murat Yakin for that.

Noah Okafor has featured in all of Leeds' games so far this season

'That is exactly why I travelled to the World Cup with a good feeling, full of motivation, and with the firm will to give everything for the team and for Switzerland.

'All the more disappointing for me was what I experienced there. Not because I played little, but because of the way I was treated. For me, it was the most difficult time of my career so far.

Okafor emphasised that he was not concerned about his lack of minutes but alluded to a lack of 'mutual respect' and 'trust' from Yakin.

'One thing up front: I know that some will think again now: "Oh, Okafor again, he's just offended because he hardly played",' his statement continued.

'But again: My decision has nothing to do with my playing minutes. I travelled to the tournament to support my team in the best possible way. On the pitch and off it.

'Things happened that hit me deeply. Trust was broken. Promises were not kept. And when I was allowed to play against Algeria, even small mistakes far away from our goal were reacted to in a way that hit me deeply.

'In the weeks after that, I thought a lot and decided for myself that I no longer want to play for the national team under the current coach. Murat Yakin is doing a great job and has achieved historic things with Switzerland.

Okafor has not always seen eye to eye with Switzerland boss Murat Yakin

'The success proves him and his work right. And of course, I don't want any special treatment from him. Only mutual respect and trust, but I do not see this foundation for the coming years.

'I sincerely wish the team only the best. I am happy about every success of the team and think that we achieved great things at the World Cup. Many of my teammates are friends, and I will continue to root for them and support them.

'I am grateful to Switzerland for everything I was able to experience. Playing for this country was and remains something very special. Believe me: Whenever I was on the pitch, I left my heart out there for this jersey. See you soon, Noah.'

The Swiss FA confirmed the news, saying in a statement: 'Noah personally informed us today that he will no longer be playing for the national team for the time being. We respect his decision and wish him good luck and success with his club.'

Sports.title: Revealed: How Tottenham WOULD have won the Premier League in 2017 without Chelsea's goals from 'illegal' signings.... after Mauricio Pochettino demanded the crown be handed over
Sports.content:
Former Tottenham boss Mauricio Pochettino has fervently argued that Spurs should be retrospectively crowned Premier League champions because of Chelsea's 'illegal' activity in the transfer market - and the numbers suggest he may well have a point.

Chelsea pipped Spurs to the Premier League title under Antonio Conte in 2017, finishing the season on 93 points - seven clear of Tottenham's 86 - but have since admitted to breaking the rules by making more than £47million in secret payments to unregistered agents and third parties to facilitate transfers.

The Blues were handed a record £10.75m fine for the breaches, a sanction regarded by many football fans as little more than a slap on the wrist given what Chelsea went on to achieve with the team they had assembled.

David Luiz, Eden Hazard, Willian, Nemanja Matic, Ramires, Andre Schurrle and Samuel Eto'o were the seven signings at the heart of Chelsea's 'illegal' transfer activity under Roman Abramovich, with the first four going on to play key roles in Conte's title-winning side.

Had Hazard, Willian, Luiz and Matic not been at Stamford Bridge to score the 26 goals they managed between them during Chelsea's 2016-17 campaign, Pochettino's title claim would, at least in theory, check out - although there are some obvious caveats.

Strike these goals from the record books and Chelsea would have finished the season on just 79 points, seven behind Tottenham who would have been crowned champions.

Former Spurs boss Mauricio Pochettino believes Spurs should be retrospectively crowned Premier League champions for the 2016-17 season over Chelsea, who broke transfer rules

Eden Hazard was one of seven players signed by Chelsea 'illegally' - the Blues paid more than £47million in secret payments to unregistered agents and third parties to facilitate transfers

Tottenham finished second in the Premier League - on 86 points - behind winners Chelsea

2016-17 TABLE WITHOUT CHELSEA'S 'ILLEGAL' GOALS 1. Tottenham - 86 points 2. Man City - 82 points 3. Chelsea - 79 points 4. Liverpool - 78 points *based on Chelsea results after goals from Eden Hazard, Willian, Nemanja Matic and David Luiz are removed

Of course, Chelsea would have fielded different players in their absence, who could well have scored in their place, while it is impossible to know exactly how those matches would have played out under such different circumstances.

That aside, Chelsea's first altered result that season came on the opening weekend, when Hazard scored the opening goal to help the Blues carve out a 2-1 victory over West Ham United.

Scratch off that goal and Chelsea would have drawn 1-1, two points worse off.

In December 2016, Hazard and Willian both scored during Chelsea's 3-1 win over Manchester City at the Etihad, meaning another two points were directly gained from goals scored by 'illegal' signings.

Later that month, Willian's brace against Stoke on New Year's Eve helped the Blues to a 4-2 win over Stoke City, who would theoretically have drawn without the Brazilian's contribution. Another two-point deduction here puts Chelsea on six points worse off so far.

On January 31, Luiz scored a superb free-kick to open the scoring against Liverpool, who ultimately came from behind to draw 1-1 at Anfield.

Rule out Luiz's goal and that draw becomes a defeat, at least in the context of this thought experiment, meaning another point is stricken from Chelsea's tally.

Hazard plagued the Hammers again in the reverse fixture at the London Stadium on March 6, opening the scoring as Chelsea triumphed 2-1, a result that would have otherwise been a draw and cost them two points.

The penultimate fixture affected was the Blues' 2-1 win over Stoke on March 18, when Willian opened the scoring before Gary Cahill struck a late winner. Remove Willian's goal and another win becomes a draw, with Chelsea's three points reduced to one.

Finally, Chelsea's 2-1 triumph over Manchester City at Stamford Bridge in April came courtesy of a match-winning double from Hazard, meaning that without the Belgian's goals, Conte's side would have lost the game and failed to register a single point.

Tot up the points deductions from those matches and Chelsea would have finished 14 points worse off at the end of the season, finishing on a tally of 79 with a goal difference of just 26 (rather than 52).

The recalculation actually drops Chelsea down to third place behind Manchester City, who would have been four points better off because of the 'draw' at the Etihad in December and 'win' at Stamford Bridge in April.

City, who finished Pep Guardiola's debut season at the Etihad on 78 points, would instead have tallied 82 points and thus finished ahead of Conte's Chelsea.

Led by Harry Kane, Tottenham came close to their first Premier League title under Pochettino

Willian (left) and David Luiz (right) also played a key role in Chelsea's 2017 title-winning season

CHELSEA'S 2016-17 RESULTS WITHOUT 'ILLEGAL' GOALS Date Match Actual result Result without 'illegal' goals Points lost Aug 15 Chelsea vs West Ham 2-1 1-1 2 Dec 3 Man City vs Chelsea 1-3 1-1 2 Dec 31 Chelsea vs Stoke 4-2 2-2 2 Jan 31 Liverpool vs Chelsea 1-1 1-0 1 Mar 6 West Ham vs Chelsea 1-2 1-1 2 Mar 18 Stoke vs Chelsea 1-2 1-1 2 Apr 5 Chelsea vs Man City 2-1 0-1 3 Total: 14 points

While this recalculation should be taken with a huge pinch of salt, it does clearly display why Pochettino feels so aggrieved over Chelsea's 'illegal' transfer business.

The now USA manager said on Tuesday: 'We should win one title, one Premier League. We should have been awarded it. They were punished. They admitted it. The title should be for the team that was second.

'We deserve to be champions that year. We didn't compete with the same rules. It's impossible if some clubs play with offside and others don't or one plays with VAR and another plays without VAR. For everyone the same rules and then the same capacity to create the best team.'

He continued: 'Maybe with the same rules we could've signed some players that would have made the team better or scored more goals. It's not me complaining, it's the truth.

'I have no doubt and I'm not scared to say the truth. The Chelsea fans will be upset with me but if Tottenham broke the rules, I'd say we don't deserve the title.

'I don't say they didn't play well or that Conte wasn't great. I don't want this message twisted. But if you broke the rules, then "ciao", you need to give it to another team.'

Sports.title: Manchester United facing ANOTHER protest... as furious local residents hit back over club's plans to open fanzone behind the Stretford End
Sports.content:
Manchester United facing ANOTHER protest... as furious local residents hit back over club's plans to open fanzone behind the Stretford End

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Manchester United are facing another protest – this time from its neighbours.

Fans disgruntled with the club’s ownership are planning to march to Old Trafford ahead of the weekend’s Manchester derby.

And it appears that United is also on a collision course with local residents over plans to introduce a first-ever fanzone at its iconic stadium.

Last month, officials unveiled proposals for The Paddock, a 1,300-venue they want to open behind the Stretford End in time for the club’s autumn fixtures.

They say they have responded to demand from fans and that the facility will provide ‘food, drink and lively entertainment’.

However, the fanzone will require planning permission – and some of those who live close to the iconic stadium are not impressed. A petition of 50 signatures has been lodged with Trafford Council, with locals listing a variety of concerns over the plans.

Some have mentioned the prospect of increased ‘noise pollution’ and say the club have chosen the location without thinking of their neighbours and purely because the site involved will not take away lucrative car parking spaces.

Local residents have hit back over Man United's plans to open a fanzone directly outside Old Trafford's Stretford End

They have been accused of ignoring the quality of life of those who live nearby and only looking ‘to do what’s best for them’. ‘They have plenty of space (elsewhere),’ wrote one, ‘where their additional noise would not directly impact on residents but they have chosen to locate the fan zone a short distance away’.

The petition says the fanzone will be ‘just 110m’ from nearby houses and says it will operate for up to six additional hours on 19 to 30 occasions each year. It adds that 36 residential properties are within 150m of the proposed site with a population that includes families with young children, the elderly and those work irregular shifts – all of whom would be impacted by increased noise.

United say the free-to-enter venue will only open on matchdays and that they are fully committed to working with residents. They add that the Paddock will adhere to noise management guidelines and say further work is being carried out to mitigate concerns, which will include sound-proofing and ensuring speakers are pointed away from residential areas. A decision will land in due course.

Fans group The 1958 are organising a protest ahead of Sunday’s clash with City in a row over the club’s recent crackdown on ticket touting.

Sports.title: Baseball icon and Hiroshima atomic bomb survivor Isao Harimoto dies aged 86
Sports.content:
Baseball legend Isao Harimoto, who survived the atomic bombing of Hiroshima, has died aged 86.

The Korean-Japanese icon, who was born in Hiroshima in 1940 to Korean parents who migrated to Japan during the country's rule of Korea, died in Tokyo on Wednesday.

Growing up, he overcame huge adversity as a child. Firstly he was involved in an accident in 1944 that left him with severe burns on his right hand.

The result of that left him with limited mobility in his thumb and forefinger, while his middle three fingers became permanently curled.

Then a year later, he survived the United States of America's atomic bombing of Hiroshima during World War II on August 6, 1945.

Harimoto, whose birth name was Jang Hun, survived after his mother used her body to shield him and one of his sisters from the blast. However, sadly another sister did not survive. Between 60,000 and 80,000 people were killed instantly - with the final death toll calculated at 135,000.

Korean-Japanese baseball legend Isao Harimoto died aged 86 in Tokyo on Wednesday

Known as the 'Hit Machine' he recorded the most hits in Japanese baseball history at 3,085

After a difficult childhood, Harimoto later turned his attention to baseball. He had to learn to play left-handed due to his injuries and wore a custom glove to fit his injured right hand that allowed him to catch the ball.

But despite those hindrances, Harimoto enjoyed a distinguished 23-year career - playing for Toei Flyers, the Yomiuri Giants and the Lotte Orions across his homeland. At the Flyers he helped them win their first Japan Series in 1962.

Known as the 'Hit Machine' he recorded the most hits in Japanese baseball history at 3,085 and is the only player in Nippon Professional Baseball League (NPB) to surpass the 3,000 landmark.

Furthermore he is the only player in NPB history to hit over 500 home runs and steal more than 300 bases - with his figures at 504 and 319 respectively. By comparison, only three players in Major League Baseball history have achieved the same feat in Barry Bonds, Willie Mays and Alex Rodriguez.

An 18-time All-Star, he was inducted into the Japanese Baseball Hall of Fame in 1990.

The Golden Players Club, one of Japan’s two halls of fame, wrote: 'All members of the Meikyukai express our deep respect and gratitude for Mr Isao Harimoto’s many years of great achievements, and we sincerely pray [following] his passing.'

Sports.title: Chelsea Confidential: Marco Palestra injury update revealed, scouting blow for Blues, Xabi Alonso's view on the Declan Rice 'foul', club's stance on Mauricio Pochettino title talk and latest on missing Geovany Quenda
Sports.content:
Marco Palestra is getting closer to his Premier League debut after this week taking part in individual training with one of Xabi Alonso’s coaches at Cobham, Confidential can reveal.

That was a precursor to participating in Chelsea’s main sessions which would be the final step before being passed fit for selection. Alonso is keen to have him available, but learned his lesson when rushing back Moises Caicedo, who reinjured himself upon returning two weekends ago.

The manager has been preaching caution with both Palestra and Caicedo since that setback, with the Blues boss insisting he will only use the pair once he believes it does not represent a risk. Before the September international break, Chelsea have Hull at home and Brentford away.

Chelsea signed Palestra for £47million from Atalanta. He was named Serie A Defender of the Year while on loan at Cagliari last season, where he was named the fastest player in the division.

The 21-year-old Italian seems set to play an important role under Alonso after the wing back and full back was a feature throughout pre-season, starting in friendlies against Tottenham, Juventus, AC Milan and Real Sociedad.

However, Palestra was then missing from the first matchday squad that won 3-2 at Fulham and has not been seen since, including in Wednesday night's Carabao Cup clash with Leeds. Alonso said he picked up his problem in training a few days prior to travelling to Craven Cottage.

With sources saying Palestra is now involved in outdoor work, he appears to be nearing availability. Confidential asked Alonso earlier this week whether Caicedo was training, and Chelsea’s manager said he was, so the midfielder is likewise closing in on his own return.

Marco Palestra is getting closer to his Premier League debut with Chelsea after this week taking part in individual training, Confidential can reveal

Chelsea midfielder Moises Caicedo is likewise closing in on a return

CHELSEA LOSE SCOUT TO ADARABIOYO AGENCY

One of Chelsea’s leading scouts, Stewart Thompson, has left the club and joined the football agency, WNRS, headed up by Gbolahan Adarabioyo, the brother of Tosin. Thompson made the move to Chelsea as a first-team scout in 2023. Prior to that, he had been a UK and European scout for Manchester City since 2010.

WNRS handled Tosin’s switch to Tottenham on deadline day. That was understood to be worth an initial £10m with a further £2m in add-ons for Chelsea.

Spurs boss Roberto De Zerbi was said to play a pivotal role in that signing, along with securing Mykhailo Mudryk on a season-long loan with a £75m option to buy. In a blow to Tottenham, Mudryk has suffered an ankle injury in training and is set to be sidelined for several weeks.

Meanwhile, Mahdi Nicoll-Jazuli, the 16-year-old academy prodigy who impressed on Chelsea’s pre-season tour of Australia and Asia, has also joined WNRS. The agency’s tagline is: ‘Football management – built for winners.’

Chelsea's Mykhailo Mudryk, who is on a season-long loan at Spurs, has suffered an ankle injury in training and is set to be sidelined for several weeks

ALONSO TURNS QUESTIONER

In between asking Alonso about free agents and Caicedo earlier this week at Cobham, Confidential wanted to know the Chelsea manager's thoughts on Morgan Rogers’ reaction when he shoved Declan Rice in their 2-1 loss to Arsenal at the Emirates Stadium.

Whether he liked his player showing such passion. Whether he would have preferred his £117m summer signing to have kept a cool head. Alonso did answer, but only once he had asked Confidential a couple of his own questions first. Here’s how our exchange went:

CONFIDENTIAL: ‘Rogers got a yellow for shoving Rice – do you like that passion or would you rather he did not react?’

ALONSO: ‘Did you see the tackle?’

CONFIDENTIAL: ‘I did.’

ALONSO: ‘And?'

CONFIDENTIAL: ‘And Rice should have been the one booked with a Chelsea free-kick for the trip.’

ALONSO: ‘It was clear. It was pretty clear. It’s the emotion of the game. Sometimes, to be able to manage all of them, it’s difficult. We were trying to find the equaliser. Morgan saw the chance to get into the box. It was a tackle that was very… I don’t know how to say in English…’

CONFIDENTIAL: ‘Cynical?’

ALONSO: ‘Cynical – that’s a good one. He showed his frustration. But it’s part of the game.’

Morgan Rogers shows his frustration with Declan Rice after the Arsenal man's 'cynical' foul

CAS: NO CHELSEA CONTACT

Confidential checked in with the Court of Arbitration for Sport, who say there has been no request from Chelsea concerning how they missed out on signing Lamine Camara from Monaco on deadline day.

We have not heard of any desire to try to escalate that situation into a legal matter, either.

Chelsea remain disappointed with Monaco for how they pulled the plug on that £47m deal, but the noise coming back from inside Stamford Bridge is that they are moving on from what happened.

POCH: STRIP CHELSEA OF THE TITLE

If there was any doubt left within Chelsea that they should not have hired a head coach whose heart was still with Tottenham, Mauricio Pochettino may have just wiped that away.

In an hour-long interview conducted in London with various newspapers, Pochettino, now in charge of the United States, said Chelsea should be stripped of their 2017 Premier League title and that it should be awarded to Tottenham, who finished second that season.

That follows Chelsea being fined £10m this summer for breaching rules relating to payments to agents between 2009 and 2022. The club escaped sporting and retrospective sanctions.

Other than some raised eyebrows, it does not appear there will be an official response to Pochettino’s comments from Chelsea.

Pochettino, now in charge of the US national team, said Chelsea should be stripped of their 2017 Premier League title

GRAHAM POTTER AND THE PHILOSOPHER’S MOAN

Speaking of former Chelsea managers having a pop…

Graham Potter is currently the head coach of the Swedish national team and has been using his Instagram for some sly digs at his old club. The former Chelsea and West Ham boss was surprisingly frank after he uploaded some snaps of himself trying Pilates.

When one user commented: ‘Hopefully you are better at Pilates than you are a football manager.’

Potter replied: ‘I’ll try not to do Pilates in a dysfunctional place and I will be OK.’

When another user responded: 'Didn’t mind the money though, did you?’

Potter replied: ‘Absolutely not.’

They were West Ham fans to whom he was replying, so maybe he will still be welcomed back at Stamford Bridge should he ever want to survey a Swedish player for his national team.

Graham Potter tries a spot of Pilates - and posts it on his Instagram feed

And he was surprisingly frank in an the exchange with a West Ham fan that followed

GEORGE-OUS SAVING

Everton’s deal to sign Tyrique George was worth £24m – £18m plus £6m in add-ons – while Chelsea will retain a 15 per cent sell-on fee for any future sale.

It is already looking like a bargain from Everton’s perspective. Not only because of the 20-year-old’s goal against Manchester United at the weekend, but he can also help David Moyes with his striker shortage, having been used up front at Chelsea.

CHANCE FOR PAEZ TO GET BACK ON TRACK

There was considerable excitement before Kendry Paez arrived.

Chelsea secured him from Independiente del Valle in Ecuador on a pre-agreement worth £17.3m when he was 16 years old, and he arrived once 18. However, loans with sister side Strasbourg and Argentinian club River Plate did not go to plan amid speculation surrounding his lifestyle.

Chelsea tried to find him an English club to join on loan until the end of the summer but they were unable to do so. Now, he is 19, somewhat stuck, and not in Alonso’s first-team plans.

What it does give Paez is the chance to work with Chelsea staff for a few months at least, and hopefully that can do him some good. In the last two years, this South American teenager has lived in Ecuador, France, Argentina and England.

It has been a chaotic time for him, and hopefully he can use this period to focus on getting his once-promising career back on track.

Kendry Paez, 19, has been here, there and everywhere since joining Chelsea but is now with the club for a spell and can hopefully knuckle down

PANEL TO REVEAL GABRIEL VERDICT

The Premier League’s Key Match Incidents panel sit down each week to review the major refereeing decisions from every weekend, delivering a verdict on whether calls were right or wrong.

Previously, the results remained private, used only to tell Howard Webb’s organisation where their officials were in the wrong. As of this season, they are being made public.

That means by this time next week, we should know whether this panel believe Arsenal centre back Gabriel should have been in bother for kicking Chelsea goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez in the head during that Premier League showdown at the Emirates.

There are certainly some within Chelsea who think Gabriel got away with one. Alonso was asked for his take on the Gabriel-Martinez incident, but he said with a little smile at the end of his answer: ‘I have my opinion but we’ll leave it there.’

Arsenal's Gabriel kicks Chelsea keeper Emi Martinez in the head at the Emirates last weekend - but he escaped punishment

QUENDA ABSENCE – A TECHNICAL DECISION

Geovany Quenda was an unused substitute in the Carabao Cup against Leeds, having only appeared once in all competitions all season, coming on in the 82nd minute at Fulham in Chelsea’s first Premier League match of the campaign.

Sources close to Quenda say he is not carrying any injury, and that he is fully fit.

It appears, therefore, it is simply down to technical decisions that Alonso is not using the 19-year-old winger and wing back who arrived from Sporting CP this summer. Chelsea spent £40m to acquire him on a pre-agreement.

Sports.title: Mauricio Pochettino reignites Mike Dean spat following his 'stupid' remark in 2019 - as he claims referee is now 'showing people how he was' after his controversial 'minigames' claims while officiating Premier League games
Sports.content:
Mauricio Pochettino reignites Mike Dean spat following his 'stupid' remark in 2019 - as he claims referee is now 'showing people how he was' after his controversial 'minigames' claims while officiating Premier League games

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Mauricio Pochettino believes Mike Dean is trying to be 'controversial' to remain in the spotlight as he reflected on his personal experience with the former referee which included a 'stupid' comment from the latter.

Dean enraged many last week after admitting to playing a game where he would see how long he could go without blowing his whistle while officiating Premier League matches.

The 58-year-old, who retired in 2023 after over 20 years of officiating at the highest level, also revealed that he would try and stay in the centre-circle for as long as he could during some games.

Following the backlash, Dean has since issued a statement, insisting he did always apply the letter of the law when he was an official.

And following this incident, former Tottenham Hotspur manager Pochettino is not surprised and believes Dean is now 'showing people how he was'.

Pochettino and Dean were once embroiled in a heated moment caught on camera during the 2018-19 season with Spurs in a title challenge. On February 23, 2019, the pair were involved in a bust-up after Tottenham had lost 2-1 at Burnley.

😡 Wow! 😡



Fair to say Mauricio Pochettino is not happy with referee Mike Dean after his side’s loss at Turf Moor! 😱



Reaction in our live blog: https://t.co/8ntnbWB8dh pic.twitter.com/boXTN2od8f — Sky Sports Premier League (@SkySportsPL) February 23, 2019

Mauricio Pochettino (right) had a bust-up with Mike Dean (left) after a Tottenham loss in 2019

Pochettino's assistant Jesus Perez also got involved following Spurs' 2-1 defeat at Burnley

As soon as the full-time whistle blew, an angry Pochettino stormed on to the pitch to confront Dean before walking away then returning to argue further after an apparent comment from the referee.

His assistant, Jesus Perez, intervened and can be heard shouting 'say that again, in front of the camera,' at Dean amid the melee, as Pochettino was led away by Burnley defender Phil Bardsley.

Pochettino was subsequently given a two-match touchline ban as well as a £10,000 fine for his role, while Dean was dropped as a fourth official for the London derby between Chelsea and Tottenham just a few days later.

Speaking about Dean and the Turf Moor tetchiness, the current United States manager said: 'What he said was a stupid thing. But our code is we never talk about what happened on the pitch. It's like what happened in Las Vegas - stays in Las Vegas.

'But in that moment we were under pressure. The perception was "Tottenham need to win something." It's true that we were a little bit under pressure.

'We were disappointed in that game. He said one stupid thing, it makes you react so quick. It's not that we cannot deal with it.

'But it was like in my position, I would never do that. How do you say? Make a joke? I'm not going to be the funny guy to do some joke if you are under pressure in your job.'

And Pochettino's thoughts on Dean's latest remarks? 'He was controversial. His character now - he's showing how he was,' the Argentine continued.

Pochettino was given a two-game ban and fined £10,000 but says Dean said a 'stupid' remark

Speaking last week, Dean admitted to sometimes trying to see how long he could go without blowing his whistle when refereeing Premier League matches

'People maybe like him, people maybe do not. Maybe now he's playing a little bit with the personality, and to try to be funny, and to create some controversial things.

'He's putting some salt, pepper, like a chili, some condiments (on a steak). He needs to understand that "OK, let's not put gasoline on to the fire".

'It was always funny to be with him. We had a good relationship. It was only this action, that situation, that was tough because we were in a very sensitive moment.'

Speaking last week on the Jamie Vardy's Having a Party podcast, Dean said: 'There used to be games we would have for a laugh.

'It would kick-off, right; see how long we could go without blowing a whistle. I done that a few times in the Premier League, before VAR, obviously. Went 20, 25 minutes without blowing the whistle.

'I used to do another one in the Premier League, I used to stand in the centre circle and see how long I could stay in the centre circle before I had to leave. That was just me joking about. Got about 15 minutes once, in one game.'

Sports.title: Richarlison 'wants to RIP UP his Tottenham contract' with unhappy star looking to force return to Brazil after being relegated to Under-21 squad
Sports.content:
Richarlison wants Tottenham to terminate his contract so that he is free to move to Brazilian club Vasco, according to reports.

The 29-year-old wantaway, who was Tottenham's top scorer with 11 goals last season, failed to secure a transfer before deadline day and is now training alone in exile after being omitted from Roberto De Zerbi's official 25-man Premier League squad and relegated to the Under 21s.

Richarlison had been linked with a return to Everton as part of a deadline-day swap deal involving Iliman Ndiaye, but the move ultimately collapsed - paving the way for the Toffees winger to join Manchester City for £65million instead.

According to Brazilian outlet Globo, Richarlison is furious with Tottenham's decision not to register him for the Premier League and wants the north London club to rip up his contract so that he can join Vasco as a free agent.

The report claims Richarlison's lawyers are set to file a request in court to terminate his deal, which is due to expire at the end of the season.

Richarlison’s case is similar to that of fellow Brazilian Renan Lodi, who claimed in court last year that he was prevented from practising his profession after being left out of Al-Hilal's Saudi Pro League squad. He was subsequently able to sign for Atletico Mineiro after securing the unilateral termination of his contract.

Richarlison reportedly wants Spurs to terminate his contract so that he is free to move to Vasco

The Brazilian has not been named in Roberto De Zerbi's official 25-man Premier League squad

It is also reported that Richarlison wishes to play for the Rio de Janeiro outfit until December 2026 before considering his options.

Last week, De Zerbi told Richarlison his Tottenham exile is a problem entirely of his own making, revealing the Brazilian rejected contract talks at the start of the summer.

Spurs went on to sign Manchester City duo Omar Marmoush and Savinho to bolster De Zerbi's attacking ranks this summer after the club narrowly avoided relegation last campaign.

'You don't know one important thing,' said De Zerbi before Tottenham's 0-0 draw with Nottingham Forest on Saturday. 'At the beginning of pre-season I spoke to Richarlison and asked him if he wanted to extend his contract because I was happy to keep him with us, and he didn't want to.

'So, Richarlison is a good player, yes. He was important last season, yes very important. He's a good guy, yes. But in the end, I have to stop myself putting pressure on the players if the players show me they want to leave.

'So, I'm sorry for him but we have to go to another page and work with Dominic Solanke and Omar Marmoush.'

Sports.title: Rory McIlroy left young girl in tears with what he did at Irish Open
Sports.content:
Rory McIlroy left young girl in tears with what he did at Irish Open

Rory McIlroy is back at the Irish Open this week as he bids to defend the title he won in emotional fashion 12 months ago

View 3 Images Rory McIlroy was crowned Irish Open champion in 2025 and is back to defend his title (Image: Getty)

Rory McIlroy's warm act left a young fan in tears at the last renewal of the Irish Open. The Northern Irishman is now aiming to retain his crown at Trump International Golf Links in Doonbeg.

‌



Fresh off a historic first Masters win, McIlroy arrived at the Irish Open 12 months ago to relentless cheers from fans basking in his Career Grand Slam. He quietly began the tournament, posting a 71, before taking off in rounds two and three, carding 66 and 68, respectively.

‌



Heading into the final round, McIlroy was four strokes off the lead before having to match a late Sunday surge by Sweden's Joakim Lagergren. As McIlroy approached the 18th, he trailed Lagergren by two and needed an eagle to force a play-off. He managed exactly that, sinking a 28-footer before winning the play-off at the third hole and bagging the £752k top prize.

‌



The 37-year-old will have a third Irish Open title on his mind this week. But he already has the support of local fans, as evidenced by a heartwarming interaction with a young fan in 2025.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

Rory McIlroy lifted the lid on private remark from caddie that will always stick with him READ MORE :

After the third round had concluded last year, McIlroy headed to the media tent content with his score of 68. But as he approached the structure, he noticed a young girl from the fan area shouting his name.

‌



View 3 Images The Northern Irishman was victorious after a three-hole play-off (Image: Getty)

In a kind-hearted move, McIlroy walked over to the youngster and threw her the ball he had been using that day. Overwhelmed, the girl burst into tears of joy.

She hugged the woman next to her, presumably her mother, then stared at the ball in youthful amazement. McIlroy's actions touched commentators, as they let out a collective 'Aww'. He'd lift the title a day later with wife Erica Stoll and daughter Poppy in attendance.

‌



The atmosphere at the Irish Open will be slightly different this year, though, as the course owner, US President Donald Trump, is set to attend during the competition's final stages.

It has been confirmed that Trump plans to be at the venue for the weekend play and it has even been indicated that he may hand the trophy to the winner. Because of the increased security his presence will bring, which will involve the US Secret Service, An Garda Síochána and the Irish Defence Forces, McIlroy admits this renewal will be distinct.

View 3 Images Trump will attend the Irish Open (Image: Getty)

‌



"I think the weekend, especially when he's here [will feel different], crowds will be limited. Obviously, there's a lot that goes on," McIlroy told BBC Sport.

"So, logistically, it provides some challenges, absolutely. But at the same time, if he wants to come and watch the Irish Open, who are we to say no?

"The one thing I'd say is his golf resorts have hosted PGA Tour events, European Tour events, LIV events. He's a big fan of golf, he's a wonderful supporter of golf.

Article continues below

"He's got a beautiful property here in Doonbeg - it's the first time I've played it. I wouldn't say it's a true links golf course, it's a bit of an Americanised version of a links course, but it's still a great golf course and should provide a good test for the week.

"It's going to be different with him being here but we're here to play a golf tournament and it's a good golf course and keep our heads down and play."

Sports.title: Declan Rice knows who he wants to win Ballon d'Or and it's NOT an Arsenal player
Sports.content:
Declan Rice knows who he wants to win Ballon d'Or and it's NOT an Arsenal player

Declan Rice is among the 30 players nominated for the Ballon d'Or but the Arsenal star is already backing one of his England team-mates to scoop the historic award

View 2 Images Harry Kane is Declan Rice's pick to win the Ballon d'Or

Declan Rice admits he wants to see England colleague Harry Kane win the Ballon d'Or - despite being nominated for the award himself.

‌



The Bayern Munich superstar, formerly of Tottenham, has just enjoyed a stellar year and is the favourite to scoop the Golden Ball, which will be handed out in London later this year. If successful Kane would be the first English winner in a quarter of a century.

‌



Rice's impressive year has him among the 30 nominees with the Arsenal midfielder winning the Premier League, reaching the Champions League final and helping England make the last four of the World Cup.

‌



Meanwhile, in Germany, Bayern talisman Kane helped the Bavarians retain their German crown during a year that saw him score 73 goals in 65 matches for club and country - and Rice is backing his compatriot to claim the Ballon d'Or off the back of that.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



The Arsenal midfielder said: “It’s the second year in a row I have been nominated. It’s obviously really good, I’m really proud. Obviously I know who I want to win it. I’d love to see Harry Kane win it, so I’m wishing him all the best in that.”

Rice is one of three Arsenal players nominated for the Ballon d’Or, alongside Gabriel and William Saliba. The pair have forged a central defensive partnership that is regarded among Europe's best. Individually they have also both lapped up huge plaudits.

This is the most open Ballon d'Or for years, owing to different individuals enjoying success at club and international level. PSG retained their Champions League crown whilst Spain backed up their Euro 2024 triumph by winning the World Cup. Fabian Ruiz is the only player to play for both, but few expect him to claim the award.

‌



View 2 Images Ousmane Dembele won the Ballon d'Or 12 months ago (Image: Kristy Sparow - UEFA/UEFA via Getty Images)

Kane, despite his goalscoring exploits, was beaten to the best Bundesliga player award by Frenchman Michael Olise. Les Blues icon Kylian Mbappe broke the record for goals scored at a World Cup, but he ultimately ended the season without a trophy.

Ousmane Dembele, the current holder, Lamine Yamal, Rodri and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia are all being discussed as potential winners, but each of them also have arguments against.

Article continues below

Since Luka Modric broke the duopoly of Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo in 2018 there have been five different winners across the seven years.

Sports.title: Richarlison goes to war with Tottenham as furious striker 'tries to rip up his contract'
Sports.content:
Richarlison goes to war with Tottenham as furious striker 'tries to rip up his contract'

The Tottenham Hotspur forward has not been included in the Premier League squad and is looking to complete a move away

View Image Richarlison is reportedly taking action to have his Spurs contract ripped up. (Image: John Walton/PA Wire)

Tottenham Hotspur forward Richarlison is trying to force the club to rip up his contract and allow him to move back to Brazil, according to reports in his home nation. The Brazilian has been linked with a move away from Spurs throughout the summer transfer window.

‌



There were talks of a potential swap deal between Tottenham and Everton, involving Iliman Ndiaye. However, the latter eventually completed a move to Manchester City.

‌



Richarlison released a statement appearing to hit out at Tottenham amid the speculation over a potential return to Everton. "After everything I've gone through in recent years, I decided that NEVER AGAIN would they decide my future for me," he wrote.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

"I went through a lot of bad things during this time, and almost all of them happened because of decisions made by other people. Pressure, threats, retaliation - none of that scares me. I've been through worse things... believe me!

"I have always made it clear, at every opportunity, that my departure to another place would also have to be good for the club. If it wasn't, I would never accept it... just as I didn't accept it when everything here was crumbling and they needed me. I stayed and gave my life. So, I hope they treat my situation with the same respect that I have always had for Spurs and for all the people who worked with me during this period. Just don't try to decide for me.

‌



“If they reach an agreement Between Spurs and Everton I will return to my heart's club. My intention was indeed to return to the place where I was very happy. It's just that negotiations were going the way people wanted, and it won't be that way anymore. Despite this turmoil, I have a contract with Spurs And I will be at the club's disposal."

He has since been linked with a move to Turkish side Trabzonspor. Reports say that he agreed a move to the club, but Tottenham rejected two offers, with the highest being £20 million.

‌



Brazilian outlet Globo now claims that Richarlison is ready to fight Tottenham to try and force his way out of the club. It's claimed that he is looking to take legal action to try and cancel his contract at sign for Vasco da Gama.

Richarlison has not been included in Roberto De Zerbi's 25-man Premier League squad, meaning that his only first team appearances can come in cup competitions. The player is reportedly using the example of Renan Lodi, who was able to have his contract terminated after benig excluded from the Saudi Pro League squad.

Vasco De Gama are said to be working on a potential deal that will see Richarlison return to his childhood club, but they won't be able to meet the asking price of more that £20m. FIFA rules are also said to be making a loan deal difficult to do.

The 29-year-old has been with Tottenham since joining from Everton in 2022. He has made 134 appearances for the club, scoring 32 goals and providing 15 assists, with his only appearance this season coming in the season opener against Brentford.

Jordan McCann sparked concerns just days before his fight with Big Stacks after he claimed to have been arrested, but he insists his fight will still go ahead

Sports.title: Alisson learns his fate as FA confirm Liverpool keeper's punishment for Forest incident
Sports.content:
Alisson learns his fate as FA confirm Liverpool keeper's punishment for Forest incident

Alisson has accepted an FA charge of misconduct and will pay a four-figure fine following his antics that came after Liverpool were held by Nottingham Forest at Anfield

View 2 Images Alisson has been charged and fined by the FA

Liverpool goalkeeper Alisson has been fined for misconduct following his behaviour after Liverpool's 2-2 draw with Nottingham Forest last month.

‌



The Brazilian felt aggrieved after giving away a penalty during the game, which came after he fouled former Red Neco Williams. Morgan Gibbs-White subsequently scored from the spot.

‌



After the full-time whistle blew Alisson's frustration remained as he was seen kicking the fourth official’s board - which had already caused controversy having not worked, which delayed Liverpool from making their substitutions in the build-up to Forest’s penalty - when leaving the pitch.

‌



Alisson accepted a charge for misconduct from the FA and has now been fined £8,000.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



A statement read: “Liverpool’s Alisson Becker has been fined £8,000 for misconduct at the Premier League fixture against Nottingham Forest on 29 August. It was alleged that the goalkeeper acted in an improper manner around the tunnel area after the final whistle. Alisson Becker has subsequently accepted the charge against him and received the standard penalty.”

The contest was Liverpool's first home game of the season, but they twice found themselves behind before rescuing a point. Dan Ndoye scored Forest's opener in front of the Kop before Alexander Isak equalised.

Gibbs-White's penalty threatened to see Forest secure a third straight win at Anfield, but summer signing Victor Munoz would come up with an impressive strike to ensure Andoni Iraola didn't taste defeat.

‌



View 2 Images Alisson had given away a penalty for a challenge on Neco Williams

It has since emerged this week that the Premier League's Key Match Incidents (KMI) Panel determined that the penalty against Alisson was wrongly-awarded by referee Sam Barrott.

Three members of the five-man panel believed the goalkeeper's challenge on Williams had not been worthy of punishment, but VAR did not intervene.

Article continues below

"The contact from Alisson was inevitable as a consequence of his momentum in attempting to save the ball," the KMI Panel said. "The contact made was not reckless and below the threshold for a penalty."

Sports.title: Arsenal icon calls out supporters and hints at Mikel Arteta transfer mistake
Sports.content:
Arsenal icon calls out supporters and hints at Mikel Arteta transfer mistake

Gabriel Martinelli's seven-year spell with Arsenal ended this summer when he moved to Saudi Arabia and a former player was left frustrated by the treatment of the player

View 2 Images Freddie Ljungberg was critical of one Arsenal transfer decision this summer

Freddie Ljungberg has called out Arsenal's fans for "forgetting what Gabriel Martinelli did for the club" after he was sold in the summer.

‌



The Brazilian arrived at the Emirates in 2019, back when Unai Emery was in charge, as an unknown quantity. He impressed when given opportunities before eventually making himself a regular in an Arsenal side that begun challenging for the Premier League title.

‌



He owned the spot on the left wing when Mikel Arteta's side first became a force, scoring 15 times in his most productive season, but he gradually fell down the pecking order as the Gunners continued to invest in more forward talent.

‌



Last season he came up with just the one goal and was named amongst the subs for the club’s last six matches of the campaign, which suggested the end was nearing to his seven-year spell. A £60million move to Al-Hilal has since taken place, but Ljungberg was disappointed to see how he was treated.

‌



The Swede said on Viaplay: "A Brazilian football player, he works that hard, the age he has and numbers and stuff, that’s not a cheap football player. And they sold him for quite a lot of money so I was a little bit [surprised] when people really wanted him out and fans wanted him out.

"I was a bit like, 'That’s a good player that you just want out', but that’s what everybody felt that they seemed to be wanting and they got rid of him. They got good money for him. Sometimes the fans forget, maybe, how much he has done for this club, how many important goals he scored during the years."

Less than two years ago and Martinelli was scoring the winner to down Real Madrid at the Bernabeu, but has since been overtaken in the pecking order with Christos Tzolis joining this summer and establishing himself on the left.

‌



View 2 Images Gabriel Martinelli was sold by Arsenal, heading to Al Hilal for a record fee

Arteta had previously been adamant that Martinelli, and his compatriot Gabriel Jesus, were going to be important figures at the Emirates, despite leaving them out of the matchday squad that won the Community Shield.

Since those comments Jesus has joined Barcelona and Martinelli has headed to the Middle East, the latter seeing Arsenal secure a record fee for the sale of a player.

Martinelli left Arsenal having scored 62 times in 278 games for the Gunners.

The UK's 'Hardest Man' - commonly known as Big Stacks - has provided an update on his fight with Jordan McCann after he was involved in a physical altercation earlier this week

View Image Big Stacks found himself involved in an altercation ahead of his fight with Jordan McCann

Tempers flared when Stacks threatened to throw a chair at the unknown assailants. Security quickly intervened and dragged the 'Hardest Man' into another room. Footage showed the Misfits star dealing with a bloodied lip after the minor scuffle.

‌



But his fight with McCann is not in jeopardy after stating he is fit to compete in the ring this weekend. Taking to social media just moments after the altercation, he said: "It's all kicked off again today.

Sports.title: Mason Mount’s true feelings on Man Utd signing THREE new midfielders this summer
Sports.content:
Mason Mount’s true feelings on Man Utd signing THREE new midfielders this summer

Mason Mount has struggled for minutes and form since moving to Manchester United and this summer saw the club sign three midfielders

View 2 Images Mason Mount's career at Man Utd is yet to take off despite spending three years at Old Trafford

Mason Mount admits the influx of three new midfielders at Manchester United has ramped up the competition, which is a "must-have" with standards raising as a result.

‌



The former Chelsea star, who moved to Old Trafford for an initial £55million three summers ago, has seen Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans and Carlos Baleba all move to Manchester in a midfield spending spree that cost £155m.

‌



Adding quality in the middle of the pitch was seen as a must for Michael Carrick and Tielemans and Santos have already begun making themselves at home. Baleba arrived from Brighton with an injury issue and is yet to make his debut.

‌



Mount is yet to make his first appearance of the season and was an unused substitute during the 2-2 draw at Everton last time out. He could yet feature in Thursday night's Champions League clash vs Sabah but where he fits in the pecking order, and what his role might be, is still to be determined.

Despite that the 27-year-old is glad to see new additions being made by the club, insisting they were need if the squad and the players wanted to go up a level.

In the pre-match programme, he said: “Yeah, I think the additions within the squad really improve the squad, too. The competition for places is high, and I think that's a must-have, because it ups the level, ups everyone's level within the team. Game by game, you're competing during the week and training to get into the team and start the game, so everyone's got to be ready.

“That definitely improves the standard. You can see it already, the standard in training has gone up, so that will only improve the squad as a whole.”

‌



View 2 Images Carlos Baleba was Man Utd's most expensive summer arrival (Image: Manchester United via Getty Images)

Mount's comments come despite an underwhelming three years at Old Trafford, which have been impacted by injures, a loss of form and a struggle to establish himself in a certain position. All that added up means he's made just 25 Premier League starts in three seasons. When he was a regular at Chelsea he would start more games than that in a single campaign .

He's scored just seven times for the Red Devils and, his recent decline, has seen him fall out of the England picture, where he was once a regular. During his peak Mount was effective centrally and out on the flanks, but at United the competition and recent recruitment drive has hampered him.

Article continues below

Bruno Fernandes remains the team's playmaker and the likes of Bryan Mbeumo and Matheus Cunha have been signed to offer a threat from out wide, although both have also played through the middle. Dropping deeper would see Mount compete with United's three summer signings and Kobbie Mainoo.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
