World.title: Dangote IPO could lift GDP to $600bn — Rewane
World.content:
—Refinery expansion to drive investment, exports, industrial output

By Obas Esiedesa, Abuja

ABUJA — The proposed N2.15 trillion Initial Public Offering, IPO, by Dangote Refinery could help increase Nigeria’s Gross Domestic Product, GDP, from about $278 billion to $600 billion by 2030, economist and Chief Executive Officer of Financial Derivatives Company, FDC, Mr Bismarck Rewane, has said.

Rewane, who spoke at the Abuja investor roadshow for the refinery’s IPO, said the investment could generate significant multiplier effects through increased industrial output, investment, consumer spending and exports.

He said the planned expansion of the refinery from its current 650,000–700,000 barrels per day capacity to 1.4 million barrels per day represented a major private-sector investment capable of significantly changing the structure of the Nigerian economy.

According to him, Nigeria’s GDP, estimated at $278 billion in 2025, could rise to about $600 billion following the investment, while consumer spending could increase from $166 billion to $240 billion and investment from $72 billion to $216 billion.

He added that higher net exports could strengthen the naira and further increase the value of economic output.

Rewane said Dangote Refinery currently accounted for an estimated 16.91 per cent of Nigeria’s GDP by valuation and about 45 per cent of the country’s stock market capitalisation.

He urged Nigerians to take advantage of the IPO and invest in an asset he described as capable of generating significant economic and industrial benefits.

“Start small, stay invested, reinvest in the gains, and build wealth,” he said, describing the refinery as an impact investment for Nigeria and Africa.

Earlier, Chairman of the event, Mr Oluwagbenga Oyebode, described the IPO as a landmark transaction for Nigeria’s capital market, saying it would significantly increase market capitalisation while introducing greater energy and downstream exposure to the Nigerian Exchange.

He said the offer comprised 4.1 billion ordinary shares at N525 per share, with expected net proceeds of about N2.1 trillion, representing 3.3 per cent of the company’s issued capital.

According to Oyebode, the proceeds would be deployed entirely as growth capital to finance the next phase of the refinery’s expansion, rather than for balance-sheet repair.

He described the transaction, approved by the Securities and Exchange Commission, SEC, as the first major public offering under the Investment and Securities Act, ISA, 2025.

Oyebode said the IPO could increase total market capitalisation from about N160 trillion to approximately N225 trillion, while deepening liquidity and broadening the sectoral composition of the Nigerian Exchange.

He said the offer was structured to attract retail investors, with a minimum subscription of 10 shares costing N5,250, in line with the promoters’ objective of making it an “IPO for the people.”

Oyebode said the promoters were targeting about 10 million retail investors, adding that the offer had also been assessed as Sharia-compliant, thereby widening the pool of potential investors.

Representing President of Dangote Group, Aliko Dangote, at the roadshow, Regional Adviser, Fatima Wali Abdulrahman, said the IPO was part of the group’s broader vision of accelerating Africa’s industrialisation.

Dangote said the group intended to raise N2.15 trillion, equivalent to about $1.6 billion, at N525 per share to fund the refinery’s expansion programme.

He said the minimum subscription had deliberately been set at 10 shares to encourage wider participation, stressing that the objective was for “every Nigerian to own a piece of this asset.”

According to him, the group was also planning investments in Ethiopia, Kenya, Tanzania and Namibia, while targeting listings in about six other African countries.

Dangote said Africans must take the lead in developing the continent’s economies, adding that the refinery and petrochemical complex would create opportunities for value creation across Africa.

Oyebode said the refinery’s expansion would not only increase fuel production but also strengthen Nigeria’s position in higher-value segments of the hydrocarbon value chain through petrochemicals, fertiliser, polymers and industrial feedstock.

Also speaking, Prof Uche Uwaleke of Nasarawa State University urged investors to buy and retain their shares as a long-term investment.

Uwaleke said the IPO prospectus provided for an additional share as a bonus for investors who held their shares for at least one year.

He called for greater participation by retail investors, particularly artisans, workers and small-business owners, stressing the need to take the investment opportunity to ordinary Nigerians.

World.title: NNPC to deploy 70 smart stations nationwide
World.content:
—Stations to offer self-service fuel, EV charging, LPG, CNG

By Obas Esiedesa, Abuja

ABUJA — The Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited, NNPC Ltd., has announced plans to deploy between 50 and 70 smart, self-service energy stations across the country within the next six months.

The company said the initiative was part of its strategy to transform conventional filling stations into modern energy and mobility hubs offering petrol, electric vehicle, EV, charging, liquefied petroleum gas, LPG, compressed natural gas, CNG, car wash and food services.

Speaking yesterday in Abuja at the commissioning of a technology-driven smart station, the Executive Vice President, Downstream, NNPC Ltd., Engr. Mumuni Dagazau, said the facility was the first of several smart stations planned nationwide.

According to him, the new model is designed to provide customers with greater convenience by integrating different energy sources and services in one location.

“We are hoping to roll out a significant number, probably about 50 to 70 of these types of stations within the next six months. So this is what you’ll be seeing going forward from NNPCL.

“This is the first of many smart stations that we are going to have around the country. What the whole concept is, we are trying to turn from a filling station to an energy hub,” he said.

Dagazau said the stations would integrate petrol, gas and electricity, while allowing customers to dispense fuel themselves, including at night.

He, however, dismissed concerns that the self-service model could lead to job losses, saying attendants and other personnel would remain available to assist customers and operate the technology-driven facilities.

“What NNPC does is create jobs. What this does is create jobs. You have an energy hub today. If you look at the average filling station and you look at the energy hub, you will find more people in the energy hub than you will find in the filling stations,” Dagazau said.

He added that the facilities would require personnel to manage automation, EV charging and other services.

On electric vehicle charging, Dagazau said the Abuja facility had fast chargers capable of charging an EV in about 30 to 40 minutes, depending on the vehicle and battery level.

He said NNPC was also targeting the modernisation of its existing stations as part of the broader transformation of NNPC Retail.

“We are going to modernise our stations. The customer deserves a better quality of service and we are delivering that quality of service,” he said.

Dagazau disclosed that additional smart stations were being planned for Abuja and Kano, with a significant number expected to be deployed across the country within six months.

The Executive Director, Retail Operations and Mobility, NNPC Ltd., Mr Shettima Baba-Kukawa, said the Abuja facility had a storage capacity of 180,000 litres for Premium Motor Spirit, PMS, and 45,000 litres for Automotive Gas Oil, AGO.

He said the station had 16 PMS pumps and two AGO pumps, while six EV charging points had been installed in partnership with African Motor Works.

According to him, the facility is fully powered by solar energy through a system with a capacity of more than 200 kilowatts.

Baba-Kukawa said the company was developing the facility as a lifestyle and mobility hub, with plans for a quick-service restaurant, coffee shop, automated car wash and modern service bay.

He added that LPG dispensing was being incorporated, while plans were underway to introduce CNG and a CNG conversion centre.

“The station is going to run 24 hours. And it is fully self-service. So for customers that want to trust themselves and dispense themselves, they can actually do that. Transactions are done on their phone app and concluded by dispensing the exact amount of fuel they purchased into their tanks,” he said.

Baba-Kukawa explained that customers using the self-service facility would need to download the NNPC Retail app, create and fund a wallet, and generate a code authorising them to dispense the quantity of fuel purchased.

He, however, said customers who were unable to operate the digital system would not be excluded, as staff would be available to assist them.

The Managing Director, NNPC Retail, Huub Stokman, said the transformation had become necessary as the downstream petroleum industry continued to evolve following deregulation and the commencement of operations at the Dangote Refinery.

Stokman said consumers increasingly wanted quality products, competitive prices, faster service and additional offerings at retail outlets.

He said customers were also demanding new energy solutions, including EV charging and CNG, as well as digital payment options and more sustainable operations.

“Above all, especially the younger generation, they want us to deliver it in a sustainable way, hence the fact that you also see that this station is completely solar-powered,” Stokman said.

He said NNPC Retail would continue to invest in technology, partnerships and new energy solutions to meet changing consumer expectations.

World.title: Oluremi Tinubu unveils food bank in Anambra
World.content:
AWKA — Nigeria’s First Lady, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, Thursday unveiled the National Community Food Bank Programme for the South-East geopolitical zone in Anambra State, as part of efforts to strengthen food security and social protection for vulnerable Nigerians.

Tinubu performed the unveiling at the old Governor’s Lodge, Amawbia, during her official visit to the state.

The South-East zonal food bank is designed to provide food assistance and nutrition education to vulnerable groups, including widows, elderly persons, persons with disabilities, nursing mothers and young children.

Speaking at the event, the First Lady said the initiative was a key component of the Renewed Hope Initiative, aimed at addressing hunger, promoting grassroots development and improving human capital outcomes in communities.

She said the programme would complement Federal Government policies focused on poverty reduction, sustainable agriculture and the strengthening of social safety nets.

According to her, the initiative also underscores the importance of collaboration between the Federal Government and state governments in addressing economic hardship and promoting inclusive development.

“This initiative reinforces the Federal Government’s policies aimed at tackling poverty, promoting sustainable agriculture, and strengthening social safety nets in Anambra State and the wider South-East region.

“It demonstrates a reinforced partnership between the Federal Government and the state governments of the region towards inclusive economic growth and societal welfare,” Tinubu said.

The First Lady was received at the event by Anambra State Governor, Prof. Chukwuma Soludo, and his wife, Dr Nonye Soludo.

As part of her engagements in the state, Tinubu also commissioned a state-of-the-art Information and Communications Technology, ICT, Centre at the Federal Polytechnic, Oko.

The centre is designed to equip young people with digital skills, including software development, data analysis and remote-work opportunities.

Tinubu said the initiative was part of broader efforts to expand opportunities for young Nigerians through technology and skills development.

She also said the programme would complement the Anambra State Government’s humanitarian initiatives through the distribution of empowerment grants, vocational tools and agricultural inputs to thousands of beneficiaries across the state’s 21 local government areas.

The ceremony was attended by government officials, traditional and community leaders, development stakeholders and other dignitaries.

World.title: 22-year-old Singaporean pleads guilty to $245m crypto heist
World.content:
By Adegboyega Adeleye

A 22-year-old Singaporean, Malone Lam, has pleaded guilty in the United States to his role in a cryptocurrency heist that saw him and his associates steal about $245 million in bitcoin.

Lam, who was accused of organising an international group of associates, admitted to a racketeering conspiracy charge after the group used deception and stolen personal information to gain access to victims’ cryptocurrency wallets.

According to the BBC, the US Department of Justice said Lam and his associates spent the proceeds lavishly, including up to $500,000 in a single night at nightclubs.

The group also bought more than 30 luxury vehicles, with individual cars valued between $100,000 and $3.8 million, while stolen funds were used to purchase high-end watches, designer clothing, private jet rentals, luxury homes and Hermes Birkin handbags.

The DOJ said the handbags, valued in the tens of thousands of dollars, were at times thrown into crowds during nightclub parties.

Lam, who also used the aliases “Anne Hathaway”, “$$$” and “King Greavy”, was described by US authorities as the ringleader who identified victims and coordinated the roles of other members of the criminal enterprise.

The conspirators, who came from several US states and outside the country, met through online gaming platforms, according to court documents.

They allegedly tricked victims into handing over confidential information and sometimes carried out home break-ins to obtain details that enabled them to drain cryptocurrency wallets.

Lam told US investigators that he dropped out of secondary school in Singapore at 14. He travelled to the US in October 2023 and remained there after his visa expired in January 2024.

The conspiracy began no later than October 2023 and continued until at least May 2025, according to court documents.

Lam and a co-conspirator were arrested in September 2024, bringing the operation to an end.

US Magistrate Judge Alicia Valle previously compared Lam’s lifestyle to “Ferris Bueller gone bad” during his first court appearance, citing his extravagant spending after gaining access to more than $230 million.

The US Department of Justice said Lam faces a maximum sentence of 20 years in prison. No sentencing date had been scheduled as of Tuesday.

Another member of the conspiracy, Evan Tangeman, was sentenced to 70 months in prison in April for laundering proceeds from the scheme.

World.title: British army explains how Nigerians, other foreigners can join military
World.content:
By Hannah Ogunlabi

If you are a foreigner interested in joining the British army, you will need to meet certain entry requirements before you can begin your application.

The Army considers your age, nationality, health and fitness, as well as your education and qualifications.

1. Check Your Basic Requirements

Start by checking whether you meet the Army’s basic entry requirements. You will be asked about your age, nationality, health and fitness.

Your education and qualifications will also be considered. However, you do not necessarily need formal qualifications to join the Army, as your educational background can also help determine which role is suitable for you.

2. Decide Whether You Want to Join as a Soldier or Officer

The British Army offers opportunities for both soldiers and officers. Before applying, decide which option is more suitable for you.

If you are unsure, you can use the Army’s entry options tool to help you understand which route may be right for you.

3. Find a Role That Suits You

The Army has a wide range of jobs available. You can explore the different roles through the Army’s Role Finder.

Look through the available positions and consider which one matches your interests, skills and qualifications.

4. Choose Between Full-Time and Part-Time Service

You can choose to join the Army as a full-time soldier or officer, or serve part-time as an Army Reservist.

If you choose the Army Reserve, you will serve part-time alongside full-time Regular Army soldiers.

5. Consider Specialist Roles

If you already have specialist skills, the Army Reserve offers opportunities to use them in military service.

For example, people with skills in areas such as medicine and engineering can take on specialist roles while serving as Reservists.

6. Submit an Online Application

Once you have decided on the type of service and role you want, the next step is to apply online.

The application is the starting point of the Army’s recruitment process. Make sure you provide the required information about yourself and your qualifications.

7. Complete the Recruitment Process

After submitting your application, you will be guided through the next stages by a recruiter or Candidate Support Manager.

They will help you understand the recruitment process and guide you through the required stages before you can join the Army.

The British Army says its strength comes from its people. If you join, you will become part of an organisation that aims to be competitive, adaptable and inclusive.

The Army also focuses on creating an environment where you can feel that you belong, develop your talents, maintain your health and make the most of available opportunities.

If you are considering joining the British Army, start by checking whether you meet the entry requirements and exploring the roles available to you. From there, you can submit an online application and begin the recruitment process.

World.title: Obi visit to Yelwata: Okorie condemns blockade
World.content:
Chekwas Okorie

By John Alechenu

ABUJA — National Chairman of Igbo Agenda Dialogue, IAD, Chief Chekwas Okorie, has condemned the reported blocking of Peter Obi from paying a humanitarian visit to Yelwata community in Benue State, describing the incident as “one provocation too many.”

Okorie said preventing Obi from visiting victims of the June attack in the community was dangerous and condemnable.

He spoke in Abuja, Wednesday, while recalling an open letter he wrote to President Bola Tinubu on March 12, 2026, titled, “Halt the Brewing Anarchy in Nigeria,” in which he warned against actions capable of heightening political tensions in the country.

According to him, subsequent events had reinforced the concerns raised in the letter.

Okorie cited the reported warning by Edo State Governor, Monday Okpebholo, against Obi visiting the state without his permission and the subsequent attack on a venue where Obi was scheduled to commission the ADC secretariat in Edo State.

He also referred to alleged threats by supporters of the President, including Sunday Igboho and MC Oluomo, warning Obi and former Vice President Atiku Abubakar against campaigning in the South-West.

The IAD chairman further cited a reported statement by Islamic cleric, Sani Yahaya Jingir, in Kano, in the presence of two serving governors, including Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf, that those opposed to a Muslim-Muslim ticket in 2027 should leave Nigeria.

Okorie also referenced Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, who he said had declared at a press conference that he had assigned himself the responsibility of causing political discomfort for Obi and Atiku.

He further alleged that more than 50 people were reportedly killed in election-related violence during the build-up to the recently concluded Osun State governorship election, alleging that there was no intervention or caution from the Presidency.

Okorie said: “Buoyed by the apparent but tacit nod of approval by the presidency, the tactics of intimidation and bullying of opposition politicians by those in power have assumed a frightening and dangerous dimension.”

He also alleged that some states had imposed what he described as excessive signage fees of more than N700,000 for a single billboard belonging to opposition candidates, a situation he said had contributed to the reduced visibility of opposition campaign materials in some cities.

Describing the reported blockade of Obi’s visit to Yelwata as “despicable and provocative,” Okorie said the silence of the Federal Government and National Assembly over the incident was unacceptable.

He urged Nigerians committed to peace and democracy to condemn what he described as a dangerous trend.

“All well-meaning Nigerians must rise in unison to condemn this explosive trend, which may turn our country into a killing field in the name of territorial control for the 2027 elections,” he added.

World.title: ‘I wouldn’t have married my wife Simi if she were SS’ – Adekunle Gold
World.content:
By Hannah Ogunlabi

Nigerian singer Adekunle has stressed the importance of genotype testing before marriage, saying couples should know their genotype and ensure they are compatible before having children.

Speaking during an interview, Adekunle said there is still a need for more awareness about sickle cell, adding that people should be properly informed about the condition before making decisions about marriage and having children.

Adekunle said that when he and his wife met, one of the first things they did was to check their genotypes to know whether they were compatible.

“When we met,the first thing we did was to know our genotype that we match,” Adekunle said.

When the interviewer asked how the genotype test is carried out, Adekunle explained that it is a simple test.

“Yes its easy test, you do it and then they tell you she’s AA and I’m AS. So you have to do that first,” he said.

Adekunle also spoke about the importance of considering the possible risks of having children when couples have genotypes that could increase the chances of sickle cell disease.

He said people with sickle cell should not allow the condition to prevent them from achieving their goals, but added that couples should make informed decisions before having children.

“We tell people, if you have sickle cell, forget love, you can’t do it, it makes no sense,” he said.

Adekunle explained that having a child who could be sickly could create difficult circumstances for the family.

“Because you’re about to bring a child into the world and about to be sickly, what is the point?” he said.

When the interviewer asked how he would have handled the situation if his wife had sickle cell, Adekunle replied, “There’s no way I would have done that.”

Vanguard News

World.title: Nigeria Cuts AfCFTA Export Certificate to 24 Hours As Trade with Africa Grows
World.content:
Kuni Tyessi, Abuja

The Federal Government has reduced the processing time for African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) Certificates of Origin to 24 hours, down from over five days, in a bid to boost intra-African trade and ease business for Nigerian exporters.

The Minister of Industry, Trade and Investment, Dr. Jumoke Oduwole, disclosed this on Thursday in Abuja at the 2026 Third Quarter meeting of the AfCFTA Central Coordination Committee.

The minister, who said Nigerian goods remain competitive and are in high demand across the continent, cited the recent Nigeria-Botswana AfCFTA Trade Mission where CSO Fashion Academy secured an immediate order to supply 6,000 T-shirts to a Botswana business.

“A lot of Nigerians have the perception that Nigerian goods are not competitive on this continent. Nigerian entrepreneurs have shown that they can compete anywhere in the world, and are doing particularly well in the rest of Africa,” Oduwole said.

She noted that the country’s non-oil exports have grown exponentially due to increased trade across Africa.

According to her, a survey of 13 eastern and southern African countries showed high demand for shea butter, zobo drink, plantain chips, prepacked jollof rice, female apparel and wigs.

To facilitate exports, the minister said Nigeria opened an air cargo corridor with Uganda Air last year and added another airline this year.

Meanwhile, the National Coordinator of the Nigeria AfCFTA Coordination Office, Mrs. Patience Okala, said the reduction in certificate processing time was achieved through the digitisation and automation of registration, verification and certification by the Nigeria Customs Service (NCS).

Okala added that Nigeria has resolved eight reported cases of Non-Tariff Barriers affecting businesses trading under AfCFTA between Q2 and Q3.

She disclosed that the AfCFTA Secretariat has formally requested Nigeria to lead a peer-learning session on implementation for other African countries during upcoming institutional meetings in Zimbabwe.

The NACO boss also announced that five Nigerian businesses have applied for the $10 million AfCFTA Adjustment Fund established with Afreximbank, with one female-led business progressing to the next stage.

She congratulated Dr. Oduwole on her election as Chairperson of the Bureau of the AfCFTA Council of Ministers, noting that the position places Nigeria in charge of all AfCFTA institutional committees.

Okala listed other Q3 achievements to include the hosting of AfCFTA Week, the HerAfCFTA event for women-owned businesses, the 18th Council of Ministers meeting in Abuja, and the AfCFTA Digital Trade Forum in Lagos.

She said the government has also launched the Africa Digital Access and Public Infrastructure for Trade, ADAPT initiative to support implementation of the Digital Trade Protocol.

Looking ahead to Q4, Okala said NACO will prioritise simplifying the AfCFTA framework, intensifying sub-national engagements, and developing more business-friendly tools.

“Ultimately, we need to see more Nigerian businesses trading under AfCFTA, more Nigerian products entering African markets and stronger participation of Nigerian businesses in continental trade,” she said.

World.title: Mbah Presents Report Card to Justify Quest for Mandate Renewal in 2027
World.content:
* Records over 10,000 milestone achievements as proof Enugu is on course to greatness

Emmanuel Ugwu-Nwogo in Enugu

With 39 months of his four-year tenure already spent, Enugu State Governor, Mr. Peter Mbah, has presented his report card of achievements to back his quest to have his mandate renewed by Enugu people in 2027.

He listed over “10,000 milestone achievements” as proof that he deserves a second term in office on completion of his first term next year, insisting that through his purposeful governance, Enugu is on course for greatness.

Mbah’s accomplishments compiled in a compendium entitled ‘A Thousand and One Reasons Why Dr. Peter Ndubuisi Mbah Should be Re-elected as Governor of Enugu State,’ was presented to the public at the International Conference Centre, Enugu.

His listed achievements included physical infrastructures, innovative programmes and policies implemented across various sectors of the state to engender the ‘Quantum Leap’ that placed Enugu as the fastest improving state in Nigeria.

This was affirmed by Phillips Consulting in its recently released State Performance Momentum Index, in which Enugu outperformed 32 other states across the country in governance and development.

The 222-page compendium of recorded milestones shows that the Mbah administration has so far constructed or reconstructed over 1,521 kilometres of roads, built over 7,000 classrooms and 260 Type-2 Primary Healthcare Centres.

It also recorded that Mbah established an airline, Enugu Air, for the state, revamped several moribund assets, and is presently engaged in building the New Enugu Smart City, among other achievements.

Represented by the Deputy Governor, Ifeanyi Ossai, Mbah said that the compendium was a proof of the diligent implementation of the Citizens Charter, also known as Executive Order 001, which was executed immediately he was sworn into office on May 29, 2023.

It was meant to be the binding force of his administration’s commitment to accountability, traceability and transparency.

However, the Enugu governor noted that though the compendium highlighted his administration’s philosophy of disruptive innovation and its focus on large-scale infrastructure, it did not include all that had been accomplished up to the day of unveiling.

He said: “It is important to note that the (unveiled) document does not entirely capture everything this government has done because, given the time it took to prepare this document, there was a cut-off point running months behind.”

Mbah stressed that the compendium “does not in any particular material represent the actual successful modest achievements of this government as at 9th of September 2026”, adding that it represents a tip of the iceberg.

“Our assignment today,” he stated, “is not just to unveil the Citizens Charter via the compendium. It is a lot more than that. It is a conversation on the sacrosanct duty and responsibility you gave to us to midwife and preside over your resources.

He acknowledged that the achievements recorded by his administration were made possible through collective efforts of those who believed in his vision and worked for his election in 2023.

Mbah also admitted that some policy decisions of his government may have caused consequential discomfort and social and economic dislocations for some people.

He, therefore, urged those affected in any way by the tough decisions his administration had to make for the transformation of the state, to bear with his government and show understanding as everything was done for the overall good of Enugu.

“What you must take home with you is that our intentions are noble. What we try to do is to put Enugu on irreversible path of greatness. What we try to do is to ensure that Enugu will not compete with Nigeria but within Nigeria,” Mbah said.

The governor assured Ndi Enugu that the Coal City State was on its way to greatness of emerging as a $30 billion economy and the preferred destination for investment, business, tourism and living.

Alluding to political defections that followed his change of party, Mbah expressed gratitude to “all those who made sacrifices, who lost their friends because they felt supporting us was the right thing to do. I want to thank all those who invested their resources”.

“I want to thank all those who took pains in very unimaginable circumstances to ensure that Enugu moves to the next level,” he added.

The Secretary to Enugu State Government, Prof. Chidiebere Onyia, had in his welcome address, said that the state was pursuing an extensive urban development agenda, including the New Enugu Smart City, environmental sustainability and urban renewal.

He noted that the state’s fiscal architecture had undergone significant reform through revenue automation, reforms at the Enugu State Internal Revenue Service, improved financial management, the Treasury Single Account, enterprise resource planning and broader institutional restructuring.

According to him, the administration has also sustained its investments in youth empowerment, women development, technology, skills acquisition, social protection, tourism, environmental sustainability and community development.

He stated that the ultimate goal of the Mbah administration was to improve the lives of the people.

“Behind every project is a community; behind every policy is a citizen; and behind every statistic is a human being whose life government seeks to improve,” he said.

Onyia also stressed the importance of institutional reforms in sustaining government programmes, adding that: “Sustainable development requires not only projects that citizens can see, but institutions and systems that can sustain those projects.”

Mbah’s achievements received avalanche of commendations from people that attended the event, including political leaders, traditional, and religious leaders, captains of industry, professionals, public servants and other stakeholders.

The Deputy National Chairman (South) of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Dr. Ben Nwoye, commended the administration for its development record and the scale of projects executed across the state.

The Speaker of the Enugu State House of Assembly, Hon. Uchenna Ugwu, commended the governor for his developmental strides, pledging the continued support of the legislative arm of the state government.

On his part, the Chairman of the Enugu State Council of Traditional Rulers, Igwe Samuel Asadu, equally spoke glowingly about the administration’s performance, saying a performing government should be supported to continue till 2031.

“We have never had it so good. It is not about party. But let us give the job to those who understand the job. The governor wants to move the Enugu State economy to a $30bn economy and that is exactly what he is doing,” he stated.

World.title: NECO Constructs, Donates Palace to Host Community in Niger
World.content:
Laleye Dipo in Minna

In line with its social responsibility policy, the National Examination Council (NECO) has built an ultra modern palace for the traditional ruler of Gidan-mangoro in Bosso Local Government Area of Niger State.

Speaking at the inauguration and presentation of the palace on Thursday, the Registrar and Chief Executive Officer of NECO, Prof. Danlami Ibrahim Wushsihi, defended the construction of the edifice, saying the community has continued to provide peaceful environment for the organisation to operate.

“By supporting the construction of this palace, NECO affirms that tradition matters and development must respect cultural foundations,” Wushsihi declared.

“When leadership structures are strengthened, communities become better positioned to address challenges and achieve growth

“As a council, we understand that strong education systems thrive where communities are stable, peaceful and well coordinated” he said.

Prof. Wushsihi added that as hosts of the headquarters of the council, the Gidan Mangoro community has also continued to demonstrate a spirit of hospitality, understanding and peace, adding that the peaceful coexistence enjoyed by NECO and the host communities throughout the years is a testament to the goodwill that exists between the council and the people.

The registrar therefore explained that the inaugurated palace symbolizes unity, cultural heritage and the enduring role of traditional institutions in strengthening social cohesion and also serves as a centre for leadership, counsel, reconciliation and community organization .

In appreciation of NECO’s gesture, the Gidan Mangoro community bestowed the registrar with the Maji Dadin Gidan Mangoro title.

The ceremony witnessed traditional dancing and cultural displays.

World.title: FRSC Launches National Movement to End Overloading, Adopt Abuja Declaration 2026
World.content:
Kasim Sumaina in Abuja

The Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC) Thursday launched the National Movement for Safe Loading and Safe Road Use at the National Breakfast Policy Dialogue in Abuja, with a call for shared responsibility across the transportation value chain to end unsafe loading practices.

The event, convened in partnership with Business Day Media Limited, brought together government agencies, transport operators, cargo owners, regulators, civil society, and the media with the theme: ‘Ending Overloading, Saving Lives: A National Commitment to Safer Roads and Responsible Transportation in Nigeria.’

The Corp Marshal, FRSC, Shehu Mohammed, noted that overloading is not just a traffic violation but a road safety, infrastructure, logistics and economic development issue.

Mohammed explained that excessive loads compromise braking, steering, and vehicle stability, adding that it accelerates vehicle deterioration, increases crash rates, and contributes to the premature deterioration of Nigeria’s road infrastructure.

According to him, the danger also lies in mixed and improper loading, including the combination of passengers and cargo, incompatible or dangerous materials, and poorly distributed loads which put drivers, passengers and other road users at risk.

He added that: “A vehicle must carry only what it is designed, licensed, and safely configured to carry. No reduction in transportation costs or commercial benefit is worth the loss of human lives.”

Mohammed maintained that Nigeria’s economy depends on the safe movement of agricultural produce, raw materials, manufactured goods, fuel and other commodities, add that a safe transport system is the foundation for prosperity.

“When overloading damages our roads, government bears the cost. When it damages vehicles, operators bear the cost. When it delays the movement of goods, businesses and consumers bear the cost. But when it causes a fatal crash, a Nigerian family bears the cost that money can never replace,” he said.

He stressed that enforcement alone cannot end the problem.

“Responsibility must be shared by cargo owners, shippers, loading agents, transporters, fleet operators, drivers, regulators and government.”

He urged cargo owners to accurately declare weights, operators to maintain vehicles and comply with limits and drivers to refuse unsafe or poorly secured loads.

Regulators, he said, must strengthen weigh infrastructure, data sharing and coordination.

The corps marshal added that FRSC will intensify enforcement, public education, intelligence-led operations and the use of technology to drive compliance, shifting from reactive enforcement to proactive and preventive road safety.

On the adoption and signing of the Abuja Declaration 2026, he said the declaration must go beyond ceremony to become a national compact with clear responsibilities, measurable commitments, timelines and monitoring mechanisms.

“Our assessment will not be measured by the quality of our speeches or the number of signatures. It will be measured by what changes on our roads. Are fewer vehicles overloaded? Are cargo weights properly declared? Are crashes and fatalities reducing?” the official asked.

He called on all stakeholders to ensure the National Movement for Safe Loading and Safe Roads becomes a movement of action, stating: “Our roads must carry Nigeria’s goods. They must carry our people. They must carry our economic aspirations. But they must not carry avoidable deaths.”

He however thanked participants and stakeholders even as he expressed hope that the dialogue would mark a decisive turning point for safer roads and a stronger Nigeria.

Speaking in similar vein, Director General/Chief Executive Officer, Voice of Nigeria (VON), Jibrin Baba Ndace, urged drivers, transport unions and regulators to treat passenger safety as non-negotiable and to ensure vehicles are not overloaded or poorly maintained.

Ndace, who doubles as the keynote speaker, recounted two near-fatal road accidents in Kaduna and Kano States, using his experience to call on drivers to listen to passengers and prioritize safety over speed.

He narrated how a vehicle he was travelling in developed a fault near a NYSC camp in Kaduna shortly after dusk.

“The driver saw a tire on the road. It was almost getting dark and he applied the brakes and the vehicle somersaulted. The vehicle turned to its side. The driver was down. I was in the front. I was up. The glass was broken, but we were all lucky to survive,” he said.

He said he escaped through the broken windscreen and helped other passengers, mostly women, out of the wreckage before assisting the driver last.

“The lesson there is that sometimes drivers don’t listen to passengers even when you caution them,” he noted.

World.title: UN Investment Forum Organisers Move Leadership Summit to November to Secure Participation of Key Speakers, Partners
World.content:
Sunday Aborisade in Abuja

The 2026 INT International STEP Delegate Leadership Summit earlier scheduled for October 26 to 30 in Abuja has been rescheduled for November 2 to 6 to avoid a clash with the World Investment Forum convened by the United Nations Trade and Development (UNCTAD).

The organisers said the one-week adjustment became necessary because a significant number of speakers, facilitators, resource persons and institutional partners expected at the summit are also scheduled to participate in the World Investment Forum.

The summit is being organised by the Institute for National Transformation International (INT International) and will take place at the Shehu Musa Yar’Adua Centre, Abuja.

In a statement signed by the Director General and Convener of INT International, Prof. Vincent C. Anigbogu, and the Director of Sponsorship and Marketing, Mr. Anthony Bugembe, the organisers said retaining the original date could have affected the participation of key contributors.

They said the decision was taken after it became clear that the overlapping engagements would make it difficult for some of the expected participants to attend the Abuja summit.

“The STEP Delegate Summit is a working summit, not a ceremonial gathering. Its outcomes depend directly on the quality of the experts, mentors and institutions in the room,” the organisers said.

They expressed regret over the change, particularly to international stakeholders, invited guests and delegates who had already made arrangements around the original October dates.

The organisers, however, said the change affected only the dates, adding that other aspects of the summit would remain unchanged.

The five-day meeting is expected to include plenary sessions, clinics and project development sessions, after which participants will undergo a 10-month mentorship programme.

The mentorship programme is intended to support participants in developing projects from the idea stage towards funding and implementation.

The organisers said the summit would focus on translating major continental, international and national development frameworks into specific programmes and projects.

Among the frameworks to be considered are the African Union’s Agenda 2063, the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), the African Development Bank’s High 5s and national development plans.

The summit is also expected to focus on science, technology and innovation-driven projects and their potential for development financing and implementation.

The organisers said the decision to move the summit was intended to avoid a situation in which competing international engagements would reduce the participation of experts and institutions considered important to the programme.

The World Investment Forum, which is convened by UNCTAD, brings together governments, investors and other stakeholders to discuss investment and development issues.

With the revised dates, the INT International summit will now hold from Monday, November 2, to Friday, November 6, at the Shehu Musa Yar’Adua Centre in Abuja.

World.title: NEMA Announces 30 Winners of 2026 National Essay Competition
World.content:
* Pledges stronger disaster awareness culture

Kuni Tyessi in Abuja

The National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA) has announced winners of its 2026 National Essay Competition, recognising 30 students and corps members for essays on disaster risk reduction, climate change and technology in emergency response.

The Director General of NEMA, Mrs. Zubaida Umar, unveiled the winners on Thursday at the agency’s headquarters in Abuja during the recognition ceremony.

Umar, who was represented by the director in charge of Internal Audit, Aliyu Waziri, said the competition was organised as part of NEMA’s commitment to strengthening disaster awareness, emergency preparedness and resilience among young Nigerians.

She noted that the agency received an exceptional volume of entries nationwide, which extended the assessment period.



“We considered it important that speed should not take precedence over credibility. Every eligible entry passed through a painstaking assessment, validation and corroboration process designed to ensure fairness, transparency and merit,” she said.

The DG congratulated all winners and participants, stating that: “Every young person who researched Disaster Risk Reduction has become better equipped to contribute to a safer and more resilient Nigeria.

“Emergency management must increasingly become a culture rather than an activity undertaken only when disaster strikes. Through these young voices, we see encouraging evidence that a new generation of disaster-conscious Nigerians is emerging.”

In his speech, the Consultant of the initiative, Hakeem Bello, said the competition was conceived to strengthen emergency preparedness, disaster awareness and resilience among young Nigerians.

He noted that the agency received a remarkable number of entries, which made the assessment process painstaking and methodical.

Bello commended the Internal Assessment Panel, Oversight Committee, and External Lead Assessor for ensuring credibility and transparency in the screening and ranking of submissions.

According to him, the three essay topics reflected NEMA’s mandate.

Secondary school students wrote on ‘My Role in Disaster Risk Reduction’, tertiary students on ‘Climate Change and Disaster Management in Nigeria’, while the NYSC Emergency Management Vanguards examined ‘Technology for Disaster Response: Opportunities and Challenges’.

Bello congratulated winners who received cash prizes, plaques and certificates, and applauded all finalists and participants.

“The ultimate value of this competition is not merely in identifying winners, but in building a generation that understands that disaster management begins before disaster strikes with awareness, prevention, preparedness and shared responsibility,” he said.

World.title: Katsina Approves N500m to Tackle Acute Malnutrition
World.content:
Francis Sardauna in Katsina

The Katsina State Government has approved N500 million as counterpart funding for the procurement of nutrition commodities to strengthen the fight against acute malnutrition among children across the state.

The approval was granted by the State Executive Council at its 15th Regular Meeting, chaired by Governor Dikko Umaru Radda on Wednesday at the General Muhammadu Buhari House, Katsina.

The Commissioner for Health, Musa Adamu, said the funding would sustain the provision of essential nutrition commodities for children suffering from acute malnutrition and further strengthen the state’s response to the condition.

The commissioner said the intervention was part of the Radda administration’s unflinching efforts to improve healthcare delivery and address critical needs affecting vulnerable residents, particularly children.

Also speaking, the Commissioner for Information and Culture, Dr Salisu Bala Zango, said the counci also approved the procurement of 95,000 bags of assorted grains for distribution to less privileged and vulnerable residents across the state.

He said the grain distribution is aimed at cushioning the effects of the current economic hardship and providing direct assistance to households in need.

He added that the council approved the procurement and distribution of non-food items and cash support to vulnerable groups, including orphans, widows, persons with special needs and other less privileged members of the society.

On his part, the Special Adviser on Market Development, Mustapha Bala Batsari, said the council approved the modernisation of Dandume, Daura, Mashi and Jibia markets.

He explained that the modernisation of the markets selected across the three senatorial zones of the state would improve commercial infrastructure and strengthen the socio-economic wellbeing of residents.

World.title: Foundation Hosts Do What U Love Festival
World.content:
Street Project Foundation (SPF) has announced the return of its flagship creative platform, the Do What U Love (DWUL) Festival, for its seventh edition. Taking place on

Friday, 11th September 2026 in Lagos, DWUL Festival 7.0 will bring together hundreds of young creatives, entrepreneurs, and industry stakeholders for a single day dedicated to the business and craft of creativity.

This year’s theme, “The Creator’s Market,” reflects the festival’s continued commitment to positioning creativity as a viable and sustainable economic pathway for young Nigerians. The event will feature a packed programme including a creative pitch competition, a poetry slam, masterclasses, a panel discussion, live performances, a film screening, and the presentation of the Wole Oguntokun Legacy Award, alongside games and networking opportunities.

Ahead of the main event, SPF opened three calls for entries to identify standout talent for the Festival stage: the “Mic Check” Poetry Slam, offering a N100,000 prize for original spoken-word performance; “Pitch It,” a creative pitch competition for entrepreneurs and innovators aged 18–35 years

with N400,000 in prize money on the line; and an open call for performers inviting musicians, dancers, spoken-word artists, and filmmakers to apply to perform. Selected applicants across all

three categories are currently being contacted directly ahead of the event.

Commenting, Founder of FSP, Rita Ezenwa Okoro, said: “Every year, Do What U Love reminds us that creativity is not a hobby, it is an economy. This year’s theme is about giving young Nigerians the tools, the stage, and the recognition to build real, sustainable careers from what they love to do.”

The festival will also honour the legacy of the late Wole Oguntokun through the presentation of the

Wole Oguntokun Legacy Award (WOLA), recognising young Nigerians aged 18–35 years who are using

theatre, storytelling, and social advocacy to drive change in their communities. Last year’s inaugural recipient, Ayodeji Ajadi, was celebrated with a cash prize of N500,000 for his contributions to storytelling and advocacy.

World.title: The ultimate VISA-FREE bucket list for South Africans in 2026
World.content:
South African passport holders can travel visa-free to 101 destinations in 2026: Image Pexels

South African passport holders can currently travel to 101 destinations without needing to apply for a visa before departure, according to the 2026 Henley Passport Index.

That places the “Green Mamba,” as it’s affectionately known, at 48th globally, sitting between Qatar and Belize.

Of those 101 destinations, 53 are fully visa-free, 28 offer visa on arrival, and 20 can be accessed through an eVisa or ETA system.



how the number has shifted this year

South Africa’s access has actually narrowed slightly through 2026.

The country lost visa-free or visa-on-arrival access to five destinations compared to the previous year:

Mauritania

Nigeria

Pakistan

Kosovo

Somalia

That brought the total down from 106 to 101.

Despite the drop, South Africa’s overall global ranking held steady at 48th, and it remains the fourth-strongest passport in Africa, behind:

Seychelles — 25th globally, 156 destinations Mauritius — 29th globally, 148 destinations Botswana — 59th globally, 87 destinations South Africa — 48th globally, 101 destinations

It’s worth noting the index is updated continuously throughout the year as visa policies shift, so these figures can move again before 2027’s rankings are released.

where South Africans can go easiest right now

Neighbouring and regional African destinations:



Botswana

Namibia

Zimbabwe

Zambia

Mozambique

Lesotho

eSwatini

Mauritius

Tanzania

Egypt

Middle East:

Israel

Jordan

Oman

Qatar

Europe (the exceptions):

Georgia

Russia

A full Schengen visa is still required for the UK, Ireland and most of the rest of the continent, making Europe by far the toughest region for South African passport holders to access easily.

I’ve always found it worth double-checking these lists before booking anything, visa rules can shift with surprisingly little warning.

As an avid solo traveller myself, visa-free destinations always make my bucket list first.

Knowing this genuinely opens up the world, and makes travel feel a little more accessible, especially when our Green Mamba sometimes feels like the odds are against us.

Still, it’s good to know there are plenty of places we can go without the extra hassle.

Has a sudden visa rule change ever caught you off guard while planning a trip?

Let us know in the comments below…

World.title: Shoppers are spending nearly R1 billion a month at this famous hotspot in SA
World.content:
The V&A Waterfront had another strong year, with millions of visitors and billions of rand spent at its retailers. Image: canva

The V&A Waterfront continues to attract huge numbers of shoppers and tourists, with new figures revealing that retailers at the Cape Town destination generated R11.3 billion in sales over the past financial year.

Growthpoint Properties, which owns a 50% interest in the V&A Waterfront, released its latest full-year results this week, showing that retail sales at the precinct increased by 6.2% in FY2026.

Put into monthly terms, the annual figure works out to an average of approximately R942 million in retail sales every month.



That is not money going directly into the V&A Waterfront’s bank account, but rather the total value of sales generated by retailers operating at the precinct.

Millions of visitors for V&A Waterfont

The huge retail turnover comes as the V&A Waterfront continues to attract millions of visitors.

According to Growthpoint, the precinct recorded 27 million visits during FY2026, an increase of 7% compared with the previous year.

Growthpoint attributed the stronger footfall partly to increased domestic and international tourism, with international arrivals at Cape Town International Airport increasing by 8%.

The Waterfront also continues to have extremely low vacancies, with only 0.9% of the precinct vacant.

The strong retail performance also comes as the Waterfront expands its luxury offering.



The new 3 752m² Lux Mall at Victoria Wharf has been completed, with major international brands including Burberry, Louis Vuitton, Gucci, Zegna, Versace and Rolex already trading.

The remaining tenants are expected to open by the end of October 2026.

Growthpoint said trading densities at the V&A were well ahead of the Morgan Stanley Capital International (MSCI) benchmark for super-regional shopping centres.

The V&A Waterfront is still expanding

The development story is also far from over.

The City of Cape Town Municipal Planning Tribunal has approved an increase of 440 000m² in development rights at the V&A Waterfront.

The first phase allows for 200 000m² of mixed-use development, including at least 110 000m² of residential space, as well as hotels, offices and retail.

At least 10% of the residential component must be affordable housing.

A second phase could add another 240 000m², subject to a traffic impact assessment, with at least half of that phase required to be residential.

The Waterfront is also progressing with a number of other developments, including 160 new built-to-rent apartments scheduled to open in March 2027 and the 142-room Cape Town EDITION Hotel by Marriott, which is expected to open in October 2026.

Another big year expected

Growthpoint expects the V&A Waterfront’s operating profit to grow by double digits in FY2027.

The precinct’s performance is therefore becoming an increasingly important part of Growthpoint’s overall business.

The company’s 50% interest in the V&A Waterfront accounts for approximately 12.1% of Growthpoint’s total asset book value and 18.6% of its distributable income per share contribution.

World.title: Sad news as Fish River Canoe Marathon cancelled
World.content:
The Fish River Canoe Marathon organising committee has cancelled the 2026 event due to the ongoing Foot and Mouth Disease in the Eastern Cape. Image: Facebook @FishMarathon

The Fish River Canoe Marathon organising committee has taken the difficult decision to cancel the 2026 event scheduled to take place on 2 to 3 October due to the ongoing Foot and Mouth Disease (FMD) in the Eastern Cape.

The decision was made jointly by the Fish River Canoe Marathon Race Committee in consultation with members of the local community, the Fish River Farmers Association and the local farming community, taking into consideration the potential impact of the event to the area at this time.

Responsible course of action

While this is an extremely disappointing decision, the organisers believe it is the responsible course of action given the circumstances.



Importantly, the decision has been taken as early as possible, in order to give paddlers, teams, supporters, accommodation providers and other affected parties as much notice as possible to make alternative arrangements.

“We know how much the Fish means to the paddlers, and know this will be disruptive to those who have already entered, and to those who were planning to make the trip to Cradock,” said a spokesperson for the race committee.

“Cancelling an event that people have trained for, planned around and looked forward to is incredibly difficult, and we are genuinely sorry for the disappointment this will cause. At the same time, we have a responsibility to listen to the concerns of the local farming community and to ensure that the event does not add unnecessary pressure or risk while the FMD situation remains a concern.”

Full refund

The organisers are particularly conscious of the disappointment this decision will cause to those who have already entered the race, as well as to paddlers who may have been finalising their plans or preparing to enter.

All entrants will receive a refund directly from Paddlesport South Africa entry portal and the race organisers will assist if there are any issues with the refunds.

The organisers would like to thank the paddling community for its understanding and patience, and particularly the local community for its openness and input during the decision-making process.



The Fish River Canoe Marathon remains committed to returning and staging the 2027 event.

World.title: South Africa’s tides are about to change – and the moon is to blame
World.content:
South Africans heading to the coast this weekend should expect noticeably stronger tides. Image: canva

The new moon is often celebrated as the best time for stargazing, thanks to its darker skies.

But while the moon may seem to disappear from view, its influence on Earth is anything but gone.

In fact, the new moon can have a particularly noticeable effect on the ocean, helping create higher high tides and lower low tides along South Africa’s coastline.



And with the new moon occurring this Friday, 11 September, beachgoers, anglers and coastal explorers could see some of the more dramatic tidal differences of the month over the coming days.

Why does the new moon affect the tides?

The moon’s gravitational pull is one of the biggest forces behind Earth’s tides.

During most of the month, the gravitational effects of the moon and sun don’t line up perfectly. But during a new moon, the Sun, moon and Earth are positioned more closely in alignment.

This means the gravitational pull of the sun and moon works together, producing what are known as spring tides.

Despite the name, spring tides have nothing to do with the season.

Instead, they refer to tides that have a greater range, meaning high tides can be higher and low tides can be lower than usual.



The same thing happens during a full moon.

What does that mean for South Africa’s coast?

The difference can be particularly useful for people planning a day around the ocean.

Lower low tides can expose more of the shoreline, tidal pools and rocky areas, while higher high tides can bring the water significantly further up beaches and coastal areas.

That means anyone planning to go fishing, explore rock pools or spend time near the water should pay close attention to local tide times.

It is also worth remembering that tides are only one part of the coastal picture. Weather, wind and wave conditions can make the sea more dangerous, particularly around high tide.

World.title: What is La Niña – and what does it mean for South Africans?
World.content:
La Niña brought two years of favourable rainfall to South Africa before ending in early 2026: Image Pexels

If South Africa’s summer rains have felt unusually generous over the past couple of years, there’s a reason for that.

A specific climate pattern called La Niña has been quietly shaping the country’s weather, and according to the latest forecasts, it’s now come to an end.

La Niña is a natural climate pattern caused by cooling sea-surface temperatures in the tropical eastern Pacific Ocean.



It’s the direct opposite of El Niño.

It typically brings above-average rainfall to Southern Africa.

what’s actually happening right now

According to the World Meteorological Organization, ENSO-neutral conditions generally prevailed from mid-2024 through to late 2025.



Along the way, there was a brief dip into weak La Niña conditions during late 2024 and early 2025.

A fresh La Niña then developed in late 2025 and lasted until early 2026.

By May 2026, the WMO’s Global Seasonal Climate Update signalled a clear shift in the equatorial Pacific, with sea surface temperatures rising rapidly and pointing toward a likely return of El Niño conditions.



That transition has since been confirmed.

Forecasters at SAWS, the Australian Bureau of Meteorology, and the International Research Institute for Climate and Society all agree.

The country is now moving into an El Niño phase for late 2026 through 2027.



That means La Niña’s run has officially ended.

why this actually mattered for South Africa

This particular La Niña was relatively weak, but it still delivered real, tangible benefits.

South African maize farmers reaped a bumper crop largely thanks to the rains it unleashed.



The 2025-26 season’s summer grains and oilseeds production is estimated at 20.3 million tonnes, only slightly down from the 2024-25 season, itself the second-largest on record.

Excellent harvests across various fruits and vegetables followed too, supported by two consecutive years of La Niña-induced rain.

There’s a genuine silver lining buried in this shift, though.



Agricultural economist Wandile Sihlobo has noted that the favourable conditions from the preceding La Niña years could help soften the impact of the coming El Niño.

The extended rains improved dam water levels, the overall water table, and grazing veld conditions across much of the country.

That gives South Africa a real buffer heading into what forecasters expect to be a considerably drier season ahead.



so, what’s actually the difference between the two?

El Niño and La Niña are essentially mirror images of each other.

Both are part of a natural, irregular cycle called ENSO (El Niño-Southern Oscillation) that plays out in the equatorial Pacific.

El Niño means warmer-than-average Pacific waters, typically bringing hotter, drier conditions to Southern Africa.



La Niña means the opposite, cooler Pacific waters, and typically wetter conditions for the same region.

It’s a genuinely elegant, if slightly unsettling, system once you see it laid out like this: two opposite phases of the very same ocean, taking turns reshaping weather patterns across an entire hemisphere, whether we notice it happening or not.

Did you notice the wetter summers over the past two years, even without knowing why?

Let us know in the comments below…

World.title: Can Zim learners write matric without a South African ID? Department explains
World.content:
Zimbabwean learners preparing to write their South African matric examinations do not necessarily need a South African identity document to enter the National Senior Certificate (NSC) examinations.

The Department of Basic Education has clarified that affected Zimbabwean Grade 12 learners can use other forms of identification, with an affidavit also available for those who do not have identity documents.

The clarification comes as Zimbabwean learners who left South Africa following the 30 June immigration deadline prepare to return to the country for their 2026 matric examinations.



Zimbabwean matric learners can use other identification

Speaking to CapeTalk, Department of Basic Education spokesperson Lukhanyo Vangqa said learners do not have to produce a South African ID specifically to write the NSC examinations.

“They would need to have some form of identification. It doesn’t have to be South African,” Vangqa said.

He explained that learners who do not have identification documents can obtain an affidavit from a police station.

This means the absence of a South African identity document does not automatically prevent a Zimbabwean learner from entering the examination room.

What if a matric learner has no identification?

Vangqa said the department’s identification requirements are intended to ensure that the correct learner writes the examination and to prevent examination fraud.

He added that teachers could also assist in confirming the identity of learners who had been attending a school for more than a year.



“If they don’t have this identification then they need to have an affidavit,” Vangqa said, adding that the same approach can apply to South African learners who do not have identity documents for various reasons.

The department therefore does not treat identification as a mechanism for automatically excluding a learner from the examination.

Instead, it is used to positively identify candidates and prevent another person from writing an examination on their behalf.

Zimbabwean matric learners must write exams in SA

The clarification comes as affected Zimbabwean Grade 12 learners prepare to return to South Africa ahead of the October NSC examinations.

Vangqa said there is no provision for the learners to write the South African matric examinations from Zimbabwe.

He explained that the NSC examinations are governed by the South African Schools Act, which applies within South Africa’s borders.

Learners therefore need to be physically present in South Africa to write their examinations.

Exams must be written at accredited centres

Another important requirement is the examination centre where the learners will write.

Vangqa said the centre must be accredited by Umalusi to administer NSC examinations.

This means affected Zimbabwean learners cannot simply choose any school or venue in South Africa to write their final examinations.

The requirement comes as the Zimbabwe Exemption Permit Coordinating Committee (ZEPCC) Academy works to facilitate the return of affected Grade 12 learners.

The organisation previously told parents that returning learners would be accommodated at a boarding facility in Johannesburg while preparing for their 2026 examinations.

The number of learners expected to use the arrangement, as well as who will cover the costs of accommodation and other necessities, remains unclear.

World.title: Kaizer Chiefs fixture against Golden Arrows gets new venue – and date
World.content:
Kaizer Chiefs' Betway Premiership fixture against Golden Arrows has been moved to a new venue - and date. Image: Kaizer Chiefs website

Kaizer Chiefs’ Betway Premiership fixture against Golden Arrows has been moved to a new venue – and date.

The match was originally scheduled to take place at King Zwelithini Stadium in Durban on Saturday, 19 September.

However, the fixture will now be played at Mbombela Stadium in Nelspruit on Sunday, 20 September, with kick-off scheduled for 15:00.



READ | SIX Kaizer Chiefs players currently injured, but it’s not all bad news

Ticket information to follow

The change means supporters planning to attend the match will need to take note of the revised arrangements.

Golden Arrows, who are the designated home side, will provide ticketing information in due course.

Kaizer Chiefs will communicate the ticketing details once it has been made available by the hosts.

For Kaizer Chiefs supporters, the match now presents a trip to Mpumalanga rather than Durban, while the later date means the two teams will meet on the Sunday afternoon.

Further information regarding tickets and match-day arrangements is expected to be announced ahead of the fixture.



Next fixture

Meanwhile, Kaizer Chiefs’ next Betway Premiership match will take place this Saturday, 12 September when they take on Polokwane City.

The clash at the Old Peter Mokaba Stadium will kick off at 15:00.

Amakhosi find themselves in third place in the standings after five matches with 11 points after three wins and two draws.

They trail log leaders Mamelodi Sundowns by eight points, but have played two fewer matches.

World.title: Six South Africans still missing after devastating Nepal floods
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Six South Africans remain unaccounted for following devastating flash floods in Nepal, with authorities still unable to confirm their whereabouts.

The Department of International Relations and Cooperation (DIRCO) says it currently has no information on the missing South Africans.

The department is assisting efforts to identify people who may have been affected by the disaster. As part of the process, the South African Police Service (SAPS) has collected DNA samples from relatives of those who remain unaccounted for.

READ | Nepal flood death toll rises as rescuers scour tunnels

The DNA profiles have been shared with Nepali police and Interpol in Kathmandu to assist with possible identification.

South African diplomatic missions in New Delhi and Beijing are also working with local authorities to coordinate the response.

DIRCO says it remains in contact with the affected families and will continue providing updates as more information becomes available.

World.title: 'Arrogance of power' | Politicians under scrutiny over public outbursts
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Questions are being raised about how politicians should conduct themselves when engaging with angry or frustrated communities, following heated exchanges involving Water and Sanitation Minister Pemmy Majodina and Johannesburg Mayor Dada Morero.

Both incidents have sparked debate over whether public officials should be held to a higher standard when faced with provocation from residents.

Majodina came under scrutiny after she exchanged profanities with a community member during an engagement in Kouga in the Eastern Cape.

The incident happened at the launch of an upgraded pump station by the Department of Water and Sanitation.

Political analyst Jan-Jan Joubert says politicians should expect difficult and sometimes confrontational interactions with members of the public.

“They 

Joubert says that while many South Africans rarely have direct contact with politicians, emotions can run high when communities do get the opportunity to confront their leaders.

He says politicians who feel provoked should consider taking a diplomatic approach and involve other officials to help de-escalate the situation.

The incident involving Majodina is not the first recent example of a senior political figure losing their temper during a community engagement.

In August, Johannesburg Mayor Dada Morero told a community member during a public meeting in Tshepisong that they were “talking sh**”.

The meeting was held to address ongoing electricity problems affecting the community.

A resident called Morero a thief, an allegation the mayor repeatedly denied while asking the resident to retract the statement. When the resident persisted, Morero responded: “You are talking sh**.”

Morero later apologised publicly for his comments.

President Cyril Ramaphosa also condemned the mayor’s utterances as unacceptable, while acknowledging his apology.

“Our mayor has made utterances which we find completely unacceptable, but he has apologised. He’s gone public and apologised and we, as the ANC, have taken him up on that,” Ramaphosa said during a campaign in the same area.

The Department of Water and Sanitation has not commented on the incident involving Majodina.

World.title: Job losses threaten SA's fragile household recovery
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - South African households may be showing signs of recovery, but mounting job losses are raising questions about how sustainable that recovery really is.

The latest Altron FinTech Household Resilience Index has improved for a seventh consecutive quarter.

But that progress is being overshadowed by growing pressure on household incomes.

South Africa lost 190,000 formal-sector jobs in the first quarter, putting further strain on household finances.

As consumers turn to their savings to make ends meet, life insurance policy surrenders increased by 24 percent.

The report says households are feeling the impact of having fewer income earners, while warning that higher interest rates could put the recovery at risk.

Further interest rate cuts, however, could provide some relief to financially stretched households.

World.title: Taught to be strong, left to suffer: Breaking the silence on male suicide
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - As the world marks World Suicide Prevention Day, society is being urged to take a closer look at how boys and men are taught to deal with emotions, vulnerability and mental health.

For generations, many men have been expected to be the protectors and providers, the ones who remain strong, suppress their emotions and avoid showing weakness.

But mental health advocates warn that these expectations can come at a devastating cost.

Men account for the majority of recorded suicides in South Africa, with at least 30 male suicides reported each day. Of the 13,774 annual suicides recorded in South Africa, 10,861 are men.

Leon de Beer of the South African Federation for Mental Health says one of the first steps towards preventing male suicide is learning to recognise the signs of depression, particularly because depression in men may not always present in ways people traditionally expect.

READ | Concern over mental health of students

“When we think of depression, we think of social withdrawal, people feeling low mood, a loss of interest,” De Beer says.

However, he says depression in men can manifest differently, including through anger, irritability and aggression.

De Beer says individuals and communities need to educate themselves about these warning signs and be prepared to intervene when they notice them.

He also stresses the importance of taking any mention of suicide seriously.

“People should never ignore the signs and never dismiss or make light of comments if people are talking about suicide.”

Rather than avoiding difficult conversations, De Beer encourages people to listen, engage and offer support.

He says communities need to be brave enough to ask questions and have conversations about suicide instead of dismissing warning signs or assuming that someone is simply having a bad day.

World.title: Rooigrond escapee rearrested, DCS probing possible inside job
World.content:
PRETORIA – Wanted Rooigrond escapee Edward Khomotso Madiba has been rearrested.

According to Correctional Services, Madiba was rearrested 72 hours after escaping from the Rooigrond Maximum Security Correctional Centre near Mahikeng. He is now being held at the Kgosi Mampuru Correctional Facility.

Madiba escaped from the prison on 6 September while serving a 20-year sentence for robbery, possession of a firearm and ammunition, kidnapping and parole violations.

Correctional Services national commissioner Makgothi Thobakgale said Madiba was captured within 72 hours, in line with the department’s standing order to apprehend escapees as quickly as possible.

“This is a standing order in the department that when we have an escape, within the first 72 hours, we apprehend,” Thobakgale said.

World.title: Zero alcohol limit proposed, but can SA enforce it?
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The Department of Transport is moving closer to introducing a zero blood-alcohol limit for motorists, with plans to amend the National Road Traffic Act.

While the proposed change is being welcomed as a potentially significant step towards reducing road deaths, questions are being raised over whether South Africa has the capacity to enforce a zero-tolerance approach consistently.

Kashifa Ancer of the DG Murray Trust says enforcement remains one of the biggest challenges facing any move to tighten the law.

“We do not have enough police presence on our roads to ensure that enforcement is even,” Ancer said.

She pointed to the increased deployment of law enforcement resources during peak periods such as Easter, long weekends and the December holidays, saying enforcement is not consistently maintained throughout the year or across the country.

READ | Creecy calls for advanced training for scholar transport drivers

Ancer also raised concerns about what happens after motorists are caught driving under the influence.

“Once people are caught, we often see that there are programmes that they attend, rehabilitation programmes, education and awareness, and are not fully prosecuted according to the extent of the law,” she said.

She attributed this, in part, to capacity constraints and other challenges within the justice system.

Ancer said another major obstacle is the perception among some motorists that drinking and driving carries little risk of serious consequences.

“People still feel like they can take the risk. People still feel like there won’t be any impact for their behaviour.”

According to Ancer, public pressure for tougher measures often intensifies only after major crashes in which lives are lost.

She said the proposed zero blood-alcohol limit should therefore be accompanied by a clear implementation and enforcement strategy.

“It’d be very, very curious to know how the Ministry of Transport is going to position all of these challenges when thinking about how a 0.0 limit is actually going to be enforced,” Ancer said.

“How have they considered implementation and enforcement beyond just changing the number itself?”

World.title: August hottest month ever recorded globally: EU monitor
World.content:
BRUSSELS - The EU's climate monitor said that August was the hottest single month ever recorded globally, with ocean temperatures also reaching unprecedented highs as western Europe capped its warmest summer.

In response to the assessment by the Copernicus Climate Change Service, the UN warned that until humanity weaned off fossil fuels, the planet would only push deeper into uncharted territory.

Copernicus observations go back to 1940 but other evidence -- such as ice cores, tree rings and coral skeletons -- allow scientists to place today's climate against a much longer historical context.

"Humans haven't seen temperatures as hot as today for, arguably, at least the last 100,000 years," Samantha Burgess from the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts, which oversees Copernicus, told AFP.

Global average air temperatures in August were 16.96C, Copernicus said -- surpassing by 0.01C the previous all-time monthly record set in July 2023. Copernicus said it considered the two months joint-highest given the narrow difference.

Scientists say that human activity -- primarily the burning of coal, oil and gas -- has warmed the planet by roughly 1.4C since pre-industrial times and increased the severity and likelihood of extreme weather.

Yet heat-trapping greenhouse gas emissions rose to new highs in 2025.
