World.title: Prime minister: 2027 budget like a suitcase already full to bursting
World.content:
The government wants to reduce next year's budget deficit from 4.4 percent to 4 percent of GDP. According to Prime Minister Kristen Michal, there is no room for additional spending in the budget.

Eesti 200 Chair and Education Minister Kristina Kallas said expectations for pay raises should generally be kept low.

"As always, expectations are high, but the possibilities are considerably more limited. The state budget situation has not improved or changed in the meantime. In general, Ministry of Finance officials do a good job. When they give us a forecast, it usually holds true. And it should continue to do so," Kallas said.

"So, after two weeks of budget negotiations, the situation remains such that the deficit is already large before we have even begun discussing any additional funding requests. Therefore, we currently have practically no room to increase spending," Kallas said.

PM: Deficit could fall to 4 percent

Prime Minister Kristen Michal added that if the government granted all the requests for additional funding currently submitted by the ministries, next year's state budget deficit would rise to 7.3 percent of GDP.

"The spring forecast for next year was minus 4.9 percent. We have now brought that down by half a percentage point, to 4.4 percent. The goal could be to get to 4 percent. That could be a target that allows us to keep the growth of the debt burden under control," Michal said.

"At the same time, there are also many requests for additional funding. I'm not dismissing any of them. They are all understandable. Wages and incomes rose quite quickly this year because, in addition to pay raises, we also abolished the progressive income tax system known as the 'tax hump,'" Michal said.

Michal said the debate would continue, but that the situation was exactly as Kristina Kallas had described it.

"It's like packing for a trip, when you're sitting on the suitcase with your knee, trying to squeeze everything into that minus-four-percent case. And the sides still won't come together. If anyone thinks there's room to put anything else in there, it certainly doesn't look like it. When you're packing for a trip, try seeing whether you can fit another pair of boots into your bag when it's already overflowing and the suitcase won't close. That's exactly where we are with the budget right now," Michal said.

World.title: Hostage-takers hold Tartu family at gunpoint for a million euros
World.content:
According to the charges, the crime was committed by a group of people who travelled to Estonia from Bulgaria for precisely that purpose, Eesti Ekspress writes.

Two Romanian men have appeared in Tartu County Court accused of taking hostages and demanding €1 million from a person working in IT and cryptocurrency.

Constantin Ligi and Ionut-Dorin Soimosan deny the charges, which prosecutors say relate to a four-member group that travelled to Estonia specifically to carry out the crime.

According to the Prosecutor's Office, three masked men entered a Tartu apartment on the evening of March 10 last year, tied up four people and threatened them with a firearm and what they claimed was a bomb.

The hostages were relatives of the intended extortion target, whom the attackers contacted by video call to demand payment.

The men eventually left the apartment, warning the victims not to leave or contact police, before fleeing Estonia and using false information and vehicle changes to conceal their movements.

Prosecutor Lauriine Tšitškan described the case as an example of "crime-as-a-service," in which international organized crime networks carry out offences for clients.

Four suspects were arrested in different countries this year, with Ligi and Soimosan the first to be extradited to Estonia.

At the preliminary hearing, both sought release from custody: Ligi cited his role as his family's sole breadwinner in Germany, while Soimosan said he needed to manage his business in Malta.

The prosecutor opposed their release, citing nine previous convictions for Ligi and five for Soimosan and questioned how Soimosan could attend future hearings if, as he indicated, authorities in Malta would confiscate his passport upon his return.

Judge Heli Sillaots is expected to rule on their continued detention later on Thursday.

World.title: Gallery: Mythbústers' comics exhibition opens at Estonian Academy of Arts
World.content:
The Estonian Academy of Arts (EKA) in Tallinn has opened "Mythbústers," a Nordic‑Baltic comics exhibition featuring works by 16 artists reflecting their perspectives on life in the region.

The works on display were originally published in a Latvian comic book magazine at the end of last year. The exhibition has since toured various countries, and at the end of September the works will move on from EKA to Helsinki.

According to participating artist Liisa Kruusmägi, comic books and strips are well suited to the exhibition format, as this gives people who do not normally read comic books a chance to become acquainted with the medium. She is also optimistic about Estonia's comic book scene.

"We have the famous Joonas Sildre, who has published a lot and whose work is also translated, with English‑language editions available in bookshops, but of course there could be more," Kruusmägi said.

She encouraged more people to try their hand at the genre. "I encourage people to make comics, and EKA has had comic book courses and similar things over the years, so I hope it develops somehow," she said.

Kruusmägi added that she does relatively little with comics herself. "I've contributed to that comics magazine a few times and published a little on my own. I would also like to publish a graphic novel myself, but for me it is difficult because it also requires good writing skills," she added.

The exhibition is open in the foyer at EKA at Põhja pst 7 until the end of the month.

World.title: Iraq secures US, South Korean, Turkish air defenses
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNew.com) — Iraq has finalized contracts for new air defense systems from the United States, South Korea, and Turkey, with the first deliveries due shortly as Baghdad prepares to regain more control of its airspace when the US-led coalition mission expires on September 30.

Baghdad intends to deploy the technology around the nation to safeguard oil installations, important infrastructure, and Iraqi territory while it develops an integrated network of long-, medium-, and short-range defenses backed by radar and command systems.

The effort took on new significance as Iraq’s airspace became a conduit for missiles, drones, and military aircraft amid regional warfare involving Iran, the US, and Israel.

Iran has also directly attacked US sites in Iraq, highlighting Baghdad’s inadequate capacity to prevent foreign assaults and protect its airspace on its own.

Iraq had initially planned a six-year program to upgrade its air defenses, but Al-Zaidi reduced the timeline to three years.

The increase corresponds with the final evacuation of soldiers assigned to the multinational coalition’s mission in Iraq.

Baghdad claims Iraqi troops can now manage the residual ISIS threat, and Operation Inherent Resolve will officially finish inside Iraq at the end of the month.

The new systems from the United States, South Korea, and Turkey are likely to play a key role in Iraq’s efforts to bridge a long-standing air-defense gap and gain more control over its skies after the coalition departs.

World.title: Yemen’s Houthis seize key city on Red Sea: military source
World.content:
Sanaa – Yemen’s Houthis seized control of the strategic Red Sea port city of Mokha on Thursday, a Yemeni military source told AFP, as the Iran-backed group reported fresh strikes by Saudi forces.

The Houthis, who control large parts of northwest Yemen, launched a large-scale offensive last week against Yemeni government forces, who are backed by Saudi Arabia.

They also launched attacks on Saudi territory that left dozens of people wounded, in a conflict that has reignited during the Middle East war that began with US-Israeli strikes on Iran in late February.

Witnesses told AFP they saw Houthi forces entering Mokha on Thursday while chanting “death to America, death to Israel”.

The Yemeni military source said they were advancing towards the strategic Bab al-Mandab strait “after having taken control of Mokha”.

The waterway, which links Asia to Europe via the Red Sea and Suez Canal, has gained importance as a transit route since the start of the wider Middle East war, which saw Iran blockade the Strait of Hormuz.

The military source said the Houthis also seized Zuqar Island, in the southern Red Sea, “after rocket attacks and a ground assault carried out using boats transporting fighters”.

Also on Thursday, the Houthis reported airstrikes.

“The Saudi enemy’s air force conducted around 40 strikes in recent hours in the governorates of Taiz, Hodeida, Al-Jawf and Marib,” Houthi news agency Saba said.

– Hundreds dead –

Yemen relapsed into war in July after years of relative calm punctured by sporadic violence and deepening poverty.

Since last week, the fighting in Yemen has left more than 500 dead, mostly combatants, according to an AFP tally compiled from several sources.

It has also forced nearly 20,000 people to flee their homes, the International Organization for Migration said on Tuesday.

On Wednesday, the Saudi-led coalition battling the Houthis said the anti-government fighters fired ballistic missiles and drones at several cities in southern Saudi Arabia.

The Saudi civil defence issued alerts warning of “potential danger” in two areas, Khamis Mushait and Abha, before lifting them soon after.

The Houthis triggered the return to hostilities in July when they let an Iranian plane land in defiance of Saudi control of Yemeni airspace.

The government retaliated by striking Sanaa airport, an attack the Houthis blamed on its sponsor, Saudi Arabia.

The ongoing exchanges risk returning Yemen to a conflict that left hundreds of thousands of people dead and sparked one of the world’s worst humanitarian crises.

The Houthis, after seizing Yemen’s capital and forcing out the internationally recognised government, fought a Saudi-led coalition from 2015 until a United Nations-brokered ceasefire in 2022.

World.title: France will not support Infantino in FIFA election: federation chief
World.content:
Paris – France will not support the candidacy of Gianni Infantino, who is running for a new term as FIFA president in March 2027, the French Football Federation (FFF) announced on Thursday.

The FFF is aligning itself with the position of other European federations such as Belgium, Italy, Scotland, Sweden and Wales, who have also publicly withdrawn support for Infantino.

FIFA confirmed last weekend that Infantino will stand in the FIFA presidential election next March, despite the backlash over his now-abandoned plan to bring private investment into the men’s and women’s World Cups.

At this stage, the 56-year-old Swiss is the only candidate.

“We believe that the trust placed in the FIFA president has been betrayed, and that the way in which the governance of world football is envisaged no longer reflects us,” FFF president Philippe Diallo said in a statement.

“That is why, by a unanimous decision of its members, the French Football Federation has decided to withdraw its support for Gianni Infantino’s candidacy for the FIFA presidency.”

World.title: Vance takes spotlight as Republicans close Trump-heavy convention
World.content:
Dallas – US Republicans return to the stage Thursday to close their midterm convention, still betting that Donald Trump’s political magnetism can overcome grim election forecasts — while giving Vice President JD Vance a prime-time showcase as a potential heir.

Trump will dominate the finale of the two-day gathering, delivering closing remarks after Vance’s keynote address at the American Airlines Center in downtown Dallas.

The unusual convention has been built around a simple message: Trump may not literally be on November’s ballot, but Republicans want the president’s supporters to behave as though he is.

That strategy comes with the party under heavy pressure.

US election tracking site Decision Desk HQ projects Democrats will win the House 230-205 and take the Senate 51-49. Trump’s approval rating has languished in the low-to-mid 30s amid stubborn inflation and an unpopular war with Iran.

Trump dramatically raised the stakes in his opening night keynote Wednesday, promising a $5,000 “Trump dividend” to every American adult if Republicans retain both chambers of Congress in November.

He also made explicit the convention’s central electoral pitch.

“I’m asking you to pretend that I’m on the ballot — I’m on the ballot, I’m on the ballot — just one more time,” he said.

He strongly defended the Iran war, predicting victory would bring down oil prices, and warned that the United States would become a “communist country” if Democrats prevail in the election.

– Heir apparent? –

Vance’s appearance adds intrigue to the closing night.

The 42-year-old vice president is widely regarded as an early front-runner for the 2028 Republican presidential nomination, although he has said he will not make a decision until after the midterms.

His place immediately before Trump’s closing remarks gives him one of the most prominent speaking slots of the convention and an opportunity to address a party already beginning to consider its post-Trump future.

But in the more immediate contest, Republicans need Vance and other party figures to help deliver Trump’s voters in an election in which the president himself is absent from the ballot.

Republicans also hope to use the closing night to promote tax cuts, immigration enforcement and other administration policies while depicting Democrats as increasingly extreme.

The convention has resembled an extended Trump rally more than a traditional party meeting, with no nominations or formal business and more than 50 speakers or presentations each night.

The atmosphere inside the arena on Wednesday was festive despite the political headwinds. Yet not all Republicans have embraced the experiment.

Numerous lawmakers in competitive races chose to remain in their districts rather than spend valuable campaign time in Dallas, while both convention nights were facing competition from the opening games of the NFL season.

Those who have shown up will be looking for evidence that Vance can emulate Trump in energizing the voters who powered the flamboyant billionaire’s return to the White House.

And Vance, whether he acknowledges it or not, will be speaking to a party already asking who might inherit those voters when Trump is no longer the headline act.

“If the American people give Republicans another chance to govern, we’re going to create more prosperity,” Vance told Fox News after Trump’s speech.

“And we want the American people to share in that prosperity.”

World.title: Iraqi Airways doubles Baghdad-Amman flights on peak days
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraqi Airways will double flights between Baghdad and Amman on peak travel days beginning Friday, Sept. 11, in response to increased passenger demand between Iraq and Jordan.

The airline said that it would boost flights from one to two each day on Thursdays, Fridays, and Saturdays, increasing capacity on three of the busiest days of the week.

Daily service will continue on the other days.

The increased schedule provides additional alternatives for travelers traveling between Baghdad International Airport and Amman’s Queen Alia International Airport, both of which are already available on Iraqi Airways’ booking network.

Iraqi Airways said that the extra flights are being added in response to a large increase in passenger traffic on the route, with the goal of providing more flexibility as demand develops.

The move improves air connectivity between Iraq and Jordan, which have strong business, tourist, and family travel relations.

The development coincides with Iraqi Airways’ efforts to expand fleet operating capacity and widen its regional and international network.

As part of its attempts to increase fleet availability, the state-owned airline has recently resumed aircraft operations and expanded repair capabilities.

The revised Baghdad-Amman timetable becomes effective on September 11.

World.title: Seahawks beat Patriots again in NFL opener
World.content:
Los Angeles – The Seattle Seahawks shrugged off Sam Darnold’s early injury to beat the New England Patriots 13-10 in the NFL’s opening game, piling more misery on the team they defeated in last season’s Super Bowl.

Backup quarterback Drew Lock threw for 187 yards and a touchdown to Jackson Smith-Njigba, as reigning champs Seattle rallied from 10-0 down for their 11th consecutive win.

The latest loss inflicted more pain on New England quarterback Drake Maye, who threw three costly interceptions, including a particularly wasteful one in the final seconds from field-goal range to throw away a patchy, defensive game.

Maye — who had been sacked six times in February’s Super Bowl, and suffered three more here — was picked off by Seahawks cornerback Josh Jobe in the end zone.

“It was game on the line. You know, fourth quarter… we only was up three points, and we got to take the ball away, and we did,” said Jobe.

“Holy cow, we did it! Here we are, one-and-zero,” said Lock.

And it was a night to forget for the Patriot’s new acquisitions too, as AJ Brown limped off with an ankle injury and Romeo Doubs was beaten for one interception and was guilty of a terrible drop shortly before a second.

The Seattle evening began in festive fashion. A new Super Bowl LX championship banner was unfurled from Lumen Field’s colossal rafters. Pearl Jam’s Mike McCready performed the national anthem.

But the mood was punctured on the game’s first drive. Darnold was sacked on third down by Dre’Mont Jones, and limped to the locker room via the medical tent clutching his hip. He did not return.

The Patriots struck first. Maye hurled the ball 34 yards to Brown on the edge of the endzone. Defensive pass interference was called, and Maye immediately lofted a short pass over the top to newly drafted tight end Eli Raridon for the season’s first touchdown.

Seattle fought back. Veteran receiver Cooper Kupp took a stunning one-handed diving catch from Lock for a 24-yard gain on third down. The pair then celebrated a touchdown pass, before the score was ruled out for an illegal shift, and the Seahawks settled for a field goal.

– Interceptions –

After a promising Patriots drive, Maye’s ambitious downfield hurl to Romeo Doubs ricocheted off Rodney Thomas’s fingers to Nehemiah Pritchett for the game’s first interception.

The Seahawks made Maye pay. At 4th & 1, Lock passed to an open Smith-Njigba, who raced past the Patriots defense at lightning speed for a 45-yard touchdown, tying the game 10-10.

Seattle drove again, with Lock peppering passes before charging 14 yards into the red zone. A series of errors from a hugely promising position meant it was only a field goal.

An increasingly desperate Maye suffered his first sack of the night trying to break through the Seattle defense. Two more swiftly followed, though the Patriots somehow edged the ball upfield, twice successfully going for fourth downs.

But sensing a chance for a winning touchdown, despite being in field goal range, Maye hurled a deep right pass to Mack Hollins in the end zone, resulting in Jobe’s game-ending interception.

“We’ve moved on. This is a new season. We did the banner thing. It’s time to find out who 2026 Seahawks are going to be,” said Lock.

World.title: Philippine ferry fire kills 5, dozens missing
World.content:
Manila – At least five people were killed and 86 remain missing after a fire erupted aboard a ferry near a tourist hotspot in the Philippine province of Palawan, the coast guard said Thursday.

The blaze broke out on the M/V June Aster Wednesday evening about 2.2 kilometres (1.3 miles) offshore, the coast guard said, adding that five casualties had been brought ashore.

Video shared by the coast guard on Facebook showed the vessel completely engulfed in flames.

Hundreds of people, desperate for news about the incident, have left comments on the Coron town mayor’s Facebook page, searching for relatives, friends and even a dog.

“Based on the data we have right now on rescued (42) and the casualties, we still have 87 people who are unaccounted for,” coast guard Captain Noemi Cayabyab told a local radio station on Thursday.

The ship’s manifest had listed 134 passengers and crew, Cayabyab said.

Of those rescued, 38 were passengers and four were crew, she added.

Hours later, the Philippine Coast Guard told reporters that another person had been rescued, but their identity had yet to be confirmed.

“Just to make it clear, this is live data and may change as our search and rescue operations are ongoing,” Cayabyab said in the radio interview.

“However, we have not yet been able to obtain information from the rescued individuals because we have not been able to speak with them,” she said, adding attempts to put out the blaze were ongoing.

There were no immediate reports of foreigners on board.

Tracking data from MarineTraffic showed the June Aster had departed from Manila.

In January, a triple-decker ferry carrying more than 340 people sank off the southern Philippines, killing at least 52 people.

The M/V Trisha Kerstin 3 sank along nearly the same route where 31 people died in 2023 after a fire broke out aboard the Lady Mary Joy 3 ferry.

World.title: Asian Games begin with Qatar basketball win, nine days before opening ceremony
World.content:
Tokyo – The Asian Games began in Japan on Thursday when Qatar beat Iran in the men’s basketball opening group game, the first action in the continental multi-sport showpiece that has more participants than the Olympics.

Over 17,000 athletes and officials are expected to take part in 43 sports at the Nagoya-Aichi Games — which do not officially start until the opening ceremony on September 19 and will run until October 4.

Several events such as basketball, football, cricket, hockey and modern pentathlon will get under way before the opening ceremony.

Qatar held off a comeback from Iran to win their Group B encounter 59-35 at the Aichi International Arena in Nagoya in the first match of a men’s basketball competition that will hold medal finals on September 20, the day after the opening ceremony.

Los Angeles 2028 Olympics qualifying spots are up for grabs in several sports at the Asian Games, which are returning to Japan for the first time since 1994.

Organisers hope the athletes will have a “unique experience” staying in eye-catching accommodation ranging from a cruise liner and wooden containers to standard hotel rooms.

Officials are confident that the plan will not be affected by Japan’s typhoon season, which is usually in full swing in September-October.

Weather has already caused disruptions, with record rainfall on Tuesday forcing hundreds of athletes briefly to evacuate their accommodation.

Rainwater also leaked into some competition venues, with more wet weather forecast for the coming days.

Among those in action at the Games will be Philippine tennis sensation Alexandra Eala and a pair of world-class teenage talents in 15-year-old Indian cricketer Vaibhav Sooryavanshi and 13-year-old Chinese swimmer Yu Zidi.

World.title: Ladakh groups express disappointment over MHA meet; Wangchuk warns of fresh stir from Sept 19
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Ladakh groups have expressed disappointment after a meeting with the ministry of home affairs sub-committee, saying the Centre failed to present the much-awaited draft for a proposed elected body for the Union Territory.

Climate activist and Leh Apex Body (LAB) member Sonam Wangchuk said there had been âno special progressâ since the May 22 meeting, while Kargil Democratic Alliance (KDA) representative Sajjad Kargili said the delegation had come to Delhi expecting a draft detailing the structure and powers of the proposed body.

What are the demands?

The LAB and KDA have been seeking an elected legislative body at the UT level and safeguards for land, jobs, culture and identity since talks with the Centre began in 2021, news agency PTI reported.

Kargili said the meeting reiterated that the proposed body would be elected, with separate delimitation and constituencies. However, the groups said there was still no clarity on the overall distribution of powers, including law and order.

The groups also pressed for early legislation and elections.

Wangchuk also mentioned that Centre indicated that compensation would be provided to those killed or injured during the September 24, 2025 violence in Leh and that an announcement was expected soon.





âWe demanded that all cases should be withdrawn together. They said they will think about it,â Wangchuk said, adding that the delegation could not say the Centre had agreed to the demand.

Wangchuk warns of fresh agitation

Wangchuk has warned that the groups could resume agitation if major decisions were taken before an elected democratic body was established.

World.title: 'Can't browbeat child': SC on CJP protester's intimidation complaint against 'influencer'
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Thursday took serious note of allegations that a 14-year-old girl associated with the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) protests was harassed and that her residence was subjected to stone pelting, directing authorities to act on her FIR and provide protection to her and her family.

A bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, comprising Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, asked Solicitor General Tushar Mehta to ensure action on the girl's FIR and sought status reports from the Delhi and Uttar Pradesh governments on the allegations, security arrangements and action taken against those allegedly involved.

The court stressed that nobody could be allowed to intimidate a victim or her family to prevent them from pursuing criminal proceedings.

"Such matters cannot be taken lightly. Nobody should be protected if violence against a child is involved... if persons accused of such acts were roaming free and attempting to browbeat the child or her family so that they do not pursue criminal proceedings, it would be a serious matter.

"There cannot be any second opinion about it. Such matters cannot be taken lightly. Nobody should be protected. If violence against a child is involved and persons are roaming free and trying to browbeat the child or the family so that they do not pursue the criminal proceedings, that may be a serious matter," the bench observed.





The counsel appearing for the minor told the court that she had been harassed and her house vandalised after she registered an FIR against a person who allegedly claimed in a video that he had attacked her father during the CJP's protest.

The lawyer alleged that instead of prosecuting people who accompanied the accused and were allegedly captured on camera, an FIR had been registered against the child. The counsel also submitted that this was contrary to an earlier Supreme Court order and that video evidence showing stone pelting at the girl's residence could be placed before the court.

"The high-powered committee will take time, but if something happens to the child in the meantime, that cannot subsequently be reversed or repaired through the committee," the counsel submitted.

Responding to the submission, CJI Surya Kant said, "If there are anti-social elements who indulged in violence against child, and they are roaming free, and are trying to browbeat the child, that may be a serious thing."

The Chief Justice further told the Solicitor General, "Child is a child. Some measures to protect the child can be taken. This incident can be taken as a standalone [case] by local police."

Justice Joymalya Bagchi also directed that immediate action be taken on the FIR and that the minor and her family be provided police protection.

"We would like immediate action on that FIR and police protection to victim and family by UP police.

Investigation be conducted by Parliament Street PS".

The counsel also alleged that videos showed four policemen accompanying the persons who attacked the protesters and claimed that no action had been taken against them.

Delhi Police action against accused

Bhardwaj was detained in Bulandshahr after the CJP staged a protest outside Parliament Street police station demanding his arrest over the alleged assault.

The police action followed an interview in which Bhardwaj allegedly claimed that he had "cracked the skull" of the minor activist's father during the July 20 protest and escaped arrest because of his political connections.

During Thursday's hearing, Senior Advocate PV Dinesh also mentioned a plea filed by second-year law student Akshat Tripathi challenging a notice issued to him by the Executive Magistrate, Greater Noida. The notice was subsequently withdrawn.

Dinesh urged the court to hear the plea, arguing that a strong message needed to be sent to IAS officers.

World.title: How BJP, Congress turned 80s AI trend turned into an all-out meme war
World.content:
NEW DELHI: What began as another harmless social media trend, turning present-day photographs into portraits straight out of the 1980s, has now found its way into the social feeds of politicians has triggered BJP-Congress war of memes.

Over the past few days, Instagram and X have been flooded with AI-generated photographs featuring big hair, aviator sunglasses, denim jackets, vintage suits and the grainy finish of old family albums.

BJP leaders were among the first to jump onto the trend. Union commerce minister Piyush Goyal shared an AI-generated photograph of himself dressed in a grey suit and aviators, writing simply: "Vibing to the 80s trend."

Union minister Kiren Rijiju followed with his own retro look, posing beside a car in an image designed to resemble a photograph from the decade.

"Why is everyone going back to the 80s vibes? I'm also forced to 80s nostalgia!" he wrote.

Congress Sevadal brought

into the picture, posting AI-generated photographs of the leader of opposition with the caption: "Rahul Gandhi catches the 80s trend wave."

The BJP's official X handle also shared some original pictures of Prime Minister Narendra Modi believed to be from the 1980s era.





What started as politicians recreating their younger selves soon became another format for the BJP and Congress to take veiled potshots at each other with AI doing the set design.

The Congress's Kerala unit shared an AI-generated image showing a bald man sitting in the front passenger seat of a Maruti Suzuki Omni, with the caption: "A Gujarat street in the 80s."

For context, the van, launched in India in the 1980s, became a familiar sight in Bollywood films where it was often shown being used by goons and kidnappers, eventually earning its own "kidnapping van" meme identity.

BJP Gujarat hit back with an AI-generated image of its own.

BJP's Telangana unit also responded to the Congress post. It shared an image showing a woman in a red dress dancing on a table inside what appeared to be a bar, with liquor bottles visible in cabinets behind her.

The description read: "Lusiana, Italy. Circa-1970s."

The BJP did not name anyone in the post either, but the reference was widely seen as an allusion to Lusiana, the Italian town where former Congress president Sonia Gandhi was born.

Congress MP

, however, found a way of joining the trend without asking AI to take him back in time.

"The 1980s seem to be back, courtesy of AI. I thought Iâd join the trend the old-fashioned way," he wrote, sharing photographs that were actually taken during the decade.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The pictures included Tharoor with his sons Ishaan and Kanishk.

What is the trend?

The trend itself is simple. Users upload a present-day selfie to AI tools such as ChatGPT or Google Gemini and ask them to recreate the image as if it had been taken in the 1980s.

Unlike a regular vintage filter, the AI rebuilds the photograph around the personâs face, adding everything from big hairstyles and retro clothes to film grain and old-school studio lighting.

The result is a polished throwback image that looks straight out of an old photo album or Bollywood publicity still. The trend has spread rapidly across Instagram and X, with influencers, celebrities and now politicians joining in.

World.title: ‘Hoping draft ready by Oct’: Ladakh chief secy as UT seeks Article 371 safeguards
World.content:
Breakthrough in talks with MHA on legislative powers: Ladakh grps

What Ladakh is seeking

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

What does Article 371 provide?

NEW DELHI: Ladakh chief secretary Ashish Kundra said on Thursday that the Union Territory is moving towards seeking constitutional safeguards for its local population under Article 371, along with the creation of a UT-level elected body with legislative and financial powers.Kundra said a meeting of the sub-committee was held at the ministry of home affairs on Wednesday with the leadership of the Apex Body and the Kargil Democratic Alliance from Ladakh. Discussions focused on incorporating a special provision under Article 371 to protect the interests of the local population.He said the next meeting is scheduled for October, with the administration hoping to have an advanced draft of the proposed Constitutional Amendment Bill ready by then.The proposed framework would include a Union Territory-level body elected directly through constituencies and vested with legislative and financial powers.The move comes amid demands for greater constitutional protection for Ladakh following its transition into a Union Territory.Articles 371 contain special provisions for specific states. These provisions differ from one state to another but broadly seek to protect local political, cultural, social and economic interests.Article 371-A, for instance, provides special safeguards for Nagaland. Articles 371-B and 371-C provide for special committees in the Legislative Assemblies of Assam and Manipur and similiarly other provisions are there for other states.If a new Article 371 provision is introduced specifically for Ladakh, it would be significant because Ladakh is a Union Territory rather than a state.The proposal would therefore require a constitutional arrangement tailored to a Union Territory, potentially making it different from the existing Article 371 provisions that primarily apply to states.

World.title: Space-based surveillance: Dhruva to get key systems worth €5m from Safran
World.content:
BENGALURU: French firm Safran Space, under contracts worth more than â¬5 million, will supply critical systems, including optical payloads, for satellites being built as part of Indiaâs Space-Based Surveillance-3 (SBS-3) programme by Dhruva Space, a release from the French Presidentâs Office has confirmed.

The contracts, signed during the International Space Summit in Paris, cover communication systems, inertial navigation units, optical payloads and ground stations for the constellation, which is planned to be deployed between 2027 and 2030.

SBS-3, a strategic project approved by the Cabinet Committee on Security, will comprise 52 satellites in low Earth and geostationary orbits and is aimed at providing the armed forces with persistent surveillance, secure communications and greater situational awareness across Indiaâs land and maritime areas of interest.

The programme marks an expansion of the private sectorâs role in Indiaâs strategic space capabilities. Of the 52 satellites, 31 are to be built by private industry, with the remaining 21 being built by Isro. The private-sector allocation has been divided among three companies: Antaris will build 15 satellites, while Pixxel and Dhruva Space will build eight each.

Dhruvaâs eight satellites therefore form part of the private-sector component of the larger SBS-3 constellation, rather than a separate constellation.





The programme is expected to improve the frequency with which strategic areas can be observed and strengthen Indiaâs ability to monitor developments along its borders and across the Indian Ocean Region.

The Safran contracts will give Dhruva access to a range of French technologies for the satellites and associated ground infrastructure. Safran said the cooperation illustrates the rise of Indian New Space and the ability of French industry to support the development of Indiaâs sovereign space capabilities.

The company also said the partnership could open the way to further cooperation under future phases of the SBS programme.

The Paris summit also produced two other India-related announcements. French launch-services provider RIDE! signed an agreement to launch two satellites for TakeMeToSpace, an Indian company developing orbital data centres. The deal builds on RIDE!âs collaboration with Indian space companies, including the launch of a European atmospheric re-entry capsule aboard Isroâs PSLV.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Separately, French Earth-observation company U-Space and Indian company Axiscades signed a commercial cooperation agreement to explore the Indian microsatellite market, addressing both commercial and institutional demand.

Together, the three announcements point to a widening India-France space relationship spanning strategic surveillance, satellite launches and commercial satellite manufacturing, with Indian private companies increasingly at the centre of the cooperation.

World.title: BSP's family drama: Why no 'Anand' for Mayawati ahead of Uttar Pradesh elections?
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Three promotions. Three demotions. And now staring at a possible exit!

Well, thatâs how the political scorecard reads for Akash Anand, whose âmaturity meterâ has not just failed him again, but has also put him on the brink of exit from the

(BSP).

7 days after his third demotion, Akash Anand finds himself in a difficult spot, with BSP chief

opening the doors for his exit from the party. "The people in the party feel that just as he was relieved of all the important responsibilities of the post of national coordinator on September 3, 2026, he should now also be completely freed from the party from today. Therefore, if Akash Anand wants to remain independent in the party, he is free to do so; that is, he has now been completely freed from the party," Mayawati posted on X.

This despite the fact that Akash Anand's father-in-law, former Rajya Sabha MP Ashok Siddharth on Thursday bowed before Mayawati's ultimatum and announced his retirement from politics and social life, after the BSP chief linked his "sanyas" to any future reinstatement of responsibilities to her nephew Akash Anand.

In an emotional post on X, Siddharth said he was retiring from political and social life "right now", adding that if he ever had to give his life for Mayawati, it would be a matter of pride for him.





FIL bends but Mayawati refuses to budge

But neither Siddharth's actions nor his words made any impact on Mayawati.

She questioned Siddharth's intentions, saying his "announcement should have come immediately after her call for him to retire." Mayawati alleged that the delay showed that Siddharth's ambitions and intentions had not changed completely.

"If Ashok Siddharth had even a little genuine concern for the bright future of his son-in-law Akash Anand and the larger interests of the BSP and its Ambedkarite Bahujan movement, he would have announced his retirement without delay," she said.

Mayawati also slammed Anand for not reposting her earlier X post linking his future responsibilities in the party to his father-in-law's retirement. She said Anand had earlier reposted posts from her social media account "to demonstrate his loyalty," but had not done so in this case despite the post being in his own interest.

Mayawati said this indicated that both Siddharth and Anand were more attached to personal and family interests than to the success of the party and its movement.

She questioned whether Anand could effectively serve the BSP while remaining caught between his family ties and the interests of the party.

"If Akash Anand is less concerned about the real interests of the party and the movement and his own political career, and more attached to family relationships, then it is natural to ask how he can work for the good of the BSP and the movement while remaining double-minded," she said.

Third time unlucky?

Akash Anandâs latest demotion was on September 3, when aunt Mayawati announced that her nephew had again lost his political maturity.

"I have allowed Akash Anand to work in the party, which is before all of you, but Akash Anand still needs to become more mature. Till then, it would not be appropriate to give him a major responsibility in the party," Mayawati said at a national-level meeting of BSP office-bearers.

And that ensured Akash Anand, the chief national coordinator of BSP, was back to square one.

His Twitter bio reflected the sudden change in his status within the party. From BSP "National Convenor", he became "Party Worker, BSP." Just a few days later, he made yet another edit to his bio, which read: "Party Supporter, BSP." This is how his X bio reads now.

It was less than a month back, August 10 to be exact, that Akash Anand had formally launched the BSPâs election campaign for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections from Sadabad assembly constituency in Hathras.

He addressed a well-attended rally and launched a broadside against the BJP government in Uttar Pradesh over jobs, education and law and order, while taking digs at Congress leader Rahul Gandhi and Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav, calling them both âuncle.

â

From being anointed Mayawatiâs successor to being a party worker and now a party supporter - it has been a tumultuous and bumpy ride for the young Akash Anand.

And this time around there is a twist in the tale: Akashâs younger brother Ishan Anand has been brought to the centre stage.

On September 3, when Mayawati entered the venue of the meeting of office-bearers, walking behind her was not Akash but his younger brother Ishan. Wearing the BSP's blue sash around his neck, he stood behind his aunt till she settled down.

Akash Anand entered politics in 2017 at the young age of 22. Anand, who did his MBA from London, made his political debut with Mayawati at a rally in Uttar Pradesh's Saharanpur, where he shared the dais with Akhilesh Yadav and Ajit Singh.

In April 2019, Akash Anand addressed his first rally in Uttar Pradesh's Agra. The BSP was then part of the opposition Mahagathbandhan, an anti-Congress and anti-BJP bloc formed in the run-up to the 2019 general election under the leadership of Akhilesh Yadav and Mayawati with Ajit Singh's Rashtriya Lok Dal.

Mayawati appointed him BSPâs national coordinator in June 2019. Since then, it has been a bumpy ride for him.

Every promotion since then has been followed by a demotion.

Anand's FIL connection and maturity question

After 6 days of suspense, Mayawati finally revealed what triggered her against Akash Anand yet again. In a long post on X, Mayawati explained how Akash Anand had once again, after two years, lost his âpolitical maturity.â And also, what he could do to get it back.

The trigger this time around was Ashok Siddharth, the father in law of Akash Anand. Ashok Siddharth was expelled by Maywati from BSP last month for the second time over indiscipline and anti-party stance.

Taking to X, the BSP supremo wrote: âIt is well known that Ashok Siddharth had previously been expelled for indiscipline and violating guidelines, specifically regarding the distribution of party tickets and a failure to coordinate properly with BSP Maharashtra state president during state elections. He had been reinstated on the condition that he would not repeat such mistakes and would be assigned responsibility of expanding the party's support base only in other states, not in Uttar Pradesh.

â

She also informed that Ashok Siddharth will not be taken back into the party âunder any circumstances in the futureâ.

Hardening her stand further against Ashok Siddharth, Mayawati stated that a clear path remains for Akash Anand to resume an active leadership role within the movement, provided Siddharth steps aside completely.

Akash Anand's on-off jouney with BSP.

"In such a situation, keeping in mind the interests of the BSP Party and Movement, as well as his own family and the future of his son-in-law Shri Akash Anand, Shri Ashok Siddharth still has the opportunity to renounce his political ambitions, rise above personal interests, etc.,

and completely retire from politics. Only then will Shri Akash Anand be able to work freely in the party, and only then will the party sympathetically consider restoring his responsibilities so that he can play an active role in the partyâthis is the general consensus in the party," Mayawati said in her post.

Urging people from the Dalit community, to not engage in any action driven by personal or familial interests that creates obstacles in their path, for which âhistory may not forgive them," Mayawati cited Ashok Siddharth as a prime example of an official prioritising "personal and familial interests and ambitions over the BSP's mission, despite receiving multiple opportunities to reform.

"The party gave him not just one but several opportunities to mend his ways, but he prioritised his personal and familial interests and ambitions over the BSP's mission, the consequences of which he himself, along with his son-in-law Shri Akash Anand, has had to bear," Mayawati said in her statement.

Can BSP afford this 'family drama'?

With the UP assembly elections just months away, a family drama is the last thing that the BSP cadres in the state would have hoped for.

The partyâs trajectory in the state has been downhill. In the 2022 assembly elections, the BSP could win just 1 seat with a vote share of 12.88%. This was a sharp decline from the 19 seats and a 22.23% vote share that Mayawati had got in 2017.

The 2024 Lok Sabha elections went on to showcase that Mayawatiâs dismal 2022 performance was not an aberration. The BSP supremo failed to win even one Lok Sabha seat, while her partyâs vote share dipped to 9.4% from 19.43% in 2019.

Clearly, the results reinforced the gradual decline in BSPâs influence among Dalits.

From a sweeping majority in 2007 to allegations of being the B-team of BJP, the BSPâs political fortunes have nosedived in the state. The BSP supporters have dwindled and some have even changed loyalties, but what remains still strong is Mayawatiâs appeal and popularity among the partyâs cadres.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

However, the 2027 challenge is going to be tough for Maywati and her BSP.

The SP-Congress alliance managed to garner a lot of Dalit support in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, upsetting BJPâs applecart in the state and eventually at the Centre. Cleary this was not the time when the BSP chief should have precipitated action against Akash Anand and pitched one nephew against the other.

Mayawati needs a strong comeback and to ensure that she has to first set her house in order. All the more, as she has announced that BSP will not enter into any alliance in future elections. The BSP needs to perform if Mayawati wants to remain relevant in the stateâs politics. Another poor show where she wins votes but not seats will reinforce allegations that BSP is the B-team of the BJP.

World.title: Karnataka govt to mandate only 2 stanzas of Vande Mataram at state events
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Karnataka government on Thursday directed that the national song â

â be played or sung at all state government programmes and official ceremonies.

According to a government order dated September 8, 2026, the decision was taken in accordance with guidelines issued by the Union Ministry of Home Affairs.

The order states that, except at programmes attended by the President, Vice President, Prime Minister or Governor, only the first two stanzas of âVande Mataramâ shall be sung at all state government programmes. The order was issued in the name of the governor of Karnataka.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The development comes amid a political row over the rendition of âVande Mataramâ, after Congress general secretary KC Venugopal said the full version of the song âsits uneasilyâ with the syncretic and pluralist ethos envisioned by Indiaâs freedom fighters.

Venugopal urged Congress allies to respect the version of the national song adopted by the party in 1937, saying the decision to use only the first two stanzas at official party programmes was aimed at preventing the song from being âcommunalisedâ.

His remarks came after Jammu and Kashmir chief minister Omar Abdullah and National Conference president Farooq Abdullah stood through the full rendition of âVande Mataramâ at the inaugural International Film Festival in Srinagar.

The issue has also drawn criticism from the BJP, with Union home minister Amit Shah earlier targeting the Congress over its adherence to the 1937 position and accusing the party of pursuing appeasement politics.

World.title: Tamil Nadu Minister inaugurates completed development projects in Kallakurichi
World.content:
Minister for Social Justice Vanni Arasu on Wednesday inaugurated a slew of completed infrastructure projects worth ₹8.83 crore across Kallakurichi district and distributed welfare assistance to the tune of ₹4.87 crore to 455 beneficiaries.

The completed works, included additional classrooms for government schools, siddha wing buildings in primary health centres among other projects

The Minister also handed over financial assistance to the tune of ₹62.46 lakh to nine beneficiaries. Earlier, he inaugurated a hostel building constructed at a cost of ₹1.45 crore under the National Urban Livelihood Mission. He inspected the Kallakurichi Government Medical College and Hospital and reviewed the treatment and basic facilities.

Mr. Vanni Arasu also visited the Social Justice students hostel in Kallakurichi and inspected the quality of food and other amenities. Collector J.E. Padmaja was present.

World.title: 100 mobile toilets, 27 medical camps to be made available during Sri Meenakshi Sundareswarar Temple consecration ceremony
World.content:
Madurai Corporation has deployed dedicated conservancy and medical teams to ensure a safe and hygienic environment for devotees visiting the Sri Meenakshi Sundareswarar Temple for the consecration ceremony on September 17.

Corporation Commissioner Gaurav Kumar said 60 conservancy workers had been assigned exclusively to clean the temple surroundings.

To oversee the work, 24 Sanitary Inspectors had been given additional monitoring duties, including supervising 100 mobile toilets in addition to the 24 permanent toilets already existing in the area.

Each facility would have a dedicated attendant to clean it immediately after use and keep the restrooms comfortable for the public, he added.

For health and safety, 27 medical camps staffed with doctors and nurses would be set up across the temple region.

“The emergency response fleet will include 10 ‘108’ ambulances, two two-wheeler ambulances and eight mobile medical units,” Mr. Kumar said.

Further, 14 specialised medical teams would be stationed during the ceremony — seven on the roof near the puja area and seven on the ground level.

Mr. Kumar added that green corridors had also been established to ensure swift emergency transit and advanced life support for devotees who might fall ill.

One vehicle would be deployed for mosquito fogging operations and another would be used to remove accumulated sand and debris from the areas surrounding the temple.

The Corporation and temple administration currently possess a total of 360 wireless devices, comprising SIM-card-operated and high-frequency wireless devices. In the event of telecommunication network disruptions caused by heavy crowds, these devices would be provided to officials on duty to manage communications effectively, he said.

Moreover, notices had been served to owners of houses located in the Chithirai Street and Avani Moola Street areas, instructing them not to allow outsiders or unfamiliar persons into their houses on the day of the consecration to prevent crowd congestion.

Dilapidated and old houses in these areas had also been identified, and their owners had been informed to ensure that no outsiders entered them on that day. The police department had also been informed.

To facilitate vehicle parking, Mr. Kumar said, “Permissions are being obtained with the assistance of the police department to park vehicles at the parking lot near the Periyar Bus Stand and on vacant lands owned by private entities, and related works are under way.”

World.title: KTU Deputy Registrar suspended over Pookode lake beautification project in Keralam
World.content:
B. Anand, Deputy Registrar of the APJ Abdul Kalam Technological University, has been suspended from service in connection with a vigilance case registered over alleged financial irregularities in the Pookode lake beautification project in Wayanad.

The government had informed the university that Mr. Anand was named as the first accused in the case registered by the Vigilance and Anti-Corruption Bureau (VACB), and directed it to adopt action based on the recommendation.

At the time when the irregularities related to the case were reported, Mr. Anand was serving as the member secretary of the District Tourism Promotion Council (DTPC), Wayanad.

The VACB submitted a recommendation to the government that the official should remain suspended until the completion of the investigation, citing the possibility that he could influence witnesses or destroy evidence in a manner that could affect the probe.

The suspension will remain in effect until further orders or until the investigation into the vigilance case is completed.

World.title: Challenges in Telangana’s Indiramma houses construction, dilapidated housing societies in Hyderabad raised in Assembly
World.content:
Escalating cost of construction material which increases the expenditure for building an Indiramma House beyond the ₹5 lakh subsidy issued by Telangana government, difficulty in raising initial amount to lay foundation for the houses and the need for repairs or replacement of dilapidated housing societies in Hyderabad were brought up by MLAs on the fourth day of Telangana Legislative Assembly session.

Responding to them, Housing and Revenue Minister Ponguleti Srinivas Reddy said on Thursday (September 10, 2026) that an MoU was recently signed to provide 50kg cement bags for ₹230 to people for construction, instead of market price of ₹ 310-320. Soon, a similar measure will be taken for steel.

While 4.5 lakh houses would be provided under the first phase of Indiramma, 2.5 lakh houses would be provided under the second phase with 2,000 in each constituency.

All India Majlis-e-Ittehadul Muslimeen (AIMIM) Floor Leader Akbaruddin Owaisi said that new buildings were required in place of a few existing housing societies in the city as they were dilapidated. Responding to this, Mr. Reddy said that the replacement is needed in some housing societies.

Munugode MLA Komatireddy Rajagopal Reddy said that construction of an Indiramma house takes not less than ₹10 lakh as the material cost has increased and people have decried taking loans or mortgaging property to raise money for construction. He asked if more than ₹5 lakh subsidy would be provided, when other MLAs contended that modest houses can be built with the subsidy amount.

The Housing Minister said that there are nearly 59,000 huts across the State and the Cabinet has decided to make TG hut-free. People living in such houses were given priority under the second phase of Indiramma. Out of the 2,000 houses in each constituency under the second phase, 500 would be sanctioned to people who have already started constructing houses with their own money but left it midway. He assured that the government would examine if the subsidy is insufficient.

Regarding the issue in raising the initial amount, he said that an advance amount of ₹1 lakh is provided by Self Help Groups (SHG) if beneficiaries are members.

He said that nearly 3,200 houses construction were stalled due to various reasons. The issue would be addressed by end of the week.

While ₹22,500 crore is needed for the 4.5 lakh houses under the first phase, ₹11,000 for 2.5 lakh houses under the second phase and ₹5,500 crore for the one lakh houses proposed to be constructed in Hyderabad (CURE) limits. Altogether, the government would bear expenditure of ₹39,000 crore for the eight lakh houses. The government is positive to provide houses under third and fourth phases too, the Minister said.

World.title: Drop plan for Tamil Nadu Secretariat at Pattinapakkam, CPI urges State government
World.content:
CPI State secretary M. Veerapandian on Thursday (September 10, 2026), has urged the Tamil Nadu government to immediately drop its plan to construct a new Secretariat at Pattinapakkam (Foreshore Estate) in Chennai, citing concerns over the livelihood rights of fishermen, the marine environment, climate change, people’s access to the beach and the security of the government administration.

In a statement, he said nine fisher hamlets including Srinivasapuram, Rajiv Gandhi Nagar, Bhavani Kuppam, Selvarajapuram, Duming Kuppam, Notchi Nagar and Notchi Kuppam were located around the proposed site for the Secretariat.

Loss of fisherfolk habitation, livelihood

“The people in these hamlets depend on the sea not just for habitation. The sea is the fount of their livelihood, general wealth, fishing, movement of boats, unloading of fish, drying of fishing nets and fish, and storage,” he said.

Mr. Veerapandian, whose party provides outside support to the government, said the creation of such a mammoth administrative complex, along with roads, parking spaces and security infrastructure, would affect the seashore, which was already facing a space crunch. “Around 1,500 families will be forced to relocate and their livelihood will be at stake,” he pointed out.

The CPI leader said the proposed new Secretariat-Assembly complex, with high-security arrangements, movement of vehicles carrying VIPs and deployment of police personnel, would soon turn the area into a controlled zone dominated by security and administrative infrastructure.

Climate change risks, Olive Ridley turtle nesting ground

“Moreover, it is dangerous to create a Secretariat when the globe is facing a climate change emergency. Chennai’s seashores are being affected by storms, floods, high tides and rising sea levels. The government should opt for a safe place,” he said.

Mr. Veerapandian also said the proposed site was a nesting ground for Olive Ridley turtles. “Just naming it a green complex will not make it safe for the environment,” he stated.

World.title: Bengaluru-Karwar-Goa Ganapati Special train on September 11
World.content:
The South Western Railway will operate one round trip of a Ganapati special train service between Yeshwantpur in Bengaluru and Karwar in coastal Karnataka, and further to Madgaon in Goa, to clear the extra rush of passengers during the festival season. The services will be operated on September 11 and 14.

According to a notification from the SWR, Train No. 06591 Yeshwantpur-Karwar-Madgaon Festival Special (train on demand) will depart from Bengaluru on Friday September 11 at 11.55 p.m. and reach Karwar at 4.50 p.m. on Saturday September 12. The train will reach Madgaon at 6.10 p.m.

On the return trip, Train No. 06592 Madgaon-Bengaluru Cantonment Festival Special will leave Madgaon in Goa at 11 a.m. on September 14, and Karwar at 12 noon to reach Bengaluru Cantonment at 5.20 a.m. on September 15.

The two services will have commercial halts in Kunigal, Channarayapatna, Hassan, Sakleshpur, Subrahmanya Road, Kabaka Puttur, Bantwal, Surathkal, Mulki, Udupi, Barkur, Kundapura, Byndoor, Bhatkal, Murudeshwar, Honnavar, Kumta, Gokarna Road, Ankola, Karwar, and Canacona. However, Train No. 06592 Madgaon-Bengaluru Cantonment Festival Special, would not halt at Yeshwantpur; it would reach Sir M Visvesvaraya Terminal, Bengaluru, before terminating at Cantonment.

The train comprises one 2-tier AC, three 3-Tier AC, 10 second class sleeper, four general second class, and two luggage-cum-brake van coaches.

Udupi-Chikkamagaluru Member of Parliament Kota Srinivas Poojary, who had demanded the festival special, thanked the Railway Ministry for operating the special service.

World.title: Street vendors urged to stop using polythene bags in Thoothukudi
World.content:
Thoothukudi Corporation Mayor Jegan Periyasamy has urged the street vendors to stop using polythene bags, at a loan mela organised under the PM SVANidhi scheme at the Corporation office premises on Thursday.

Corporation Commissioner S. Priyanka presided over the event. Mr. Jegan distributed loan sanction orders and identity cards to 100 street vendors.

Speaking at the event, the Mayor said applications had been received from 9,224 eligible street vendors across all 60 wards of the corporation. Of these, loans had been sanctioned to 7,846 vendors, while 7,593 vendors had received the loans so far.

He added under the scheme street vendors are provided loans of ₹15,000 in the first tranche, ₹25,000 in second tranche and ₹50,000 in third tranche through banks. Identity cards are also being issued to the street vendors by the corporation and so far 1,864 vendors had received while 500 more identity cards have been issued recently.

The Mayor noted the financial assistance had helped improve the business and livelihood of street vendors and had been particularly useful in helping them avoid high-interest loans from private lenders.

He urged the vendors to repay the loans regularly, and advised them to conduct their businesses only in spaces allotted to them and not cause inconvenience to the public.

He further urged them to stop the usage of polythene bags, highlighting the impacts of those bags and cooperate with the civic body in keeping the eco-system clean and green..

World.title: Assistant engineer held for  accepting bribe, suspended
World.content:
A woman assistant engineer of the Thiruppullani Panchayat Union was suspended from service for accepting a bribe of ₹3,000 to issue a permit for extracting silt from a water tank.

Sheik Dilshad Parveen, an Assistant Engineer of the Thiruppullani Panchayat Union in Ramanathapuram district, allegedly demanded a bribe of ₹5,000 from a farmer to extract silt for agricultural use from a local tank.

Following this, while she was accepting a bribe of ₹3,000 at her residence in Sethupathi Nagar near the Ramanathapuram Collectorate on August 29 Ramanathapuram Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption (DVAC) police caught her red-handed and arrested her.

She was subsequently produced before a court and jailed. In this connection, Ramanathapuram District Collector M. Sivaguru Prabhakaran issued orders suspending the Assistant Engineer.

World.title: IMF mission due on Sept 23 for biannual review of Pakistan’s economic performance
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: An International Monetary Fund (IMF) mission is due to visit Pakistan on September 23 for a biannual review of the country’s economic performance and implementation of the $7 billion Extended Fund Facility (EFF) and the $1.4bn Resilience and Sustainability Facility (RSF) for the period ending June 30, 2026.

Pakistan is currently under a $7 billion, 37-month IMF programme , aimed at stabilising the economy through fiscal discipline, structural reforms, and measures to support long-term growth.

Official sources said that during an almost two-week visit ending in the first week of October, the IMF staff mission, led by Iva Petrova, would conduct the fourth review of the EFF and the third review of the RSF.

The mission would begin its visit with technical discussions at the State Bank of Pakistan, followed by meetings with the government’s sectoral teams, alongside a customary inaugural meeting with Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb.

The engagement would also examine policy implementation at the start of the fiscal year, particularly the Federal Board of Revenue’s (FBR) ability and preparedness to meet its first-ever half-yearly revenue collection structural benchmark under an IMF programme, given the revenue machinery’s repeated large annual shortfalls.

This would also be the first review after the provincial governments surrendered more than Rs1.035 trillion of their National Finance Commission (NFC) shares to the Centre during the current fiscal year for national security and water resources, on top of the Rs1.8tr cash surplus separately committed under IMF pressure.

The programme’s performance against the fiscal targets as of end-June 2026 — the period under review — has mostly been on track, albeit with a major revenue shortfall and slippages in the policy matrix. These include the government’s intervention in commodity operations, particularly wheat and sugar, in violation of an IMF condition requiring the government to keep its hands off the commodities market.

Given the biannual reviews of the $7bn EFF and the $1.4bn RSF, the two sides will have to agree on past performance as well as forward-looking implementation plans.

Upon successful completion of the review, Pakistan will be eligible for the disbursement of about $1bn (760 million Special Drawing Rights) under the EFF and another $200m under the RSF by the end of November or early December.

Official reports suggest that while qualitative performance criteria on the fiscal and monetary sides were mostly on track, progress on economic governance reforms lagged far behind requirements. They suggested that only a couple of targets out of more than three dozen for improving economic governance during the January-June 2026 period had been met.

These targets were set by the prime minister after the IMF’s governance and corruption diagnostic assessment found serious shortcomings in efforts to combat corruption.

While the government had introduced reforms to ensure transparent procurement processes in state-owned entities (SOEs), direct contracting with SOEs without open competitive bidding continued unabated.

There were also reports of agencies issuing tenders after projects had been completed through preferred contractors, compromising competitive pricing and transparency. The rules aimed at ending such preferential treatment have yet to be passed.

Earlier in July, an IMF representative hailed Pakistan’s “strong” economic reforms carried out under the lender’s $7 billion loan programme.

IMF’s Resident Representative for Pakistan Mahir Binici noted that the country’s performance under the 2024 EFF had been “strong so far”, according to a press release issued by the SDPI on its guest lecture in Islamabad.

World.title: FO says Makkah defence pact 'defensive' in nature, expansion currently 'not on the cards'
World.content:
The Foreign Office (FO) said on Thursday that the Makkah Defence Alliance between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye was “defensive” in nature, adding that expansion of the pact was currently “not on the cards”.

FO spokesperson Sajjad Haider Khan made the remarks while addressing a weekly press briefing. He said that the pact was primarily a “defensive alliance to ensure regional security primarily through deterrence”.

He said that expansion of the pact was currently “not on the cards”, adding that “Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye must first further consolidate their organisation and cooperation”.

He said that following the consolidation, the agreement will be “open to all countries that share similar stances and perspectives”.

The spokesperson said that the three member states were holding consultations at various levels under the framework.

He reiterated that the states will make a decision on the agreement’s expansion at a later stage.

“At this stage, there are no discussions regarding the expansion of the Makkah agreement,” he said.

He said information on future meetings will be shared “on an ongoing basis”, adding that exact timing was not yet known.

Khan said the pact was in the initial stage of formation and detailed consultations on “its structure, procedures and other matters” will be held.

“Significant work lies ahead to finalise the organisation’s structure, mechanisms, and procedures,” he said, adding that any future developments will become clear in due course.

The defence pact , signed on Aug 7, aims to strengthen collective deterrence and empower its signatory states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all of them.

Its inaugural meeting was held on August 31 in Istanbul, where it was decided that a secretariat headed by a secretary general will be established in Saudi Arabia to support the alliance’s work under the agreement. The secretariat will initially be headed by a secretary general from Pakistan for a period of three years.

‘State-sanctioned’ demolition of Muslim worship sites in India condemned

The FO spokesperson also condemned what he described as the “systematic” and “state-sanctioned” demolition of Muslim worship sites in India.

In response to a question about how Pakistan planned to build more pressure on the Indian government regarding the issue of demolition of worship sites, given the demolition of a mosque in India’s Saharanpur on September 5, the spokesperson said, “Pakistan expresses deep concern and condemns the systematic state-sanctioned demolition of Islamic holy places in India under different pretexts”.

Khan held that the demolitions were in breach of the Liaquat-Nehru Pact signed in 1950, which the spokesperson said guaranteed the security and rights of religious minorities.

He noted that the ongoing repression also breached India’s own laws, particularly the Places of Worship Special Provisions Act, 1991, which he said mandated the maintenance of the religious character of places of worship “as it existed on August 15, 1947”.

Referring to the recent demolition of a mosque in Uttar Pradesh, he noted: “The Hindu-driven Islamophobic campaign has resulted in an imminent threat and the destruction of centuries-old heritage sites and places of worship, including the Akhonji, Ajgaib Shaeed Mosque, the Saharanapur Collectorate mosque, as well as the 1,000-year-old mosque, Ganj Shahida mosque, which has recently received notices from the court.”

He recalled that the 1992 demolition of the Babri mosque remained a “dreadful memory of this ideology of religious intolerance, prejudice, and hatred”.

Explaining what steps Pakistan planned to take towards the issue, Khan said, “Pakistan calls upon the international community to take immediate notice of this systematic persecution in India against Muslims and continued desecration and destruction of their places of worship”.

In the weekly briefing, Khan also issued a categorical rejection of a statement made by the Indian Ministry of External Affairs over a Hindu temple in Narowal.

“Contrary to India’s claim, the temple’s structure was damaged in torrential rain,” he said.

Yasin Malik’s decision to forgo defence ‘damning indictment’ of Indian judicial system

The spokesperson was also asked about the recent implication of the Jammu Kashmir Liberation Front (JKLF)’s incarcerated chairman, Muhammad Yasin Malik, in a case from 1990.

Malik was named in June by India’s State Investigation Agency (SIA) as one of five men charged with the killing of Sarla Bhat. However, he submitted an affidavit stating that he had decided not to contest the trial and that his decision should not be treated as an admission of guilt or acceptance of the prosecution’s allegations.

Referring to Malik’s action, the FO said, “The stance taken by Yasin Malik is beyond an act of heroism. It is a damning indictment of the Indian judicial system, which has acted as a convenient tool in the hands of the Indian government, suppressing the Kashmiri people and depriving them of any recourse to justice”.

Khan held that in repudiating the right to defence, Malik has “struck a stinging blow to the judicial sham that the Indian government wanted to stage in its sinister campaign to malign the Kashmiri leadership”.

The spokesperson also expressed concern at Malik’s deteriorating health.

“The international community must not allow the Indian design to mortgage his life and well-being to advance its oppressive occupation of the IIOK,” he said, adding that Pakistan condemned the prosecution of Malik.

The FO spokesperson urged the UN and other humanitarian bodies to take note of Malik’s situation.

World.title: NA panel irked over poor mobile services, seeks efforts to bring Apple to Pakistan
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The National Assembly Standing Committee on Information Technology and Telecommunication on Thursday expressed serious concern over the poor quality of mobile and internet services and decided to summon telecom companies (telcos) to seek direct answers over persistent network problems.

The committee was also informed by an official of the Engineering Development Board (EDB) that efforts were underway to seek tech giant Apple’s entry into Pakistan’s manufacturing market.

In its proceedings, the committee expressed concerns over the quality of mobile services, with chairman Aminul Haque remarking that subscribers had to dial a number three times just to make a call.

“The quality of mobile and internet services is deteriorating day by day after the spectrum auction instead of any improvement,” the Muttahida Qaumi Movement-Pakistan (MQM-P) lawmaker said.

The chairman then questioned the PTA about the fines imposed during the last six months, noting that the regulator issued show-cause notices and warning letters, but did not impose sufficient fines on telecom companies.

Committee members Zulfiqar Ali Bhatti, Ahmad Ateeq Anwar, Sadiq Memon and Dr Mahesh Kumar stressed that the root causes of poor mobile service were not being addressed and criticised the PTA for repeatedly giving the same response without improving the situation.

Committee member Shazia Fareed recalled she had received virtually no mobile signals during her stay at Islamabad’s Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (Pims).

The committee made it clear that the PTA should perform its duties and inform the parliament if there was any obstacle preventing it from taking action. Members proposed summoning representatives of telcos and seeking explanations from them directly.

Meanwhile, PTA officials assured the committee that the authority continuously monitored mobile and internet services and conducted surveys in cities to assess service quality.

They said telcos were given 30 days to improve their service quality and networks, while the PTA could impose a maximum fine of Rs350 million.

PTA officials further said that telcos often obtained stay orders from courts against penalties, and that several cases were pending before the courts. They added that the Telecom Tribunal was functional, but its decisions had also been challenged before courts.

The authority maintained that service quality was improving after the launch of 5G and that rollout targets for telcos had been clearly defined. A PTA member informed the committee that the number of 5G sites in Karachi was increasing and had reached 279.

IT Secretary Zarar Hasham Khan told the committee that telcos had installed equipment meeting international standards, and the government had prioritised improved service quality over revenue generation during the 5G spectrum auction held in March.

The committee decided to summon telcos at its next meeting and directed the PTA to provide details of fines imposed on them and the amount recovered.

Committee seeks efforts for Apple’s entry in Pakistan

The committee also discussed efforts to bring Apple to Pakistan, with Haque questioning why the tech giant could not enter the country’s market when other international mobile companies were already operating.

EDB Chief Executive Officer Hammad Mansoor told the committee that negotiations were under way to bring Apple into the country.

He added that efforts were also being made to arrange a meeting between Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Apple CEO John Ternus during the former’s upcoming visit to the United States.

Mansoor said that an Apple store had already been established in Pakistan and expressed optimism that the company would also enter the country’s manufacturing market.

The EDB chief informed the committee that 37 companies were currently manufacturing mobile phones in Pakistan, and that more than 35 million devices had been manufactured locally so far.

The committee was told that all major smartphone companies were manufacturing phones in Pakistan, except Apple.

Haq directed the IT ministry and the PTA to come prepared with detailed information at the next meeting, and to continue efforts to bring Apple to Pakistan.

Mobile phone tax issue discussed

The committee also discussed the issue of taxes on imported mobile phones, and the potential payment of levies in instalments.

A PTA member clarified that the authority had no role in placing mobile phone taxes or in developing a mechanism for payment of such taxes in instalments, as all the tax matters were the domain of the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR).

Committee member Syed Ali Qasim Gilani said he raised the issue and also took up the matter of allowing consumers to pay the tax in instalments.

He said the FBR had informed him that the mechanism was available with the PTA, but questioned how the authority could develop an instalment mechanism when it did not collect the tax.

The IT secretary said the issue of mobile phone tax instalments was not in his knowledge and assured the committee that he would discuss it with the PTA chairman and brief the committee, which sought a detailed briefing on the matter at its next meeting.

“Our vision should be smartphones for all,” Haque said, pointing out that a good quality phone was available in Pakistan for around Rs60,000.

Telecom sector seeks industrial tariff

Additionally, the committee also discussed the issue of electricity supplied to telecom infrastructure and the demand for industrial tariffs for telecom companies.
