World.title: Russian Orthodox Church calls on pilgrims to ‘boycott’ New Athos Monastery in Abkhazia
World.content:
The Russian Orthodox Church (ROC) has called on pilgrims not to visit the New Athos Monastery in Abkhazia.

The ROC considers the monastery’s abbot, Father Dorotheus, a schismatic.

However, this did not stop Sergei Kiriyenko, first deputy chief of staff of the Russian presidential administration and the Kremlin’s point man for Abkhazia, from visiting the monastery.

The Moscow Patriarchate’s chancellor, Metropolitan Grigory, has sent a circular letter to all bishops of the Russian Orthodox Church warning that Russian pilgrims must not attend services at the New Athos Monastery. The services there are led by defrocked hieromonk Dorotheus (Dbar).

“We are concerned about cases in which Orthodox pilgrims from dioceses of the Russian Orthodox Church visit the New Athos Monastery and take part in services held there. Pilgrims often go to confession and receive communion there without knowing that they should not.

I ask you to take measures to ensure that pilgrims travelling to holy sites in Abkhazia with your blessing are always informed that they must not engage in prayer or Eucharistic communion with the monk Dorotheus. They should also be informed that the sacraments performed in schism have no spiritual grace,” Metropolitan Grigory wrote.

Archimandrite Dorotheus

Archimandrite Dorotheus heads the Holy Metropolis of Abkhazia, one of two unrecognised Orthodox churches operating in the republic. A graduate of Aristotle University of Thessaloniki in Greece and a doctor of theology, he is highly popular in Abkhaz society and well known in church circles.

His “rival” is Father Vissarion, who heads the Abkhazian Orthodox Church (AOC). He is the only serving Abkhaz cleric ordained by the Georgian Orthodox Church during the Soviet era. Despite its unrecognised status, the AOC enjoys the active support of the Russian Orthodox Church.

The ROC, by contrast, has opposed Archimandrite Dorotheus and officially defrocked him in 2023 for refusing to submit to its authority.

The Holy Metropolis of Abkhazia and the AOC have been engaged in a long-running and bitter conflict.

Father Vissarion has also addressed not Russian but Abkhaz believers, saying they should not take part in services at New Athos.

Father Dorotheus himself believes that the Moscow Patriarchate’s letter was prompted by Archpriest Nikolai Balashov, an adviser to Patriarch Kirill of Moscow and All Russia. According to Dorotheus, Balashov has consistently worked in the interests of the Georgian Orthodox Church for decades.

“Similar circulars have appeared repeatedly. Yet their authors stubbornly refuse to acknowledge the main point: pilgrims who visit the New Athos Monastery are not there ‘out of ignorance’. The overwhelming majority of them knowingly take part in the services I conduct.

These people know the church bureaucracy well and can see that it contains no spiritual truth — only political and administrative manipulation,” Father Dorotheus wrote on his social media page.

Dorotheus believes another factor also prompted the AOC leadership to step up its activity. On 28 August 2026, Abkhaz President Badra Gunba and Sergei Kiriyenko, first deputy chief of staff of the Russian presidential administration, made an unofficial visit to the New Athos Monastery.

According to Dorotheus, this was the first time since 2011 that such high-ranking officials had visited their monastery.

The terminology, place names and views expressed in this article are those of the author and do not necessarily reflect the editorial position of this website.

Boycott of the New Athos Monastery

World.title: Georgian ‘delegation’ delivers gifts to Russian unit fighting against Ukraine
World.content:
According to Russia’s RIA Novosti news agency, Georgian volunteers on a “humanitarian mission” in the so-called Donetsk People’s Republic delivered an icon of St George the Victorious, motorcycles and prayer rooms to a Russian unit named after St Gabriel Urgebadze and the Nevsky Brigade, which are fighting against Ukraine. Besik Danelia, a Georgian “public figure” who leads the volunteers, told the agency about the initiative.

The Georgian Orthodox Church strongly opposes the use of Archimandrite Gabriel Urgebadze’s name to justify or support military action. Archpriest Andria Jaghmaidze, head of the Georgian Patriarchate’s press service, said it was particularly unacceptable that some Russian Orthodox Church clergy had supported the initiative.

Father Gabriel (Urgebadze) was a Georgian Orthodox monk and archimandrite whom the Georgian Orthodox Church canonised as a saint. One of the best-known episodes of his life took place in 1965, during the Soviet era. During a 1 May demonstration, he publicly burned a huge portrait of Lenin. Authorities beat him severely, arrested him and sent him to a psychiatric hospital. Later, despite pressure and persecution from the authorities, he continued his church service. His life became associated with strict asceticism, helping others and the idea of love.

What is known about the unit named after Father Gabriel and Besik Danelia

In an interview with RIA Novosti, Besik Danelia said he had travelled to Donetsk to visit “brothers” who, according to him, “are defending their homeland on the front line”, and had brought them humanitarian aid.

Andrei Kramar, a representative of the de facto authorities in occupied Donetsk, also said that a “Georgian delegation” that openly supports Russia’s war had visited the region.

“A Georgian delegation came to us and brought humanitarian aid. They are doing this openly. They are proud to support and have chosen a side in the special military operation,” Kramar said.

Reports about the existence of a “Orthodox” unit named after Father Gabriel Urgebadze and made up of ethnic Georgians first emerged in January 2026.

Besik Danelia (right) in Donetsk. Photo: press service of Andrei Kramar, deputy chairman of the so-called DPR’s People’s Council

Besik Danelia was previously a member of Nino Burjanadze’s pro-Russian Democratic Movement – United Georgia party. He has also appeared on the Georgia Wave media platform, which is linked to Putin supporter Mamuka Pipia, where he echoed the Georgian Dream ruling party’s calls for an apology to Georgia’s occupied regions.

Georgian “delegation” in Donetsk

What the Georgian Patriarchate says

The Georgian Patriarchate says that using the name of Archimandrite Gabriel Urgebadze for a military unit is particularly incompatible with his legacy.

Archpriest Andria Jaghmaidze: “First of all, let us note that Orthodox people are dying on both sides of the Russia-Ukraine war. We watch this with deep pain in our hearts. We pray and ask the saints to intercede so that the Lord may grant peace to Ukraine, Russia and the whole world. And at such a time, without any consultation with the Georgian Orthodox Church or consideration of its position, we have unexpectedly encountered an unprecedented situation.

For us, it is categorically unacceptable to use the name of the Venerable Father Gabriel, an archimandrite, confessor and holy fool, for a military unit. The life and spiritual struggle of the saint were entirely devoted to faith in our Lord Jesus Christ and to preaching love and compassion for others.

It is also deeply disturbing that some clergy of the Russian Church support such an unacceptable use of the Venerable Father’s name.

It appears that the authors of this initiative are poorly acquainted with the life of Saint Gabriel. Against this background, this action appears to be a biased attempt to exploit the name of the Church.

The Georgian Orthodox Church distances itself from the use of the name of the Venerable Gabriel the Confessor and Holy Fool to justify or support military action.”

Gabriel Urgebadze unit

World.title: From ‘crown prince’ to prisoner: Irakli Garibashvili’s break with Georgia’s ruling party
World.content:
Irakli Garibashvili vs Georgian Dream

Georgia’s two-time former Prime Minister Irakli Garibashvili is currently in prison, from where he has openly challenged the authorities he himself represented for many years.

Over the past few weeks, he has published six letters accusing the Georgian government of persecution, blackmail and attempts to destroy his political future.

Garibashvili initially said the pressure against him had been exerted on the orders of Bidzina Ivanishvili, the founder and honorary chairman of the ruling Georgian Dream party. His criticism, however, later focused primarily on current Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze and another influential party figure, Mamuka Mdinaradze.

The confrontation is particularly unusual for a party that for many years appeared from the outside to be an entirely monolithic political organisation.

Irakli Garibashvili is far from an ordinary former official. For almost two decades, he was one of Bidzina Ivanishvili‘s closest and most trusted associates. When Ivanishvili stepped down as prime minister in 2013, he effectively installed the then 31-year-old Garibashvili as his successor.

Now Ivanishvili’s former chosen successor is writing from prison that the very system he once served has “stabbed him in the back”.

Garibashvili’s case is therefore no longer simply a criminal case involving a former prime minister. It has exposed a conflict within Georgian Dream and raised a broader question: is a new redistribution of power beginning within the ruling party?

From prime minister’s office to prison cell

Irakli Garibashvili’s career under Bidzina Ivanishvili’s wing began long before Georgian Dream came to power in 2012.

As early as 2011, Ivanishvili referred to Garibashvili as one of his closest advisers and aides.

Following Georgian Dream’s victory in the 2012 parliamentary election, Garibashvili became interior minister. A year later, Ivanishvili stepped down as prime minister and named Garibashvili as his successor.

Garibashvili consequently served his first term as Georgia’s prime minister from 2013 to 2015. He unexpectedly left government at the end of 2015, but returned in 2019 as defence minister. In 2021, he became prime minister for a second time.

During his second premiership, Garibashvili was one of Georgian Dream’s most hardline figures. He frequently clashed with the opposition, civil society and Western critics. Following Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine, Garibashvili repeatedly echoed the government’s narrative about the threat of a “second front” being opened in Georgia and accused some Western figures of supporting the opposition.

In January 2024, he again stepped down as prime minister and was replaced by Irakli Kobakhidze. Garibashvili, meanwhile, became chairman of Georgian Dream. At the time, the party presented the change as a routine internal reshuffle.

In April 2025, Garibashvili announced that he was leaving politics altogether.

Several months later, a criminal investigation was launched against him.

How former prime minister ended up in prison

In October 2025, prosecutors charged Irakli Garibashvili with laundering a particularly large amount of illicit income.

According to investigators, the former prime minister provided false information in his asset declarations in an attempt to make illegally obtained income appear legitimate.

At the time, Garibashvili chose to remain silent and did not contest the case. On 12 January 2026, he pleaded guilty and reached a plea agreement with prosecutors. Under the deal, he was sentenced to five years in prison and fined 1m lari ($360,000). Two of his cars and $6.5m seized during a search of his home were also forfeited to the state.

After being taken into custody in the courtroom, Garibashvili was transferred directly to Penitentiary Establishment No 12 in the city of Rustavi.

Garibashvili later gave an almost sacred significance to his decision to remain silent. He now says that, at the time, he had consciously chosen not to confront the authorities.

Garibashvili and Ivanishvili: relationship spanning almost 20 years

Garibashvili worked in Ivanishvili’s circle even before Georgian Dream was founded. When Ivanishvili entered politics in 2011, Garibashvili was one of his closest associates. And, as noted above, in 2013 Ivanishvili handed him the leadership of the Georgian government.

Ivanishvili himself has often spoken about the early years of their personal relationship. In 2013, he recalled that Garibashvili had worked in the commercial department of one of his companies when Ivanishvili was buying a French-made helicopter. According to Ivanishvili, the young Garibashvili handled the negotiations with the French side so successfully that the sellers wanted to meet him in person.

In Georgian political circles, their relationship was widely seen as one between a patron and his political successor. Government opponents even described Garibashvili as Ivanishvili’s “obedient servant”, while Georgian media frequently portrayed him as a politician “groomed” by Ivanishvili and as being as close to him “as a son”.

Another episode also illustrates the hierarchical nature of their relationship.

In 2021, when Garibashvili was serving his second term as Georgia’s prime minister, a video recording of Bidzina Ivanishvili giving evidence in a Bermuda court was made public. The case concerned Ivanishvili’s legal dispute with Swiss bank Credit Suisse.

In court, Ivanishvili was asked what role Garibashvili had played in his financial affairs years earlier. Ivanishvili explained that Garibashvili had not been a financier and had mainly performed organisational tasks, such as arranging meetings, making phone calls and handling similar matters.

Asked, “So was he something like your secretary?”, Ivanishvili laughed and replied: “Call him whatever you like. Use whichever description you prefer.”

Following the release of the recording, political commentators highlighted the fact that Ivanishvili had twice appointed as the country’s prime minister a former subordinate whose earlier duties he had described in court in dismissive terms.

Ivanishvili mentioned in Garibashvili’s letter from prison

Against this backdrop, Garibashvili’s first public reference to Ivanishvili in a letter from prison, published on 17 August 2026, was particularly significant.

Garibashvili wrote that he had received an offer made on Ivanishvili’s instructions: to confess to another offence, this time a serious corruption crime. In return, he said he had been promised that the new charge would not add to his existing five-year prison sentence.

According to the former prime minister, the deal came with another condition: after his release from prison, he would not be allowed to return to politics.

Garibashvili said the authorities were seeking to ensure that he could not make a political comeback. In the same statement, he held Ivanishvili and the Georgian Dream leadership personally responsible for his own safety and that of his family.

In his next letter, Garibashvili again referred to Ivanishvili, but this time in a markedly different tone.

He wrote that he had endured the authorities’ actions for many months because of his “20-year relationship with Bidzina Ivanishvili, immense love and respect for him, boundless gratitude and absolute loyalty to him“.

In subsequent letters, Garibashvili has sought gradually to shift the focus of the conflict away from Ivanishvili and towards the Kobakhidze-Mdinaradze tandem.

Some analysts believe Garibashvili is trying to avoid burning his remaining bridges with Ivanishvili and to persuade him that the real problem lies with the current prime minister and his circle.

Garibashvili, his wife Nunuka Tamazashvili and Bidzina Ivanishvili

Irakli Kobakhidze and Irakli Garibashvili

What changed after Garibashvili‘s letters

After 17 August, Garibashvili definitively broke his silence.

Several key allegations gradually emerged from his letters. He claims that the authorities deceived him, put pressure on members of his family, demanded that he confess to another corruption offence, and ultimately sought to eliminate any possibility of his return to politics.

Garibashvili also said that he had been given indications that his 75-year-old father could also be arrested.

Mamuka Mdinaradze rejected these allegations.

However, subsequent developments lent additional weight to Garibashvili’s claims.

On 24 August, prosecutors brought new charges against him.

This time, the case concerns the alleged receipt of a particularly large bribe, an offence punishable by between 11 and 15 years in prison if he is convicted.

According to prosecutors, Garibashvili received 750,000 lari ($275,735) through a scheme involving classified procurement contracts at the Defence Ministry. The investigation relies primarily on testimony from former Defence Minister Juansher Burchuladze and his alleged accomplice, Vasil Mkheidze.

Garibashvili has pleaded not guilty to the new charge.

The former prime minister says the proceedings are being used as a tool to exert political pressure on him.

Mdinaradze’s sudden departure

Meanwhile, against the backdrop of Garibashvili’s letters and his allegations against Kobakhidze and Mdinaradze, another significant development took place:

Mamuka Mdinaradze and Irakli Kobakhidze

Mamuka Mdinaradze, who for many years was one of Georgian Dream’s most influential figures and one of Kobakhidze’s closest political allies, announced that he was leaving the government and withdrawing from politics altogether.

In 2025, Mdinaradze was appointed head of the State Security Service, but remained in the post for only a short time. In July 2026, Irakli Kobakhidze announced that Mdinaradze would become regional development minister in September and was expected to play a key role in overseeing regional policy.

However, on 27 August, Mdinaradze unexpectedly announced that he was not only stepping down from his ministerial post but leaving politics altogether.

Garibashvili linked the move to his letters.

“Mamuka Mdinaradze made such serious and grave mistakes in this case that they resulted not only in his removal from office, but also in his departure from politics,” the disgraced former prime minister wrote on 2 September in his fifth letter.

Mdinaradze himself presented his departure as a personal decision.

Why Garibashvili has become a problem for Kobakhidze

Garibashvili’s letters have raised questions about how much political influence the former prime minister retains while in prison. Some analysts believe Garibashvili still has supporters within Georgian Dream and that the authorities’ sharp response to his letters is evidence of his continuing political significance.

Conflict analyst Paata Zakareishvili says Garibashvili realised that he enjoyed greater sympathy within Georgian Dream than Kobakhidze did, and that this encouraged him to continue resisting.

Kobakhidze, Zakareishvili argues, in turn discovered that “even Garibashvili sitting in prison is stronger than he is”.

One possible explanation for this assessment lies in the two men’s very different political backgrounds.

Garibashvili belongs to the first generation of the ruling party and has been part of Georgian Dream since its foundation. He was a member of Ivanishvili’s inner circle and built up strong political connections over the years, particularly in the regions.

Kobakhidze’s power, by contrast, is much more closely tied to the party apparatus and Ivanishvili’s direct backing.

Analyst Irakli Melashvili describes Garibashvili as a “symbolic figure” for supporters of the “old Georgian Dream”. In his assessment, the former prime minister was particularly close to the party’s conservative and pro-Russian electorate.

At the same time, Melashvili points to a fundamental contradiction: Garibashvili has now himself become a target of the system of which he was one of the principal architects and leaders for many years.

For that reason, his resistance cannot automatically be seen as a struggle for a democratic system.

“This is a struggle for his own survival, not for the public good,” Melashvili says.

Lazare Jorbenadze case and a new phase of confrontation

On 1 September, Garibashvili went a step further.

In another letter from prison, he demanded that the authorities provide answers about the circumstances surrounding the death of human rights activist Lazare Jorbenadze, who had publicly criticised Kobakhidze.

Garibashvili also wrote that questions remained unanswered about other cases of suicide which, he said, were linked to the period when the Kobakhidze-Mdinaradze group was in power.

Prosecutors subsequently questioned Garibashvili himself, as well as several other politicians and public figures. A prosecution service representative said Garibashvili had provided no information to substantiate claims that Jorbenadze may have been murdered.

Sixth letter: open confrontation with authorities

On 8 September, Garibashvili published his sixth letter.

He described the authorities’ response as a “ridiculous, repulsive and tragic masquerade” and said the questioning over the Jorbenadze case was an attempt to link him to the opposition United National Movement party.

Garibashvili also responded sarcastically to allegations in pro-government media that he had been acting in the interests of the “deep state” or France.

“I am lucky that I don’t know any other foreign languages, otherwise I would probably have been declared an agent of other countries as well,” he wrote.

He then addressed the authorities directly: “Stop these dirty political games against me!”

Garibashvili said he served neither the West nor the East, neither the North nor the South, and that his sole aim had been to serve Georgia.

He addressed parliament speaker Shalva Papuashvili separately: “Shalva, this is not a legal process — this is ruthless political persecution!“

The letter ends with a message the former prime minister has repeatedly made in recent weeks:

“I am not fighting anyone — you yourselves stabbed me in the back… Now I am forced to defend myself and my family against this injustice and cruelty.”

‘Criminal’, ‘traitor’, ‘agent’: how party responded to former PM

Following Garibashvili’s fifth letter, Georgian Dream’s response became particularly harsh.

A man who twice served as prime minister for the party is now being described by his former allies as a “criminal” and a “traitor”.

A politician who for years himself used harsh rhetoric against government opponents has now become a target of the same system. The language being used against him will be familiar to the government’s critics: allegations of corruption, betrayal, serving the radical opposition and acting in the interests of foreign states.

Georgian Dream representatives say Garibashvili’s narrative has become indistinguishable from that of the “radical opposition”.

MP Gia Volski suggested that the former prime minister may have been led to believe that his struggle could help advance a “revolutionary process” in the country and that he could subsequently benefit from it politically.

Another MP, Dimitri Samkharadze, described Garibashvili as a “self-confessed criminal” and a traitor.

Meanwhile, pro-government television channels, citing Azerbaijani media, circulated allegations that Garibashvili had been acting in France’s interests in Georgia.

Current Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze also responded in exceptionally harsh terms.

He described his predecessor’s letters as “ridiculous and tragic”, saying Garibashvili had “sunk to the level of a blogger for some shady little newspaper”.

Georgian Dream secretary-general and Tbilisi mayor Kakha Kaladze, meanwhile, said it was regrettable to see his former ally in such a position, but publicly expressed his full support for Kobakhidze.

Ivanishvili remains silent

The key figure in the entire confrontation has so far remained largely out of public view.

Bidzina Ivanishvili has remained silent.

This is particularly notable because both sides in the conflict ultimately derived their political weight from his backing.

Political analyst Gia Khukhashvili sees one possible scenario in which Ivanishvili himself is managing the current process, with the ultimate aim of weakening Kobakhidze’s team.

Other analysts offer a more cautious interpretation: Ivanishvili is watching the confrontation unfold and will make a decision only when it becomes clear which figure is more useful for preserving his system.

David Zurabishvili, who supports this interpretation, says Ivanishvili has no permanent allies, only permanent interests. Accordingly, neither Garibashvili nor Kobakhidze is indispensable to him.

This explanation is also consistent with Georgian Dream’s history: prime ministers have changed repeatedly during the party’s time in power, while the centre of power has consistently remained with Ivanishvili.

Kobakhidze has no intention of stepping down

Against this backdrop, speculation is already mounting in Georgia over the possible resignation of Irakli Kobakhidze himself.

He has, however, dismissed the rumours.

Kobakhidze said journalists ask him “every three months” whether he is planning to step down as prime minister, adding that he expects to be asked the same question again in another three months.

More significant, however, was his explanation of what had happened within the government after he took office.

According to Kobakhidze, he and his team needed a year and five months to address what he described as “fundamental problems” that had accumulated within the system of government, acting on Bidzina Ivanishvili’s instructions.

Kobakhidze did not directly name Garibashvili in his remarks. The chronology, however, is clear: he was referring to problems that had accumulated in the system during his namesake’s tenure as prime minister.

Is Georgian Dream’s monolith beginning to crack?

Georgian Dream formally retains almost complete control over Georgia’s political system.

It dominates parliament, is seeking to ban several opposition groups, and many opposition leaders are in prison.

Yet it is under these circumstances that a conflict has erupted not between the government and the opposition, but between current and former leaders of the ruling establishment itself.

Giorgi Melashvili, head of the Europe-Georgia Institute, describes the situation as two parallel processes: on the one hand, the circle of decision-makers is narrowing and the system is becoming increasingly centralised; on the other, the Garibashvili case has exposed cracks in Georgian Dream’s internal monolith.

In his assessment, neither the opposition nor other former Georgian Dream figures have dealt the party a blow comparable to that inflicted by Garibashvili’s letters.

Gia Khukhashvili, meanwhile, describes the developments as a confrontation between two factions “at the royal court”. In his view, Ivanishvili remains the only person with the final say.

Much about these scenarios remains speculative, but the facts themselves already present a highly unusual picture:

Former PM behind bars: A two-time former prime minister is in prison, accusing the authorities of political persecution and his former allies of trying to destroy him and his family.

A two-time former prime minister is in prison, accusing the authorities of political persecution and his former allies of trying to destroy him and his family. New criminal case: Following his first letters, he was hit with a new and significantly more serious criminal charge.

Following his first letters, he was hit with a new and significantly more serious criminal charge. Mdinaradze’s sudden departure: One of his main opponents within the ruling team, Mamuka Mdinaradze, unexpectedly left politics altogether.

One of his main opponents within the ruling team, Mamuka Mdinaradze, unexpectedly left politics altogether. Question of succession: Current Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze is already having to publicly answer questions about whether he could become the “next former” prime minister.

And Bidzina Ivanishvili, who stands at the centre of all these developments, continues to remain silent.

World.title: ‘Major cause for concern’: expert view on Armenian school students’ low level of knowledge
World.content:
Low knowledge levels among Armenian school students

School students in Armenia lag behind their peers in Georgia, Azerbaijan and Turkey in terms of their level of knowledge. The comparison focuses in particular on 15-year-old students.

The Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) conducted its annual study as part of the Programme for International Student Assessment (PISA). Experts assessed students’ knowledge of mathematics and science, as well as their ability to analyse what they read.

The study included 760,000 15-year-old students from 91 countries. The results showed that the overall state of education around the world leaves much to be desired. However, experts in Armenia are particularly concerned about the situation in their own country. The education problems have also alarmed people far beyond the field’s specialist community.

Economist Tigran Jrbashyan sees the study’s results as a major cause for concern.

“This is no longer a problem for the education ministry. It is a question of Armenia’s economic security and long-term competitiveness,” he stressed.

Jrbashyan published several posts on his Facebook page, calling on the government to take immediate action. He proposes introducing a special regime in the education sector over the coming years.

Подробнее о результатах исследования, а также комментарий экономиста Тиграна Джрбашяна.

Results for students in Armenia and leading countries

According to the study, some cities in China lead the rankings for educational achievement, followed by Japan, South Korea, Singapore and Taiwan. The UK and Estonia also rank among the top 10.

Armenia’s results lag behind those of every other country in the region. Armenian school students scored below the OECD average in all areas covered by the study.

The average share of Armenian school students reaching the benchmark was

28% in science (OECD average — 74%),

28% in mathematics (OECD average — 65%),

19% in reading and the ability to analyse written text (OECD average — 67%).

Less than 1% of Armenian students achieved the highest level in mathematics, while the figure was even lower in science.

“And virtually none of the students demonstrated reading skills that would indicate an ability to understand lengthy texts, work with abstract or contradictory concepts, and distinguish facts from opinions,” Radio Azatutyun reports.

Comment

According to Tigran Jrbashyan, an economist and head of Ameriabank’s management consulting service, the PISA study assesses not so much what 15-year-olds know as their ability to apply their knowledge in practice: understanding texts, analysing information and solving problems.

“Among our 15-year-olds, 28% reach at least the minimum, Level 2 proficiency in mathematics. The figure is also 28% in science. In reading, however, only 19% reach this level. In other words, four out of five of our 15-year-olds do not even reach the basic level of functional reading literacy,” he said.

Meanwhile, according to the PISA study, 39% of teenagers in Georgia reach the basic level of reading literacy, compared with 36% in Kazakhstan and 35% in Azerbaijan.

The economist argues that no matter how much Armenia talks about its achievements in artificial intelligence and high technology, all its planned initiatives will remain unrealised projects without human capital.

“If Armenia ranks third from the bottom in problem-solving skills among 15-year-olds, our ambitions in AI and high technology cannot be limited to investment, equipment and infrastructure alone,” he explained.

Jrbashyan notes that Armenia has built, renovated and modernised schools in recent years. He considers this an unquestionable investment in the quality of education. At the same time, he says the country needs to change how it assesses the effectiveness of education policy.

In particular, he proposes assessing

how students’ reading skills and their mathematical and scientific knowledge have changed as a result of these investments;

whether the share of students who fail to reach the basic level has decreased;

whether the share of high-performing students has increased.

The analyst insists that, given the current situation, the government needs to

take immediate action to determine at which stage of the education system, and for what reasons, students lose ground;

set measurable targets for 2028 and 2031 and consistently work towards achieving them.

“The cost of inaction in the context of PISA is not simply a low ranking. It means lost economic growth and the loss of Armenia’s competitiveness for decades to come,” he stressed.

The expert believes the PISA 2025 results show that the scale of Armenia’s education problem has outgrown the pace of the government’s response. As a result, reforms carried out at the usual pace are no longer enough:

“I would propose declaring education an emergency national priority and introducing a special management regime for three to five years.”

Jrbashyan stresses that an emergency regime should mean not only faster decision-making and more resources, but also much greater accountability for results.

Moreover, he sees a need for national mobilisation on the issue. He believes education policy should not measure its success only through the next PISA study:

“We need to create a national system of regular assessment that will allow us to see every year where we are making progress and where we are not, and adjust policy accordingly.”

Low knowledge levels among Armenian school students

World.title: Opposition says Georgian authorities are hiding demands from de facto South Ossetian authorities
World.content:
The opposition party Gakharia for Georgia claims that the de facto authorities of the Tskhinvali region (South Ossetia) are demanding the removal of a Georgian police checkpoint near the village of Chorchana and the handover of the territory to them. The Georgian authorities have not informed the public about the demands.

The party’s statement followed the latest meeting under the Incident Prevention and Response Mechanism (IPRM) in the village of Ergneti.

After the meeting, Yegor Kochiev, head of the delegation representing the de facto authorities in Tskhinvali, said no agreement had yet been reached with official Tbilisi over the Chorchana checkpoint. However, he said the issue had been discussed “very seriously”.

“The only acceptable option is to remove this checkpoint and subsequently withdraw it from the territory of South Ossetia,” Kochiev said.

What the Gakharia for Georgia party claims

“The Tskhinvali occupation regime has once again aggressively demanded the removal of the Georgian police checkpoint in the village of Chorchana and, accordingly, the transfer of these Georgian territories to the occupation forces,” representatives of the Gakharia for Georgia party said. The party was founded by Giorgi Gakharia, a former interior minister and former prime minister of Georgia.

According to the party, the Tskhinvali side is trying to portray the territory around Chorchana as its own land, while the ruling Georgian Dream party remains silent and has not told the public either about Tskhinvali’s demands or its own position.

Gakharia for Georgia also criticised the government over the ongoing criminal case against Giorgi Gakharia, which the party believes is directly linked to the establishment of the Georgian police checkpoint in Chorchana.

“Instead of defending the national interest, Georgian Dream is putting Georgia’s former interior minister on trial for setting up a Georgian police checkpoint in Chorchana and protecting Georgian land from creeping occupation,” the party said in a statement.

The party called on the authorities to immediately tell the public about their plans for Chorchana, saying that removing the checkpoint would amount to handing Georgian territory over to the occupation forces.

Background

The police checkpoint near the village of Chorchana was established in August 2019, when Giorgi Gakharia was Georgia’s interior minister. About five months earlier, a road had been built through the Chorchana forest leading to the future checkpoint.

Around the same time, the de facto authorities in the Tskhinvali region began placing borderisation markers in the area, including green banners and flags. In February 2019, the Tskhinvali side also began marking trees in the Chorchana forest.

Georgian Dream accuses Giorgi Gakharia of establishing the checkpoint without authorisation, which the government says led to an escalation of tensions in the area.

Gakharia told a parliamentary investigative commission that representatives of the occupation regime had been patrolling the Chorchana forest, detaining Georgian citizens and planning to expand the occupation line based on so-called 1992 maps. He said this posed a risk of losing around 1,800 hectares of the Chorchana forest.

After Georgian Dream declared the establishment of the Georgian police checkpoint near the village of Tsneli­si illegal, representatives of Tskhinvali and Russia called on Tbilisi to acknowledge the decision as a “mistake” and remove the checkpoint.

Checkpoint in Chorchana

World.title: Former Georgian prosecutor general says he served in Russia’s Arbat Battalion for nine months
World.content:
Former Georgian prosecutor general Otar Romanov-Partskhaladze says that before forming his own unit to take part in the war against Ukraine, he served for nine months in Russia’s Arbat volunteer corps. Russia’s state-run TASS news agency reported his statement.

In Georgia, Otar Partskhaladze has been charged in absentia with organising a murder and placed on an international wanted list.

On 7 September, it became known, that former Georgian prosecutor general Otar Partskhaladze, who now lives in Russia and is known as Otar Romanov-Partskhaladze, would lead the international “St George” unit, formed to take part in the war against Ukraine.

Partskhaladze said that after Russia launched its full-scale war against Ukraine, he “could not stand aside” and decided to help Russian troops and civilians in Donbas and regions bordering Ukraine.

“After Supreme Commander-in-Chief Vladimir Putin invited me to the Victory Day parade on 9 May 2025, I made a firm decision and joined the Arbat volunteer corps, where I served for nine months. After completing my service with Arbat, my like-minded supporters and I decided to create the international volunteer ‘St George’ unit,” Partskhaladze said.

In an interview with TASS, Romanov-Partskhaladze also explained that the unit’s name refers to the 1783 Treaty of Georgievsk, which he says played an important role in the history of the Georgian people. The treaty placed the eastern Georgian kingdom of Kartli-Kakheti under the protection of the Russian Empire.

According to him, the “St George” unit is recruiting volunteers who value the “shared history of Russia and Georgia” and their “centuries-old brotherhood”.

“Their main motivation is to defend the Christian faith, the traditional family, their culture and identity against the madness and pressure that the West is imposing today. For them, Russia is a bastion of normal, healthy human values, and they have made a firm decision to defend this bastion with weapons in their hands,” Romanov-Partskhaladze said.

Otar Romanov-Partskhaladze also told TASS that he was proud of the sanctions imposed on him by the United States, the European Union and the United Kingdom:

“I have always followed one main principle: justice, order and discipline. I faced unprecedented pressure because I stood up for the truth, took a firm patriotic position and refused to play by the West’s rules. The United States, the European Union and the United Kingdom have placed me on their sanctions lists twice. But I see these sanctions as a medal for standing up for the truth.”

What is known about Arbat

The Arbat volunteer corps was established in 2022 on the initiative of Armen Sargsyan, the head of the so-called Donetsk People’s Republic’s boxing federation and a businessman linked to criminal circles. He is also known as “Gorlovsky”. Arbat initially fought as part of the well-known Abkhazian Pyatnashka brigade. In 2023, the unit came under Russia’s Defence Ministry.

Around 500 people serve in the battalion. Its ranks include assault troops, drone operators and electronic warfare specialists. The battalion’s representatives say former Wagner PMC mercenaries also serve in its ranks. According to Ukraine’s Security Service, the unit was largely recruited from prisoners in Russian jails.

Arbat has taken an active part in fighting in Donetsk region. In August 2024, after Ukrainian forces launched an offensive in Russia’s Kursk region, the battalion withdrew from the Ukrainian front and moved to the Kursk front.

In September 2024, Armenian authorities detained several people and said that Russia-backed members of Arbat had been planning an armed coup in Armenia.

On 3 February 2025, Arbat founder Armen Sargsyan was killed in an explosion near an upmarket residential complex in Moscow.

In February 2026, Arbat commander Hayk Gasparyan was killed in fighting. He had previously served a seven-year sentence in Russia for armed robbery and joined the battalion directly from prison.

Partskhaladze has so far published no photographs or video footage from the combat zone.

Who is Otar Partskhaladze?

Otar Partskhaladze became Georgia’s prosecutor general in November 2013, after the current ruling Georgian Dream party came to power. He held the position for just 47 days and resigned on 30 December.

His resignation followed opposition claims that Partskhaladze had been convicted in Germany in the early 2000s for stealing trainers.

After leaving the prosecutor general’s office, Partskhaladze went into business. He later obtained Russian citizenship and changed his surname to Partskhaladze-Romanov.

In September 2023, the United States imposed sanctions on Partskhaladze. According to the US State Department, Russia’s Federal Security Service (FSB) worked with Partskhaladze to influence Georgian society and politics in favour of Russia. The State Department says Partskhaladze worked with FSB officer Alexander Onishchenko.

In October 2023, then-Georgian President Salome Zourabichvili stripped Partskhaladze of his Georgian citizenship.

In 2025, the United Kingdom also imposed sanctions on Partskhaladze for supporting Russia’s war against Ukraine.

Partskhaladze is currently facing criminal charges in Georgia. In December 2025, the Georgian Interior Ministry named him as the organiser of the murder of businessman Levan Dzhangveladze. According to the ministry, Partskhaladze led an organised criminal group and ordered the murder of Dzhangveladze.

Partskhaladze has been charged in absentia and placed on an international wanted list.

Former Georgian prosecutor general on serving in Arbat

World.title: Georgian parliament speaker says Brussels policy towards country ‘at dead end’
World.content:
Georgian parliament speaker on EU policy

“Yesterday’s statement by the European Union’s spokesperson once again confirms that Brussels’ policy towards Georgia has reached a dead end,” Georgian parliament speaker Shalva Papuashvili said on social media.

Papuashvili later also commented on the situation of prisoners of conscience, describing them as “prisoners of Brussels’ lack of conscience” and accusing Brussels of having encouraged them to take to the barricades.

On 8 September, addressing a session of the UN Human Rights Council, the EU’s deputy permanent representative to the UN, Michele Cervone d’Urso, said the EU was deeply concerned about the “politically motivated use” of the judiciary and the adoption of repressive measures against civil society organisations in Georgia. A report by the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights says Georgia must protect fundamental freedoms and repeal or revise all laws that undermine human rights.

According to Papuashvili, the EU representative’s statement at the UN is concerning because it repeats what he described as “worn-out lies” about “arbitrary detentions” and “repression”.

“It is thought-provoking that statements by European Union officials once again completely contradict not only the facts, but also the values and principles recognised by the EU itself,” Papuashvili wrote.

He alleged that violent protests against the Georgian authorities had been partly funded by the European Union and that an attempt to overthrow the government had been made on 4 October 2025 after the EU gave it the “green light”.

“However, the Georgian people and the Georgian government properly defended the country, its freedom, sovereignty and interests. Today, it is clear to everyone that the foreign-funded revolutionary process of 2024 has failed,” the speaker wrote.

Papuashvili also said narratives about “election fraud” and the “crackdown on peaceful protests” had been “disproved by time and reality”.

“The violent crimes that were committed have been investigated, sentences have been handed down, everything has been documented and recorded and, moreover, acknowledged by the perpetrators themselves.

Once again, facts have prevailed over perceptions. A lie does not become the truth simply because Brussels persistently repeats it, nor does a criminal become a victim simply because some European Union official wants it that way.”

The speaker compared Brussels to “a soldier who does not know that the war is over and continues to plan military operations”.

Papuashvili said that if EU officials wanted to normalise relations with Georgia, they should end what he called their “aggressive rhetoric” towards the country, stop “providing information support for the failed revolutionary scenario” and show respect for Georgia’s sovereignty and the Georgian people’s “democratic choice“.

World.title: Uzbekistan, Japan's Itochu explore new opportunities in mining sector
World.content:
Photo: the Ministry of Mining and Geology of Uzbekistan

BAKU, Azerbaijan, September 10. Uzbekistan and Japan’s Itochu Corporation discussed expanding cooperation in geological exploration and the development of mineral deposits as Tashkent seeks to attract international expertise and investment to its mining sector.

This was reflected in the statement by the Ministry of Mining and Geology of Uzbekistan.

Uzbekistan’s Minister of Mining and Geology B. Islamov met with a delegation from Itochu Corporation led by Executive and Chief Operating Officer Hisakazu Yamaguchi, the ministry said.

Representatives of the Ministry of Mining and Geology and Navoiuran State Enterprise also took part in the meeting.

The sides discussed opportunities to expand cooperation on geological exploration in prospective areas and the development of mineral deposits in Uzbekistan.

Particular attention was given to bringing Uzbekistan’s geological data into line with international standards, an area that could facilitate greater participation by international companies in exploration and mining projects.

The parties also reviewed other potential areas for cooperation between Uzbekistan’s mining sector and Itochu.

“Expanding geological exploration and aligning geological data with international standards are important steps toward strengthening international cooperation and creating new opportunities for the development of Uzbekistan’s mineral resource base,” the Uzbek Ministry of Mining and Geology said.

The meeting highlights Uzbekistan’s efforts to strengthen cooperation with international companies in geological exploration and mining while improving the quality and international comparability of geological information.

Itochu is a major Japanese trading and investment company with business interests across multiple sectors, including natural resources and energy. Its engagement with Uzbekistan could create opportunities for further cooperation in mineral exploration and resource development.

The sides agreed to continue discussions on the identified areas and explore opportunities for further practical cooperation in geological exploration, deposit development and related fields.

World.title: Azerbaijan and China's CC7 review options for expanding cooperation (PHOTO)
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, September 10. An exchange of views was held with the Chinese National Chemical Engineering & Construction Corporation Seven (CC7) on the current status of existing projects, the implementation of the next stages, and the possibilities for expanding relevant cooperation with Azerbaijan.

This was reported by the Azerbaijani Ministry of Economy following the meeting between Minister Mikayil Jabbarov and Chairman of the Board of Directors of CC7 Long Haiyang.

According to the ministry, the meeting discussed the prospects for the development of cooperation in the oil and petrochemical industry in Azerbaijan and third countries.

The parties emphasized the importance of expanding cooperation with partner companies and financial institutions.

World.title: Turkmenistan, CIS discuss expanding practical cooperation
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, September 10. Turkmenistan and the CIS discussed expanding practical cooperation in areas of mutual interest.

This was reflected in a press release published by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Turkmenistan on September 10.

According to the report, this was discussed during a meeting between Turkmen Foreign Minister Rashid Meredov and CIS Secretary General Sergey Lebedev, who arrived in Turkmenistan to attend the 111th meeting of the CIS Economic Council.

The sides exchanged views on preparations for meetings of the CIS Council of Foreign Ministers and Council of Heads of State, scheduled for October 7 and 9, respectively, in Avaza.

Particular attention was paid to organizational arrangements and the agendas of the upcoming high-level meetings.

The officials also discussed the practical implementation of Turkmenistan's priorities during its CIS chairmanship in 2026.

The ministry outlined that the sides discussed “further improvement of cooperation mechanisms within the Commonwealth, with particular attention to expanding practical cooperation in the areas of mutual interest.”

To note, Turkmenistan assumed the chairmanship of the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS) on January 1, 2026, succeeding Tajikistan, and has outlined a Concept for its year-long tenure focusing on five priority areas: ensuring peace and security (with emphasis on neutrality and trust-building), economic cooperation and transport connectivity (including North-South and East-West corridors), digital transformation, the environmental agenda, and humanitarian cooperation.

World.title: Uzbekistan, Lithuania develop new pathways for organized employment
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, September 10. Uzbekistan and Lithuania are exploring ways to expand organized employment opportunities for Uzbek citizens in Lithuania, including professional training for heavy-truck drivers.

This was reflected in the statement by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Uzbekistan, following a meeting between Uzbek Deputy Foreign Minister Olimjon Abdullaev and Albertas Sitavicius, director of Lithuanian international transportation company TVG Group.

The sides discussed opportunities to increase the organized recruitment and employment of Uzbek citizens in Lithuania, with particular attention given to the transportation sector. The talks included the preparation and professional training of Uzbek drivers who would operate heavy trucks in Lithuania.

Moreover, the officials discussed measures to prevent illegal migration and the importance of developing practical mechanisms that can support legal employment while addressing the workforce needs of foreign companies. “Expanding organized employment and professional training opportunities can contribute to safer and more transparent labor migration while creating structured channels for Uzbek workers to access employment abroad,” the Uzbek Foreign Ministry said.

The involvement of a Lithuanian international transportation company in the discussions could provide a practical framework for connecting Uzbek workers with employers and developing skills aligned with the requirements of the international road transportation sector.

The talks also reflect Uzbekistan’s efforts to diversify its labor migration partnerships beyond traditional destinations by developing cooperation with companies and institutions in additional countries. The sides expressed mutual interest in further developing cooperation and continuing practical engagement on the agreed areas, including organized employment, professional driver training and measures to prevent illegal migration, according to the ministry.

World.title: TAP’s role could grow with US LNG deliveries via Greece – ambassador
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, September 10. The Trans Adriatic Pipeline (TAP) could expand its role through delivery of American LNG through Greece to Southeast Europe in the future, the U.S. Ambassador to the Hellenic Republic Kimberly Guilfoyle wrote on her X account.

“I was pleased to meet with Trans Adriatic Pipeline Managing Director Luca Schieppati and Greece Country Representative Ioannis Maris to discuss the future of TAP. TAP continues to play a key role in diversifying energy supplies for Greece - and the region - and could expand its role through the delivery of American LNG through Greece to Southeast Europe in the future,” she wrote.

The ambassador’s remarks come at the time when the Nea Mesimvria interconnection point in Greece is about to officially achieve operational bidirectionality.This will enable the point to function as both an entry and exit point, allowing natural gas to flow in both directions between the TAP system and Greece’s National Natural Gas System (NNGS) operated by DESFA.

The development will further enhance the flexibility of the existing gas network, enabling TAP to transport gas volumes from additional sources (including LNG entering Greece’s NNGS) into the European market. According to the current arrangements, which are highly regulated, there are no technical, commercial or legal obstacles preventing such flows.

In addition, Gastrade earlier this year announced that it is assessing interest for a second floating storage and regasification unit (FSRU) in Thrace, targeted for operation by 2028. The project is expected to increase Greece’s LNG import and export capacity and strengthen supplies to the markets of the Vertical Gas Corridor. The design of the second FSRU could envisage an interconnection with TAP and/or Greece’s NNGS.

TAP is the European section of the Southern Gas Corridor, transporting natural gas from Azerbaijan’s Shah Deniz field to European markets. The 877-kilometer pipeline runs from the Greece-Türkiye border through Greece and Albania, crosses the Adriatic Sea and reaches Italy’s southern coast. TAP currently has an initial transportation capacity of 10 bcm per year, with the potential to expand it to 20 bcm per year.

World.title: Israeli PM's wife hit with $1.2m defamation suit over Oct 7 conspiracy theory
World.content:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's wife has been hit with a defamation lawsuit worth almost than $1.2 million, accused of pushing a conspiracy theory that a leading opposition politician had advance notice of Hamas' deadly October 7, 2023 attacks on Israel.

Former Israel Defense Forces (IDF) deputy chief of staff Yair Golan, who is the leader of the centre-left Democrats party, has been lauded for his actions in the hours after Hamas fighters poured over the Gaza fence line and opened fire.

After hearing about the attacks, Mr Golan raced towards southern Israel and volunteered to return to duty.

He has been widely credited as saving a number of people who had been at the Nova Music Festival, the scene of the deadliest massacre on the day.

In an interview last week with Israel's Channel 14, often regarded as one of the most right-wing media organisations in the country, Sara Netanyahu questioned how Mr Golan had managed to arrive at the scene so quickly.

She insinuated Mr Golan had some sort of inside knowledge about the terrorist attacks.

"When you're a military officer of such a high rank, claiming you were a combatant on … October 7th, you were already there from early in the morning, dressed and ready," Mrs Netanyahu said.

"And at a very, very early hour, that others didn't even know about [the attacks].

"Even the prime minister — shouldn't he know a war was breaking out? Why inform him? Never mind, that's another matter."

Mr Golan reacted angrily to the comments, and threatened Mrs Netanyahu with a 2.55 million Israeli new shekel ($1.17 million) defamation and damages claim after he said she refused to retract the remarks.

"Paranoia, it turns out, is a family business," Mr Golan said in a video statement released on his social media profiles.

"Netanyahu never stops lying and covering up. The tighter the political noose tightens around his neck, the more dangerous he becomes.

"When he feels that power is slipping from his grasp, there is no lie he won't tell, no red line he won't cross. This is a despicable and vile attempt. We're putting an end to this."

Supporters of the prime minister have frequently suggested that he was kept in the dark about the attacks by senior members of the Israeli defence and security establishment, often referred to in the Israeli media as the 'betrayal theory'.

Sara Netanyahu has been hit with a defamation lawsuit worth almost than $1.2 million. (Reuters: Gil Cohen-Magen)

Mr Netanyahu himself has repeatedly claimed the situation would have been totally different had he been woken up earlier on that day.

"And the question is why? They hide things all the time," he said in a recent interview.

"They knew exactly what I would do — they knew I would deploy the air force there, and wake the entire IDF up, I would not allow anyone to get close to the [Gaza] fences, I would immediately kill them [the Hamas fighters]."

It is part of a familiar narrative from the Netanyahu Government and its leader — that a 'deep state' is present in Israel, devoting much of its efforts to undermining the prime minister and his allies.

Mr Netanyahu has rejected calls for an independent inquiry into the failures which led to the Hamas attacks.

An independent probe is something which many of his political opponents are promising in the upcoming election, scheduled for October 27 — including his former IDF chief Gadi Eisenkot, now the leader of the Yashar party.

Netanyahu denies being warned of Hamas attack Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu denies a newspaper report that he was warned more than a week before October 7, 2023, that Hamas was planning an imminent attack.

Earlier this week, the Israeli newspaper Haaretz revealed reporting that Mr Netanyahu had been warned of a looming Hamas attack one and a half weeks prior to the October 7 2023 attacks, by the President of the United Arab Emirates.

But Haaretz reported that Mr Netanyahu did not pass on the intelligence from Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed, known in the region as MBZ.

The Prime Minister vehemently denied the report, saying there was no phone call between him and MBZ in September or early October 2023.

He instructed his lawyers to prepare a libel suit against Haaretz, but the paper insisted it stood by its reporting bases on a months-long investigation.

World.title: Why Japan wants the new world map changed
World.content:
Japan wants changes made to a new world map adopted by the United Nations because the disputed Kuril islands appear to belong to Russia.

The UN General Assembly voted last Friday to adopt the new map, which makes the African continent larger while reducing the size of North America and Europe.

New world map and perceptions of power For centuries, our understanding of nations has been laid out by a single map projection. The UN just voted to change that.

Japan was among the 164 UN members that supported the change, with the United States being the only country to vote against it.

But the Asian nation has now taken issue with the map because it shows the Kuril islands in the same colour as Russia.

The disputed islands — known as the Northern Territories in Japan and as the Southern Kuriles in Russia — were seized in 1945 by the former Soviet Union, which then expelled the Japanese population.

While Russia controls the four islands land, both countries claim sovereignty over them.

Japan says the disputed Kuril islands are marked in the same colour as Russia. (Equal Earth/Tom Patterson)

Japanese government spokesman Minoru Kihara said the new map — known as the Equal Earth cartographic projection — "contained a depiction contradicting the Japanese government's position".

"We lodged a protest with the map site's operator through our diplomatic channel to demand the correction of this depiction," Mr Kihara told reporters.

Loading

He declined to say when the issue was brought to the government's attention but said Japan needed "to prevent misconceptions of our territories and geographical names from spreading".

Relations between Japan and Russia have also soured recently when President Vladimir Putin made a surprise visit to the disputed islands for the first time.

The disputed islands are located in an archipelago between Russia and Japan. (ABC NEWS)

Japan then summoned Moscow's ambassador, with Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi saying Mr Putin's visit "offends the sentiments of the Japanese people".

She called the visit "absolutely unacceptable" with the islands being "an inherent part of Japan's territory, both historically and under international law".

Moscow hit back, saying it "categorically" rejected such statements, "which we consider politically inappropriate, insulting and, of course, legally unfounded".

The UN said the new map aimed to present "a more accurate representation" of continental landmasses than was portrayed by more traditional Mercator projections.

AFP

World.title: At least 25 people killed in cargo ship blaze in Chinese port
World.content:
At least 25 people have been killed and five remain missing after a cargo ship caught fire while docked in a Chinese port in the east of the country.

"A foreign cargo ship of Beihai Shipbuilding Co., Ltd. in Qingdao, Shandong Province, caught fire during its port call for maintenance, causing heavy casualties," state news agency Xinhua news agency said.

A photo released by Xinhua news identified the ship as the Ocean Melody, which sails under a Liberian flag, according to the public vessel-tracking website VesselFinder.

At least five dead, 87 missing as Philippine ferry catches fire Dozens of people have been rescued but scores remain missing following a fire aboard a Philippine ferry that has claimed a number of lives.

A total of 42 people had been on the vessel, and 12 of them were safely evacuated, Xinhua reported.

The ship was docked for repairs at Qingdao Beihai Shipbuilding at the port of Qingdao, a major shipping hub on the north-eastern Chinese coast.

Beihai Shipbuilding is part of the state-controlled China State Shipbuilding Corporation, the world's largest shipbuilder.

A total of 42 people had been on the vessel, and 12 of them were safely evacuated, according to Chinese state media. (Xinhua: Li Aoqiu via AP)

Its main businesses include shipbuilding and ship repairing, according to Beihai Shipbuilding's website.

Chinese President Xi Jinping called for intensified search and rescue efforts, a swift investigation and accountability measures after the deadly fire broke out aboard the foreign cargo ship.

"All regions and relevant departments must draw profound lessons from this incident, thoroughly investigate and rectify all types of fire hazards," he said.

State media reported the fire broke out around 11am (1pm AEST) Thursday and was extinguished by 2:30pm local time (4:30pm AEST).

Premier Li Qiang also urged the search and rescue of "trapped" people, and for those injured to receive medical treatment, "and strictly prevent secondary disasters".

Wires

World.title: Fresh air found for first time in inundated Nepal tunnels
World.content:
Nepali authorities have found fresh air for the first time in the tunnels filled with mud and debris in last month's floods, an Australian tunnelling expert says.

At least 11 hydropower projects were engulfed when a glacier collapsed into a river on the Nepal-China border on August 26, burying the entrances to the tunnels of the projects under debris and mud and trapping those inside.

Arnold Dix has been redeployed to Chilime in Nepal. (Supplied: ABC News)

Melbourne geologist Arnold Dix was invited to Nepal to work with rescue teams at the Chilime hydropower project in the hard-hit Rasuwa district.

"We think we've found a zone where people may have survived and that is just amazing," he said.

"This is the first time we've had fresh air, as opposed to water and mud.

"We can hear that it's hollow, we're calling out. It's not over.

" We're in miracle country. "

900 people suspected trapped in tunnels

A Chinese national was rescued by soldiers during an ongoing operation at the Trishuli-3A hydropower project. (AP: Nepal Army)

A least 1,399 people have been confirmed dead and more than 5,400 are missing in Nepal and Tibet. At least 900 of those missing are suspected to be trapped in hydropower tunnels like those Professor Dix is working on.

On Tuesday, another Australian who had been unaccounted-for was found safe. The ABC understands that the person was not in the disaster zone.

The person is the eighth Australian to be found since the floods, with 35 others still unaccounted-for.

Professor Dix said people trapped in the hydropower project tunnels have had to survive in pitch black for over two weeks, with only access to water.

"What you do is listen to your heart, you do your engineering analysis, and you go after those souls that we think could still be alive," he said.

The geologist, who also assisted rescue teams at the Trishuli 3A hydropower project, previously told the ABC people could survive in the tunnels for up to 17 days.

He said last week that some of the underground power stations likely withstood the immense pressure of the flash flooding. However, it remains unclear whether emergency systems activated in time or whether water and debris inundated them.

Rescue workers take part in a rescue operation near the tunnel of the Trishuli 3A Hydropower Project. (Nepal Prime Minister's Office/Handout via Reuters)

In recent days, search teams have rescued four people, including a Chinese national who was pulled from a tunnel on Saturday.

The others were two hydropower workers rescued from another tunnel on Friday and a Nepali woman pulled out from her buried house on Saturday.

Nepal's Prime Minister Balendra Shah vowed there would be no let-up in the rescue operations.

"We know our responsibility and its sensitivity. We are translating the humanitarian spirit of the Nepali people into practice through the search and rescue operation," he said in a social media post late on Monday.

If you want to help support the thousands affected by the crisis, the ABC is supporting the Emergency Action Alliance member charities and their local partners. You can find more information here.

ABC/Wires

World.title: Book about Kumanjayi Walker's killing wins $80,000 at literary awards
World.content:
A book about the fatal shooting of Kumanjayi Walker and the murder trial of Northern Territory police officer Zachary Rolfe is one of six winners at this year's Prime Minister's Literary Awards (PMLA).

Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander readers are advised this article contains the name of an Indigenous person who has died.

Journalist Kate Wild has taken out the $80,000 prize for non-fiction for her book The Red House, which explores the incident in November 2019, when Mr Walker was shot and killed by police in Yuendumu, a remote community in the Northern Territory, 300 kilometres north-west of Alice Springs.

The 19-year-old Warlpiri man was wanted by police for threatening two local police officers with an axe three days earlier.

When police came to arrest him at his grandmother's house, he stabbed then-constable Rolfe in the shoulder with a pair of medical scissors.

Mr Rolfe then fired his gun three times at Mr Walker, who died in custody an hour later.

The shooting sparked protests calling for "Justice for Walker", with more than 1,000 people marching in Alice Springs, six months before the murder of George Floyd in America kicked off a wave of Black Lives Matter protests.

"Justice for Walker" was spray-painted onto a road sign on the way to Yuendumu. (ABC News: Xavier Martin )

In March 2022, Mr Rolfe was found not guilty of Mr Walker's murder after a six-week trial in Darwin.

Three years later, in July 2025, the NT coroner released the findings of a coronial inquest into the fatal shooting. She found Mr Rolfe was "racist" and could not exclude the possibility his attitudes "were a contributing cause of Kumanjayi's death". He has been dismissed from the NT Police Force.

The PMLA judges described The Red House as "deeply compassionate … rigorous and urgently necessary to an ongoing national conversation".

"Her searing and unflinching investigation examines national difference, the depth of the colonial wound, and the awful repetition of state violence and dehumanisation that makes the confrontation at the heart of this book possible, even inevitable," the judges wrote.

Wild tells ABC Arts she feels "pretty stunned and proud" to have won the award.

" It's really affirming," she says. "It's really nice to know people care about this. "

Other PMLA winners include Rohan Howitt's The Southern Frontier, about Australia's relationship to Antarctica, which won the Australian history prize; and the fiction winner, A Piece of Red Cloth, which saw Leonie Norrington work with Yolŋu Elders, Merrkiyawuy Ganambarr-Stubbs, Djawa Burarrwanga and Djawundil Maymuru, on a book about the Indonesian fisher-traders visiting Arnhem Land.

• Jump to the full list of PMLA winners

Murky waters

Throughout The Red House, Wild reckons with the difficulty of the task she has set for herself: to write about Mr Walker's death in a nuanced way.

The Red House also won The Age newspaper's prize for non-fiction book of the year. (Supplied: Allen & Unwin)

In the book, she speaks to a former defence force chaplain who is also staying in Yuendumu, who asks why she wants to write about the shooting.

Wild writes: "Australia's collective view of history was changing and the country was changing with it, I said. How people reacted to Kumanjayi's death and Mr Rolfe's trial was one measure of how much."

The chaplain counsels: "it's not an easy path you're setting out on."

Wild replies: "One way or another I expect to be cancelled."

So far, Wild hasn't been cancelled.

"It's dangerous to write about very conflicted subjects and spaces, particularly in the world we live in at the moment," she says.

She had noticed within hours of Mr Walker's death people declaring where they stood on the issue — positions that were often diametrically opposed.

"I was so frustrated by those really predictable left-right positions they were taking without thinking," she says.

"I'm impatient with that approach to anything, but particularly to subjects which are so contested.

" What living in the Northern Territory teaches you more than anything is that nothing is left-right; nothing is Black-white. "

Wild had long conversations with both Indigenous and non-Indigenous friends about whether she — a white, middle-aged, middle-class woman — should write the book.

She soon resolved to do it, regardless of the possible backlash.

"After a lot of conversations and soul-searching, I came to the position it was part of the problem to frame this as an Aboriginal story," she says.

"It was a white police officer who shot [Mr Walker], and so the story is as much a white Australia story as it is a Black Australia story."

Wild brought her knowledge and connections, sown over six years reporting mostly on Indigenous affairs in Darwin from 2010 to 2016, to the book, but also a deep love of NT and its people.

"I didn't want [a story about the case] to be reduced to a bunch of racist white rednecks and a bunch of victim Aboriginal people," she says. "That's not the truth."

An expansive approach to time

Wild was interested in understanding how the altercation between Mr Walker and Mr Rolfe in Yuendumu reflected something broader about "where we're at as a nation in terms of race and reconciliation".

"But by the time I got to the end of it, I had an even bigger picture of history," she says.

ABC Radio National’s Top 100 Australian Books Countdown We take over Radio National on Saturday, 17 and Sunday, 18 October to count down the Top 100 Australian books as voted by you.

Former NT politician Scott McConnell alerted Wild to the parallels between the racial tensions in NT in 2019 and the 80s.

He pointed to three acts of violence: the shooting of a station owner by a group of Indigenous young people; the killing of an Indigenous man by police near Ti Tree; and the deaths of two Indigenous people after they drank from a bottle of wine deliberately laced with strychnine.

Those parallels led Wild to thinking about the "Everywhen", an Indigenous conception of time where the past, present and future are all happening simultaneously.

She found it a useful way to conceptualise how historical moments of violence between Indigenous peoples and the police seemed to repeat.

Loading YouTube content

Wild used the Everywhen as a structural device in The Red House, which allowed her to eschew a chronology, instead move fluidly between times and places.

"I learned not to look at [time] as a linear thing — this happens and that leads to this," she explains.

"What is happening now carries the ghosts of what has happened in the past."

The Everywhen also offered a unique way of looking to the future, taking away the seeming inevitability of both police violence and Indigenous disadvantage, instead engendering the possibility of change.

"Finding the Everywhen and understanding how I could use that to frame the whole story, to me, is such a hopeful way of looking at things," Wild says.

"Every single one of us has a responsibility to live in ways that make repair possible," Wild says. (Supplied: Nicholas Coghlan)

"Maybe if the non-Indigenous world can learn to look at life in this more open way, a more creative way, maybe that's where some of the answers lie.

" If we can open our view a bit more, we're going to find better answers and better relationships, rather than pointing fingers. "
